Worldly pleasures and possessions do not bring lasting satisfaction. Only chanting the Name of the Lord can quench our thirst. Meditating on the Name leads to supreme dignity.

blocks.scenario: You are tempted to buy something you don't really need. Do you A) Reflect on whether it will truly satisfy you, or B) Give in to the impulse and buy it?

choices.text: Reflect on whether it will truly satisfy you
Give in to the impulse and buy it

blocks.why: Reflecting on true satisfaction aligns with the passage's message that worldly desires are fleeting, connecting to the 'desire' and 'maya' tags.

blocks.question: According to the passage, what brings lasting satisfaction?
blocks.answer: Chanting the Name of the Lord

blocks.text: True satisfaction comes from within, not from external possessions.
This passage describes the Name of the Lord as a source of support and healing. It highlights the peace and blessings that come to those who serve the Lord.
The Name of the Lord is a daily support and a source of healing. Serving the Lord brings peace, liberation, and honor. The Lord's servants are blessed with understanding and love.

blocks.scenario: You have an opportunity to volunteer your time to help others. Do you A) Take the opportunity to serve, or B) Decline due to other commitments?

choices.text: Take the opportunity to serve
Decline due to other commitments

blocks.why: Serving others aligns with the passage's emphasis on seva (service) and the blessings it brings, connecting to the 'seva' tag.

blocks.question: What are some benefits of serving the Lord, according to the passage?

blocks.text: Serving others can bring you closer to the Divine.
This passage emphasizes the power and importance of the Name of the Lord. It also speaks of the value of the Society of the Saints and serving them.
The Name of the Lord is the highest form of speech and removes pain and sorrow. The Society of the Saints is obtained through good fortune. Serving the Saints allows one to meditate on the Name.

blocks.scenario: You have the chance to spend time with wise and compassionate people. Do you A) Engage with them and learn from their experiences, or B) Isolate yourself and avoid social interaction?

choices.text: Engage with them and learn from their experiences
Isolate yourself and avoid social interaction

blocks.why: Spending time with wise people aligns with the passage's emphasis on the Society of the Saints and the spiritual wisdom gained from them, connecting to the 'sangat' and 'spiritual_wisdom' tags.

blocks.question: What is the Society of the Saints obtained through, according to the passage?

blocks.text: Seek the company of those who inspire you to grow spiritually.
This passage contrasts worldly pursuits with the power of the Name of the Lord. It emphasizes that only the Name can dispel fear and bring true satisfaction.
Worldly achievements and religious rituals cannot compare to the Name of the Lord. Even with great cleverness, the fear of death remains. Only chanting the Name can dispel sorrow and bring salvation.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling anxious about the future and the unknown. Do you A) Focus on chanting the Name of the Lord, or B) Dwell on your fears and uncertainties?

choices.text: Focus on chanting the Name of the Lord
Dwell on your fears and uncertainties

blocks.why: Chanting the Name of the Lord is said to dispel sorrow and fear, aligning with the 'naam' and 'fear' tags.

blocks.question: What can dispel sorrow and bring salvation, according to the passage?
blocks.answer: Chanting the Name of the Lord

blocks.text: Find peace and strength in the Name of the Lord.
This lesson focuses on the importance of humility and remembering God's Name. It highlights how these practices can bring honor and erase sorrows. Let's explore these concepts together.

The verses emphasize that true honor comes from renouncing ego and seeing oneself as lowly. Eradicating cruelty and treating pleasure and pain equally are also important. God's Name is described as wealth, home, and honor for those in need, and the ultimate giver of all gifts.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling overwhelmed by a difficult situation at work. You can either:

choices.text: Reflect on the blessings in your life and remember God's name, seeking humility and strength.
Focus on your anger and frustration, blaming others for your problems.

blocks.why: Choosing A aligns with the lesson's emphasis on gratitude, humility, and remembering God's name to overcome sorrows.

blocks.question: According to these verses, what is the supreme person like?
blocks.answer: One who sees himself as lowly and whose mind is the dust of all.

blocks.text: Remembering God's name and practicing humility can bring peace and honor in challenging times.
This lesson explores the best path in life. It emphasizes the importance of remembering the Creator and appreciating the gifts we receive. Let's delve into these teachings.

The verses state that the best religion is to chant God's Name and maintain pure conduct. The best effort is to remember God always. We are encouraged to cherish the One who created us and to appreciate the blessings we receive throughout our lives.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling ungrateful for what you have. You can either:

choices.text: Reflect on the blessings in your life, remembering the One who created you and provides for you.
Focus on what you lack, comparing yourself to others and feeling dissatisfied.

blocks.why: Choosing A aligns with the lesson's emphasis on remembering the Creator and appreciating the blessings we receive.

blocks.question: What is the best religion, according to these verses?
blocks.answer: To chant the Name of the Lord and maintain pure conduct.

blocks.text: Remembering the Creator and appreciating our blessings can lead to a more fulfilling life.
This lesson focuses on recognizing God's grace in our lives. It also touches on the dangers of being engrossed in Maya (illusion). Let's explore these concepts.

The verses highlight that our comfort, relationships, and necessities are all due to God's grace.  However, people often forsake God and become attached to worldly things.  The lesson urges us to recognize God as our protector and to seek His saving grace.

blocks.scenario: You receive a promotion at work. You can either:

choices.text: Acknowledge God's grace in your success and use your position to help others.
Become arrogant and boastful, forgetting the source of your blessings.

blocks.why: Choosing A aligns with the lesson's emphasis on gratitude and recognizing God's grace in our lives.

blocks.question: According to these verses, what is the source of our comfort and necessities?

blocks.text: Recognizing God's grace and avoiding attachment to Maya can lead to a more balanced and fulfilling life.
This lesson explores the deceptive nature of Maya and the importance of compassion. It highlights the contrast between outward appearances and inner realities. Let's examine these teachings.

The verses describe how people may appear religious outwardly but are filled with Maya and ego.  They emphasize the limitations of those who are spiritually blind, deaf, or mute.  The lesson concludes with a prayer for God's grace to save us from these pitfalls.

blocks.scenario: You encounter someone who is outwardly religious but acts unkindly. You can either:

choices.text: Remember that appearances can be deceiving and pray for their inner transformation.
Judge them harshly and dismiss their faith as hypocritical.

blocks.why: Choosing A aligns with the lesson's emphasis on compassion and recognizing the potential for inner transformation through God's grace.

blocks.question: According to these verses, what is the 'filth of Maya'?
blocks.answer: It refers to inner desires and attachments that contradict outward religious displays.

blocks.text: Seeking inner transformation and practicing compassion can help us overcome the deceptive nature of Maya.

This lesson explores the concept of Hukam (Divine Order) and the importance of gratitude and detachment. It emphasizes that everything comes from God and is under His command. Let's delve into these teachings.

The verses state that our bodies and souls belong to God.  We should be grateful for the joys we experience through His grace.  The lesson cautions against renouncing God and attaching ourselves to other affairs, emphasizing that true success comes from abiding by His Will.

blocks.scenario: You experience a setback in your life. You can either:

choices.text: Accept it as part of God's Hukam, remaining grateful for what you have and trusting in His plan.
Become bitter and resentful, blaming God for your misfortune.

blocks.why: Choosing A aligns with the lesson's emphasis on accepting God's Hukam, practicing gratitude, and trusting in His plan.

blocks.question: According to these verses, what happens to one who renounces God?
blocks.answer: He shall never succeed and will lose his honor.

blocks.text: Accepting God's Hukam, practicing gratitude, and remaining detached can lead to inner peace and true success.

This lesson focuses on the fleeting nature of Maya and the importance of attaching ourselves to God's Name. It highlights the impermanence of worldly possessions and relationships. Let's explore these concepts.

The verses emphasize that attachment to Maya is transitory.  Body, wealth, and relationships are all false.  The love of God's Name, however, bestows peace.  We are encouraged to meditate on the Lotus Feet of the Lord, which is permanent.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling overly attached to your possessions. You can either:

choices.text: Reflect on the impermanence of worldly things and focus on your connection with God's Name.
Cling tightly to your possessions, fearing loss and feeling anxious.

blocks.why: Choosing A aligns with the lesson's emphasis on detachment from Maya and focusing on the love of God's Name.

blocks.question: According to these verses, what is permanent?
blocks.answer: Only devotional worship and the Sanctuary of the Holy.

blocks.text: Detaching ourselves from Maya and focusing on God's Name can lead to lasting peace and fulfillment.

This lesson explores the concept of falsehood and the importance of living a truthful life. It highlights the futility of actions performed without understanding and devotion. Let's examine these teachings.

The verses describe various actions as false, including listening to slander, stealing, and coveting.  Without the Name of the Lord, life is useless.  The lesson emphasizes the importance of aligning our actions with our words and filling our hearts with love for God.

blocks.scenario: You are tempted to gossip about a friend. You can either:

choices.text: Refrain from speaking negatively and instead focus on positive qualities.
Indulge in the gossip, justifying it as harmless fun.

blocks.why: Choosing A aligns with the lesson's emphasis on avoiding slander and living a truthful life.

blocks.question: According to these verses, what makes a body fruitful?

blocks.text: Living a truthful life and filling our hearts with love for God can lead to a more meaningful existence.
This lesson focuses on the importance of prayer, devotion, and seeking God's grace. It emphasizes that God knows everything and values His creatures. Let's explore these concepts.

The verses state that we should offer our prayers to God, who knows everything.  We should seek His grace to overcome negative emotions like sexual desire, anger, and greed.  By His grace, we enjoy many blessings, and we should meditate on Him always.

blocks.scenario: You are struggling with negative emotions. You can either:

choices.text: Pray for God's grace to overcome these emotions and seek inner peace.
Give in to the emotions, allowing them to control your actions.

blocks.why: Choosing A aligns with the lesson's emphasis on seeking God's grace to overcome negative emotions and find inner peace.

blocks.question: According to these verses, what should we do each and every moment?

blocks.text: Offering prayers, seeking God's grace, and meditating on Him can help us overcome negativity and live a more fulfilling life.
These verses describe how everything we have comes from God's Grace. We should sing His Praises and remember Him always.

The verses highlight that our comforts, honor, health, and even our very existence are gifts. Remembering God and expressing gratitude is a way to acknowledge His Grace. By remembering God, we find peace and honor.

blocks.scenario: You receive a promotion at work. Do you:

choices.text: Acknowledge the opportunity as a blessing and remember to be grateful.
Take full credit for your hard work and focus on the increased salary.

blocks.why: Choosing A aligns with the verses' emphasis on acknowledging God's Grace in all aspects of life, including success.

blocks.question: According to these verses, where does our honor come from?

blocks.text: Remembering God with each breath allows us to recognize the blessings in our lives.
These verses emphasize the importance of meditating on God. By His Grace, we experience many blessings.

The verses state that our ability to do good, our physical beauty, our social standing, and even our senses are gifts from God. We are encouraged to meditate on Him constantly. Awakening the mind through Guru's Grace allows us to recognize these blessings.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling overwhelmed by daily tasks. Do you:

choices.text: Take a few moments to meditate and remember God.
Continue rushing through tasks without a break.

blocks.why: Choosing A reflects the verses' message to meditate on God, even amidst daily life.

blocks.question: According to these verses, what should we meditate on?

blocks.text: Meditating on God helps us recognize the blessings in our lives and find peace.
These verses describe how chanting God's Name and singing His praises come through His Grace. The company of the Holy is invaluable.

The verses explain that enlightenment and a blossoming heart come from God's mercy. Being in the Company of the Holy brings radiance, removes negativity, and reveals wisdom. Ultimately, everything is in God's hands.

blocks.scenario: You have a free afternoon. Do you:

choices.text: Attend a gathering focused on spiritual reflection and community.
Spend the afternoon alone watching TV.

blocks.why: Choosing A aligns with the verses' emphasis on the benefits of the Company of the Holy.

blocks.question: According to these verses, what kind of company is valuable?

blocks.text: Seeking the Company of the Holy can bring enlightenment and remove negativity from our lives.
These verses describe the benefits of being in the Company of the Holy. In such company, the mind becomes stable and at peace.

The verses explain that in the Company of the Holy, one meets the Lord, flourishes, and controls passions. Enemies become friends, and selfishness is renounced. The mind finds stability and peace, and one is freed from Maya.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling angry towards someone. Do you:

choices.text: Reflect on the teachings and try to see them as a friend.
Hold onto your anger and avoid them.

blocks.why: Choosing A aligns with the verses' message that in the Company of the Holy, enemies become friends.

blocks.question: According to these verses, what happens to enemies in the Company of the Holy?

blocks.text: Seeking the Company of the Holy can help us overcome negative emotions and find inner peace.
These verses describe the transformative power of the Company of the Holy. In such company, life becomes fruitful and virtuous.

The verses explain that in the Company of the Holy, families are saved, and wealth is obtained. There is no suffering, and one is reunited with the Lord. Listening to the sweet words of the Holy leads to salvation.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling lost and unsure of your path. Do you:

choices.text: Seek guidance and support from a spiritual community.
Isolate yourself and try to figure things out alone.

blocks.why: Choosing A aligns with the verses' message that in the Company of the Holy, one's life becomes fruitful.

blocks.question: According to these verses, what happens to suffering in the Company of the Holy?

blocks.text: Seeking the Company of the Holy can provide guidance, support, and a path towards a more fulfilling life.
These verses describe the qualities of a God-conscious being. Such a being sees only the One and speaks the Truth.
The verses explain that a God-conscious being is unattached, unstained, and looks upon all alike. They possess steady patience and are like a warming fire. These qualities are bestowed by God.

blocks.scenario: You witness someone being treated unfairly. Do you:

choices.text: Intervene and advocate for them, treating everyone equally.
Stay silent to avoid conflict.

blocks.why: Choosing A aligns with the verses' message that a God-conscious being looks upon all alike.

blocks.question: According to these verses, what does a God-conscious being see?

blocks.text: Striving to embody the qualities of a God-conscious being can lead to a more peaceful and just world.
These verses continue to describe the qualities of a God-conscious being. They are the dust of all and show kindness to everyone.

The verses explain that a God-conscious being is pure, enlightened, and sees friend and foe as the same. They are humble, kind, and impartial. They center their hopes on the One alone and are absorbed in God's meditation.

blocks.scenario: You encounter someone who is struggling. Do you:

choices.text: Offer help and support with compassion.
Ignore their struggles and continue with your day.

blocks.why: Choosing A aligns with the verses' message that a God-conscious being shows kindness to all.

blocks.question: According to these verses, what does a God-conscious being show to all?

blocks.text: Striving to embody humility and compassion can bring us closer to becoming God-conscious beings.
These verses further describe the qualities of a God-conscious being. They love the One Lord and renounce their ego.

The verses explain that a God-conscious being dwells with God, takes the Naam as their support, and is always awake and aware. They renounce their ego and dwell in peaceful ease. They know God and are in love with the One alone.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling proud of an accomplishment. Do you:

choices.text: Acknowledge your efforts but remain humble and grateful.
Brag about your success and seek praise from others.

blocks.why: Choosing A aligns with the verses' message that a God-conscious being renounces their ego.

blocks.question: According to these verses, what does a God-conscious being renounce?

blocks.text: Striving to renounce our ego and cultivate love for the One Lord can bring us closer to becoming God-conscious beings.
This passage describes the qualities of a God-conscious being. They are seen as the creator, eternal, and the Lord of all.

The God-conscious being is the source of all creation and liberation. They are a helper to the helpless and extend their hand to all. Enshrining Naam in the heart and avoiding falsehood are key characteristics.

blocks.scenario: You see someone struggling to carry groceries. Do you:

choices.text: Offer to help them carry their bags.
Continue walking without acknowledging them.

blocks.why: Offering help reflects the God-conscious being's quality of extending a hand to all, aligning with the tags of oneness and truth.

blocks.question: According to this passage, what does a God-conscious being enshrine within their heart?

blocks.text: Reflecting on these qualities can guide us towards a more compassionate and truthful life.
This passage describes the qualities of a true devotee. They are kind, devoted, and focused on the divine.

A true devotee is one who pleases God, dwells apart from Maya, and performs selfless service. They are absorbed in devotion, meditate on the Lord, and inspire others to chant the Naam. They also forsake the company of wicked people.

blocks.scenario: A friend is feeling down and asks you to hang out. Do you:

choices.text: Listen to them and offer support.
Tell them to just get over it.

blocks.why: Offering support aligns with the devotee's kindness and love for others, reflecting the tags of devotion and seva.

blocks.question: What does a true devotee inspire others to chant?

blocks.text: Cultivating kindness and devotion can lead to a more fulfilling spiritual life.
This passage emphasizes the power of the Naam and God's grace. It highlights the importance of accepting God's will.

The Naam is spiritual wisdom for all, regardless of background. It is a remedy for all ills, attainable through grace and pre-ordained karma. Loving God's will and seeing joy and sorrow as equal are characteristics of a liberated being.

blocks.scenario: You receive an unexpected bill in the mail. Do you:

choices.text: Accept it and figure out a way to pay it.
Become angry and complain about it.

blocks.why: Accepting the situation aligns with loving the Will of God, reflecting the tags of grace and hukam.

blocks.question: According to this passage, what is the remedy to cure all ills?

blocks.text: Embracing the Naam and accepting God's will can bring peace and understanding.
This passage speaks to the all-encompassing nature of God. It emphasizes that everything is within God's domain and under God's will.

All places belong to God, and creatures are named according to where God places them. Whatever pleases God comes to pass, and God is merciful. Remembering God brings ecstasy, and God's creation is vast and diverse.

blocks.scenario: You are planning a trip, but your plans fall through. Do you:

choices.text: Accept it and find another way to enjoy your time.
Become upset and dwell on the disappointment.

blocks.why: Accepting the change aligns with the idea that whatever pleases God comes to pass, reflecting the tags of hukam and oneness.

blocks.question: According to this passage, what brings ecstasy?

blocks.text: Recognizing God's presence in all things can bring peace and acceptance.
This passage describes the vastness of creation and the struggles within Maya. It emphasizes that God alone knows the workings of creation.

The world is filled with countless beings, each engaged in different activities and struggles. God attaches beings to what they are engaged with, and only God knows the workings of creation. God emancipates those with whom He is pleased.

blocks.scenario: You see a friend constantly chasing after material possessions. Do you:

choices.text: Gently remind them of the importance of inner peace.
Encourage them to buy more things.

blocks.why: Reminding them of inner peace aligns with detaching from Maya, reflecting the tags of maya and attachment.

blocks.question: According to this passage, who alone knows the workings of His creation?

blocks.text: Understanding the nature of Maya can help us focus on what truly matters.
This passage speaks about the cycle of life and death. It highlights the importance of attaching oneself to the Lord's Name and love.

Beings are born, live, die, and are reincarnated. Some renounce the world and attach themselves to the Lord's Name. Those who are imbued with the Love of the Supreme Lord God are blessed. From God they emanate, and into God they merge once again.

blocks.scenario: You experience a setback in your life. Do you:

choices.text: Remember the Lord's Name and seek inner strength.
Become discouraged and lose hope.

blocks.why: Remembering the Lord's Name aligns with attaching oneself to the Lord, reflecting the tags of naam and love.

blocks.question: According to this passage, what do those who renounce the world attach themselves to?

blocks.text: Finding solace in the Lord's Name can help us navigate the ups and downs of life.
This passage emphasizes the importance of remembering God. It highlights that God alone is the Doer of deeds.

Servants of God have enlightened souls and know the essence of reality. They drink in the essence of the Naam and are absorbed in peace. God alone is the Doer of deeds, and everything is under God's order. He pervades all.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling overwhelmed by a difficult task. Do you:

choices.text: Remember that God is the Doer and seek guidance.
Try to do everything yourself and become stressed.

blocks.why: Remembering that God is the Doer aligns with the passage's message, reflecting the tags of naam and hukam.

blocks.question: According to this passage, who alone is the Doer of deeds?

blocks.text: Trusting in God's will can bring peace and clarity.
This passage emphasizes the power of God's will and grace. It highlights that everything happens according to God's pleasure.

If it pleases God, one attains salvation and even stones can swim. God acts and contemplates, and He is the Master of both worlds. Those whom the Lord blesses with devotion are absorbed into the Naam. Nanak sees no other than Him.

blocks.scenario: You are facing a difficult challenge. Do you:

choices.text: Trust in God's will and seek strength through the Naam.
Give up and feel helpless.

blocks.why: Trusting in God's will aligns with the passage's message, reflecting the tags of hukam and naam.

blocks.question: According to this passage, what are those whom the Lord blesses with devotion absorbed into?

blocks.text: Surrendering to God's will can bring peace and strength in challenging times.
This lesson explores the idea that there is no power in the hands of mortal beings. We are subject to God's Command, and what pleases Him ultimately comes to pass.
The meanings suggest that life's experiences, both high and low, are part of God's plan.  Sometimes we experience joy, other times sorrow. Ultimately, God unites us with Himself.

blocks.scenario: You planned a picnic, but it's raining. Do you:

choices.text: Accept it and find an indoor activity.
Get angry and insist on having the picnic anyway.

blocks.why: Accepting the situation reflects the idea that we are subject to His Command, aligning with the tags 'hukam' and 'oneness'.

blocks.question: According to this lesson, who ultimately decides what happens?

blocks.text: Remember, there is comfort in knowing that everything is part of a larger plan.
This lesson speaks of attaining the Company of the Holy. Subduing egotism leads to meekness, while pride consumes the arrogant.
The meanings suggest that finding peace involves humility and connection with others.  Those who overcome ego find liberation, while pride leads to suffering.

blocks.scenario: A friend takes credit for your idea at work. Do you:

choices.text: Let it go and focus on future collaboration.
Publicly confront them and demand recognition.

blocks.why: Letting it go reflects subduing egotism and seeking peace, aligning with the tags 'sangat', 'haumai', and 'peace'.

blocks.question: What is said to lead to peace?

blocks.text: Strive for humility and connection to find true peace.
This lesson discusses the dangers of ego and the importance of grace. Eliminating ego makes one acceptable, while acting in ego leads to trouble.
The meanings suggest that true goodness comes from humility and grace, not from pride or outward actions done in ego.  Those who eliminate ego find acceptance.

blocks.scenario: You receive a compliment on a project. Do you:

choices.text: Acknowledge the compliment and thank those who helped.
Take all the credit and boast about your skills.

blocks.why: Acknowledging others reflects eliminating ego and recognizing grace, aligning with the tags 'haumai' and 'kirpa'.

blocks.question: What makes one acceptable in the Court of the Lord?

blocks.text: Seek humility and recognize the grace in your life.
This lesson explores the pursuit of Maya and the importance of contentment.  God is the cause of causes, and He is the One.
The meanings suggest that chasing after worldly possessions does not bring satisfaction. True peace is found through love and recognizing God's presence in everything.

blocks.scenario: You see an advertisement for a new gadget. Do you:

choices.text: Appreciate what you already have and feel content.
Feel envious and immediately want to buy it.

blocks.why: Feeling content reflects understanding the futility of chasing Maya and recognizing God's presence, aligning with the tags 'maya', 'contentment', and 'oneness'.

blocks.question: What does chasing after Maya not bring?

blocks.text: Find peace by appreciating what you have and recognizing God in everything.
This lesson emphasizes the truth of God and the importance of seeking the Sanctuary of the Saints. Slandering the Saints leads to negative consequences.
The meanings suggest that connecting with holy people and the Word brings salvation.  Negative actions like slander have harmful repercussions.

blocks.scenario: You hear someone gossiping about a respected community leader. Do you:

choices.text: Politely excuse yourself and avoid participating.
Join in and share your own criticisms.

blocks.why: Avoiding gossip reflects seeking the Sanctuary of the Saints and avoiding slander, aligning with the tags 'truth', 'sangat', and 'bani'.

blocks.question: What is said to bring salvation?
blocks.answer: Seeking the Sanctuary of the Saints

blocks.text: Connect with truth and avoid negativity to find peace.
This lesson warns against slandering the Saints, describing it as a grave sin. Such actions lead to negative consequences and separation.
The meanings suggest that negativity and disrespect towards holy people have severe repercussions.  Even liberation is only possible through the Saint's grace.

blocks.scenario: You disagree with a spiritual teacher's opinion. Do you:

choices.text: Express your disagreement respectfully and seek understanding.
Publicly denounce them and try to discredit their teachings.

blocks.why: Expressing disagreement respectfully avoids slandering the Saints, aligning with the tags 'sin' and 'sangat'.

blocks.question: What is slandering a Saint described as?

blocks.text: Avoid negativity and seek understanding to find peace.
This lesson continues to warn against slandering the Saint, emphasizing its destructive nature. Ultimately, whatever pleases God's Will comes to pass.
The meanings suggest that negativity and lack of faith lead to suffering.  Only God's will prevails, and even the slanderer's fate is ultimately in His hands.

blocks.scenario: You see someone struggling with their faith. Do you:

choices.text: Offer support and understanding without judgment.
Criticize their doubts and tell them they are wrong.

blocks.why: Offering support avoids slandering and reflects faith, aligning with the tags 'sin', 'hukam', and 'faith'.

blocks.question: Whose will ultimately comes to pass?

blocks.text: Offer support and understanding, trusting in God's plan.
This lesson emphasizes God as the creator and the importance of remembering Him. He Himself gives His Name to those He favors.
The meanings suggest that true peace comes from surrendering to God and remembering Him constantly.  Reliance on mortals is futile; only God can truly help us.

blocks.scenario: You feel anxious about the future. Do you:

choices.text: Remember God and trust in His plan.
Try to control every detail and worry constantly.

blocks.why: Remembering God and trusting in His plan aligns with the tags 'kirpa', 'naam', and 'fear'.

blocks.question: What departs when you enshrine your hopes in the One Lord?

blocks.text: Remember God and trust in His plan to find peace and overcome fear.
This lesson focuses on remembering the Formless Lord, seeking the company of the holy, and doing the Lord's work. It emphasizes purifying the mind and finding peace through devotion.

The verses encourage praising the Formless Lord in your mind and making this your true occupation.  It speaks of purifying your tongue, finding peace, seeing the Lord's wondrous play, and walking in the Way of the Lord.  The company of the holy helps wash away sins and leads to a radiant face in the Lord's Court.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling overwhelmed by daily tasks and worries.  You can either A) Dedicate some time to quiet reflection and prayer, focusing on the Formless Lord, or B) Continue to focus solely on your tasks and worries without a break.

choices.text: Dedicate some time to quiet reflection and prayer, focusing on the Formless Lord.
Continue to focus solely on your tasks and worries without a break.

blocks.why: Choosing A aligns with the lesson's emphasis on praising the Formless Lord and finding peace through devotion, reflecting the tags 'naam', 'sangat', and 'seva'.

blocks.question: According to the lesson, what happens in the Company of the Holy?

blocks.text: By remembering the Lord and seeking the company of the holy, one can find peace and purpose in life.
This lesson explores the concept of God's grace, the understanding of oneness, and the power of the Guru's Shabad. It suggests that understanding comes through grace and devotion.

The verses state that those who receive God's grace understand the essence of reality. God is seen as both subtle and manifest, the root of all things.  Chanting the Guru's Shabad brings ecstasy, and those who chant the Naam find rest. Those who know God are glorious and redeem the world.

blocks.scenario: You are struggling to understand a complex situation in your life. You can either A) Reflect on the situation with faith, seeking understanding through the Guru's teachings, or B) Rely solely on your own logic and reasoning to find a solution.

choices.text: Reflect on the situation with faith, seeking understanding through the Guru's teachings.
Rely solely on your own logic and reasoning to find a solution.

blocks.why: Choosing A aligns with the lesson's emphasis on understanding through Guru's grace and the power of the Shabad, reflecting the tags 'grace', 'oneness', and 'shabad'.

blocks.question: According to the lesson, what happens to those who chant the Guru's Shabad?

blocks.text: Understanding and peace can be found through God's grace and devotion to the Guru's teachings.
This lesson centers on doing everything for the love of God, accepting God's will (Hukam), and finding inner peace. It suggests that true peace comes from aligning oneself with God's will.
