We cannot deny that the Divine sees all. Remembering the Divine Name can destroy millions of mistakes.
It is natural for us to err, but it is also the Divine's nature to save us. The Divine is full of kindness and compassion, and seeing the Divine can redeem our lives.

blocks.scenario: You accidentally spill coffee on a coworker's important documents. You feel terrible.

choices.text: Apologize sincerely and offer to help clean up and reprint the documents.
Quickly walk away, hoping no one noticed it was you.

blocks.why: Apologizing and helping reflects compassion and seeking forgiveness, aligning with the lesson's tags.

blocks.question: According to this lesson, what can destroy millions of sins?

blocks.text: Remembering the Divine and seeking forgiveness can help us overcome our mistakes.
The Guru's teachings should reside in our hearts, and the Divine Name in our minds. We should strive to eliminate doubts and accept what happens.
By following the Guru's guidance, we can overcome inner obstacles. Accepting the Divine's will helps us move beyond duality and find liberation in the company of the holy.

blocks.scenario: You receive unexpected feedback at work that is difficult to hear.

choices.text: Listen openly, try to understand the feedback, and consider how to improve.
Become defensive and dismiss the feedback without considering it.

blocks.why: Listening openly and accepting feedback aligns with accepting the Divine's will and detaching from ego, as taught in the lesson.

blocks.question: What should reside in our hearts according to this lesson?
blocks.answer: The Word of the Guru's Shabad.

blocks.text: By embracing the Guru's wisdom and accepting the Divine's will, we can find inner peace and liberation.
We should serve and associate with the Divine's humble servants. The dust of their feet is precious, fulfilling our hopes.
Praises of the Divine's servants are pure, and their feet are like sacred places. By seeking their company and serving them, we can cleanse ourselves of countless sins.

blocks.scenario: You see someone struggling to carry groceries to their car.

choices.text: Offer to help them carry their groceries.
Continue walking, minding your own business.

blocks.why: Offering help is an act of seva (selfless service) and humility, reflecting the lesson's themes.

blocks.question: According to this lesson, what are the feet of the Divine's humble servants equal to?
blocks.answer: Millions of sacred shrines of pilgrimage.

blocks.text: Serving others with humility and devotion can purify us and bring us closer to the Divine.
We may not understand the Divine's actions, but everything we have belongs to the Divine. The Divine knows our hearts and unspoken thoughts.
Through the Divine's grace, our minds and bodies find peace. Without the Divine, our lives are meaningless.

blocks.scenario: You are facing a difficult situation and don't understand why it's happening.

choices.text: Trust that there is a reason, even if you don't understand it, and continue with faith.
Become angry and resentful, questioning why this is happening to you.

blocks.why: Trusting in the Divine's plan, even when it's unclear, aligns with the lesson's emphasis on devotion and accepting the Divine's actions.

blocks.question: According to this lesson, what cools and soothes our body and mind?

blocks.text: By surrendering to the Divine's love and grace, we can find peace and meaning in our lives.
The Divine can transform anyone and protects those who serve. Remembering the Divine brings peace and ends struggles.
Service to the Divine is the greatest treasure. The Divine embraces us and cherishes our love.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling stressed and overwhelmed by daily tasks.

choices.text: Take a few moments to meditate or remember the Divine, seeking inner peace.
Continue rushing through tasks, ignoring your feelings of stress.

blocks.why: Taking time for remembrance aligns with the lesson's emphasis on finding peace through meditation on the Divine.

blocks.question: According to this lesson, what is the treasure of treasures?

blocks.text: By serving the Divine and remembering the Divine's presence, we can find peace and overcome challenges.
The Divine purifies sinners and asks us not to dwell on errors. The Guru has saved us completely.
The Divine is our life and breath, our wealth and peace. By the Divine's grace, egotism is burned away, and we find happiness.

blocks.scenario: You make a mistake at work that causes a minor problem.

choices.text: Acknowledge the mistake, learn from it, and move forward without dwelling on it.
Become consumed by guilt and self-criticism, unable to focus on anything else.

blocks.why: Acknowledging the mistake and moving forward aligns with the lesson's message of not dwelling on errors and seeking the Divine's grace.

blocks.question: According to this lesson, what burns away the curtain of egotism?

blocks.text: By seeking the Divine's grace and guidance, we can overcome egotism and find lasting happiness.
The Divine pervades our minds and bodies, dispelling pain and suffering. The Divine has shown mercy without considering our merits or demerits.
Singing praises of the Divine brings peace and destroys negativity. We should preserve our faith in the Divine.

blocks.scenario: You are facing a challenging situation and feeling discouraged.

choices.text: Maintain faith and trust in the Divine, seeking strength and guidance.
Give up hope and succumb to feelings of despair.

blocks.why: Maintaining faith aligns with the lesson's emphasis on preserving faith in the Divine during difficult times.

blocks.question: According to this lesson, what is dispelled when the Divine pervades our minds and bodies?

blocks.text: By maintaining faith and seeking the Divine's grace, we can overcome challenges and find peace.
Without remembering the Divine, we wander in egotism and become engrossed in corruption. Coming to the Divine's sanctuary removes our sins.
Life slips away when we are cheated by ego and sin. In the company of the holy, we can dwell upon the Divine and find liberation.

blocks.scenario: You are tempted to gossip about a friend behind their back.

choices.text: Refrain from gossiping and instead focus on positive qualities of your friend.
Indulge in the gossip, feeling a temporary sense of superiority.

blocks.why: Refraining from gossip aligns with avoiding corruption and seeking the company of the holy, as taught in the lesson.

blocks.question: According to this lesson, what vanishes when we come to the Divine's sanctuary?

blocks.text: By avoiding ego and seeking the company of the holy, we can find liberation and dwell upon the Divine.

We read: "Renouncing egotistical pride and other anxieties, I have sought the Sanctuary of the Holy Saints. Chanting, meditating on Your Name, O my Beloved, disease is eradicated from my body. Says Nanak, I have met the Perfect Guru; my comings and goings have ended."

This pauri speaks of finding peace and healing through devotion. By letting go of ego and anxieties and seeking the company of holy people, one can find solace.  Meditating on the Divine Name brings healing, and meeting the Guru ends the cycle of birth and death.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling overwhelmed by stress and anxiety.  You can either A) spend the evening alone, worrying, or B) attend a gathering with friends who share your spiritual values.

choices.text: Spend the evening alone, worrying.
Attend a gathering with friends who share your spiritual values.

blocks.why: Choosing B aligns with the pauri's emphasis on finding peace through the company of holy people (sangat) and meditating on the Divine Name.

blocks.question: According to this pauri, what is eradicated by chanting the Divine Name?

blocks.text: Finding sanctuary in good company and meditating can bring peace.

We read: "Pain is gone, and my mind is comforted; the music of bliss fascinates me. The yearning to meet my Beloved God has welled up within me. I cannot live without Him, even for an instant. Nanak has found God, of endless virtues."

This pauri expresses a deep longing and love for the Divine.  It speaks of the comfort and bliss that come from this yearning. The devotee feels they cannot live without the Beloved, and recognizes the endless virtues of God.

blocks.scenario: You feel a strong connection to something you love. Do you A) push the feeling away, thinking it's impractical, or B) embrace the feeling and allow it to inspire you?

choices.text: Push the feeling away, thinking it's impractical.
Embrace the feeling and allow it to inspire you.

blocks.why: Choosing B reflects the pauri's emphasis on embracing the yearning and love for the Divine, which brings comfort and bliss.

blocks.question: According to this pauri, what fascinates the mind?

blocks.text: Embracing love and longing can bring comfort and peace.

We read: "Eradicate all egotism, and then you shall find your Beloved Lord within the home of your heart. Meditate on the Lord, the embodiment of bliss. The Enticing Lord has revealed His form to me, my thirst is totally quenched. I have found my Beloved, Enticing Lord."

This pauri suggests that by removing ego, one can find the Divine within.  Meditation brings bliss, and the Lord reveals Himself, quenching all desires.  The ultimate goal is to find the Beloved Lord.

blocks.scenario: You are working on a group project. Do you A) insist on doing things your way, or B) try to let go of your ego and work collaboratively?

choices.text: Insist on doing things your way.
Try to let go of your ego and work collaboratively.

blocks.why: Choosing B aligns with the pauri's message of eradicating egotism to find inner peace and connection.

blocks.question: According to this pauri, what must be eradicated to find the Beloved Lord?

blocks.text: Letting go of ego can help you find inner peace and connection.

We read: "My ego is gone; I have obtained the Blessed Vision of the Lord's Darshan. I am absorbed in my Lord and Master, the help and support of the Saints. O mind, join the Company of the Holy, and turn away from the world. O Nanak, love the Feet, the Feet of the Lord."

This pauri describes the experience of losing ego and finding Divine vision.  It emphasizes being absorbed in the Lord and finding support in the company of saints.  The mind is encouraged to turn away from worldly distractions and focus on love for the Divine.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling disconnected. Do you A) isolate yourself further, or B) seek out supportive community and spiritual connection?

choices.text: Isolate yourself further.
Seek out supportive community and spiritual connection.

blocks.why: Choosing B aligns with the pauri's emphasis on finding support and connection in the company of the holy (sangat).

blocks.question: According to this pauri, what is obtained when ego is gone?
blocks.answer: The Blessed Vision of the Lord's Darshan.

blocks.text: Seeking supportive community and turning towards the Divine can help you feel more connected.

We read: "The Name of the Lord is the Dispeller of sorrow - realize this. Remembering Him in meditation, even Ajaamal the robber and Ganikaa the prostitute were liberated. The elephant's fear was taken away in an instant, as soon as he chanted the Lord's Name. Nanak says the Lord is the Saving Grace and the Protector of His devotees."

This pauri highlights the power of the Divine Name to dispel sorrow and grant liberation.  Even those who have made mistakes can be saved through meditation.  The Lord is described as a protector, offering grace and fearlessness.

blocks.scenario: You are facing a difficult challenge. Do you A) give in to fear and despair, or B) remember the Divine Name and seek inner strength?

choices.text: Give in to fear and despair.
Remember the Divine Name and seek inner strength.

blocks.why: Choosing B aligns with the pauri's message that remembering the Divine Name dispels sorrow and fear.

blocks.question: According to this pauri, what is the Dispeller of sorrow?

blocks.text: Remembering the Divine Name can help you overcome challenges and find inner strength.

We read: "Without the Name of the Lord, you shall only find pain. Without devotional worship, doubt is not dispelled. One who lays aside both pride and attachment, sings the Glorious Praises of the Lord of the Universe. Says Nanak, the mortal who does this is said to be 'jivan mukta' - liberated while yet alive."

This pauri emphasizes that true peace comes from devotion and remembrance of the Divine Name.  Without it, there is only pain and doubt.  Liberation comes from letting go of pride and attachment and singing praises of the Lord.

blocks.scenario: You are struggling with doubts and anxieties. Do you A) try to ignore the feelings, or B) engage in devotional practices and try to let go of pride and attachment?

choices.text: Try to ignore the feelings.
Engage in devotional practices and try to let go of pride and attachment.

blocks.why: Choosing B aligns with the pauri's message that devotional worship dispels doubt and that liberation comes from letting go of pride and attachment.

blocks.question: According to this pauri, what is not dispelled without devotional worship?

blocks.text: Devotion and detachment can help you find peace and overcome doubt.

We read: "There is no meditation on the Lord within him. That man wastes his life uselessly. He bathes at sacred shrines of pilgrimage, and adheres to fasts, but he has no control over his mind. Know that such religion is useless to him. So, understand it: that mortal being who lacks devotional worship is just like that."

This pauri suggests that without inner devotion, outward religious practices are meaningless.  A person who lacks control over their mind and does not meditate on the Lord wastes their life.  True devotion is essential.

blocks.scenario: You are going through the motions of a routine. Do you A) continue without reflection, or B) pause and consider whether your actions are aligned with your inner values?

choices.text: Continue without reflection.
Pause and consider whether your actions are aligned with your inner values.

blocks.why: Choosing B aligns with the pauri's message that outward actions are meaningless without inner devotion and control of the mind.

blocks.question: According to this pauri, what is lacking in a person who wastes their life?

blocks.text: Inner devotion and reflection are essential for a meaningful life.

We read: "In this Dark Age of Kali Yuga, liberation comes from the Naam. Without the Fear of God, there is no devotional worship. Imbued with the Word of the Shabad, eternal peace is attained. Says Nanak, he alone is a great man, who sings the Praises of God."

This pauri states that liberation in this age comes through the Divine Name.  Devotional worship requires the Fear of God (respect and reverence).  Eternal peace is found by being imbued with the Word. Singing praises of God makes one great.

blocks.scenario: You are trying to find inner peace. Do you A) ignore your spiritual side, or B) engage in devotional practices and remember the Divine Name?

choices.text: Ignore your spiritual side.
Engage in devotional practices and remember the Divine Name.

blocks.why: Choosing B aligns with the pauri's message that liberation and peace come through the Divine Name and devotional worship.

blocks.question: According to this pauri, what brings liberation in this age?

blocks.text: Remembering the Divine Name and engaging in devotional practices can help you find inner peace and liberation.
Many talk of spiritual wisdom, arguing and suffering without liberation. Spiritual wisdom and meditation come from the Guru; living truthfully brings the True Lord into the mind.
Maya traps the mind, and every heart is caught by sin. Everyone who comes is subject to death. Contemplating the Lord in your heart can adjust your affairs.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling overwhelmed by worries about the future and material possessions.

choices.text: Take a moment to reflect on the Lord and the teachings of the Guru.
Continue to focus on acquiring more possessions to ease your worries.

blocks.why: Reflecting on the Lord helps adjust affairs, aligning with the tags of spiritual wisdom and detachment from Maya.

blocks.question: According to the text, what traps the mind?

blocks.text: Remember to contemplate the Lord in your heart.
A spiritual teacher focuses on the Shabad. The Creator inspires devotion and blesses the Gurmukh. Those lacking the Naam are considered false.

The Vedas preach devotion, and listening and believing allows one to behold the Divine Light. The Shaastras and Simritees instill the Naam. The Gurmukh lives in peace, while the self-willed suffer reincarnation; bonds are broken by enshrining the Name.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling disconnected from your spiritual practice.

choices.text: Focus on the Shabad and Naam through prayer or meditation.
Continue with your daily routine, hoping the feeling will pass.

blocks.why: Focusing on the Shabad and Naam aligns with the tags and brings one closer to the Divine Light.

blocks.question: What does the text say about those who lack the Naam?

blocks.text: Focus on the Shabad to connect with the Divine.
Believing in the Naam brings honor. The mind acts on its wishes, feeding on virtue and vice. Intoxication with Maya never satisfies.
Satisfaction comes when the mind pleases the True Lord. Pride comes from focusing on possessions, but without the Name, nothing goes with you.

choices.text: Reflect on whether the purchase aligns with the Naam and true satisfaction.
Make the purchase to temporarily satisfy your desires.

blocks.why: Reflecting on the Naam helps avoid intoxication with Maya, aligning with the lesson's tags.

blocks.question: According to the text, what never brings satisfaction?

blocks.text: Seek satisfaction in the Naam, not in Maya.
One may enjoy pleasures, but wealth passes on, and the body turns to ashes. Without the Shabad, filth remains. Duality brings pain.
The Gurmukh finds emancipation by singing praises. Forgetting the Naam leads to drinking the wine of Maya, and without the Guru, there is no peace.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling conflicted between worldly desires and spiritual pursuits.

choices.text: Focus on the Shabad and singing praises to find balance.
Indulge in worldly desires, hoping to find satisfaction.

blocks.why: Focusing on the Shabad helps remove filth and avoid the wine of Maya, aligning with the lesson's tags.

blocks.question: According to the text, what is needed to remove filth?

blocks.text: Seek peace through the Shabad and Guru's guidance.
Without guidance, one is bound in cycles. Serving the Guru reveals the treasure. With the Naam, one prospers and is approved by the Lord.
Meeting the Guru allows one to know the Lord and act according to His Will. Understanding Hukam leads to dwelling in the Lord's Court, and the Shabad ends death and birth.

blocks.scenario: You are unsure of which path to take in life.

choices.text: Seek guidance from the Guru and reflect on the Naam.
Follow your own desires without seeking spiritual guidance.

blocks.why: Seeking guidance from the Guru and reflecting on the Naam aligns with the tags and leads to prosperity.

blocks.question: According to the text, what is found by serving the Guru?

blocks.text: Seek guidance from the Guru to find your path.
One remains detached knowing all belongs to God, dedicating body and mind. Absorbed in Truth, one merges with the True Lord.
The world may preach wisdom, but greed, falsehood, and pride lie within. Serving the Guru allows the Naam to dwell in the mind; without the Name, other loves are false.

One who doesn't understand themselves cannot instruct others. Serve the Lord, the searcher of hearts; nothing can be hidden from Him.

choices.text: Chant the Naam and remember the Guru's teachings to eradicate ego.

blocks.why: Chanting the Naam and remembering the Guru helps eradicate ego, aligning with the lesson's tags.

blocks.text: Spiritual wisdom and the Lord's Name can protect us from negative influences and guide us towards love for reality.
These verses emphasize singing the Lord's praises and finding satisfaction through the Guru's teachings. Attachment to Maya is contrasted with absorption in bliss.
The Gurmukh's mind finds its home and meets the Lord. Listening to the Guru's Bani softens the soul. While some are engrossed in Maya, the Gurmukh finds bliss and sees God in all.

The Gurmukh knows the unknowable through the Lord's Name. Joining the Society of Saints elevates one's status. Meditating on the Lord protects one from negative influences and leads to salvation.

blocks.question: What permeates all, according to these verses?
blocks.answer: The Light of the Lord's Name.

blocks.text: The Lord's Name and the Society of Saints can bring connection, elevation, and protection.
These verses compare the True Guru to a sandalwood tree, spreading fragrance. Egotistical pride is seen as a barrier to the Lord.
Meeting the True Guru transforms one into gold. The treasure of devotional worship is found in the Guru's teachings. Focusing on the Guru's Feet brings faith and a hunger for the Lord's praises.

blocks.scenario: You are struggling with feelings of pride and self-importance. Should you:

choices.text: Seek guidance from the True Guru and focus on humility and devotion.

blocks.text: Meeting the True Guru, focusing on humility, and cultivating faith can lead to transformation and devotion.
These verses discuss detachment through meditating on the Lord and chanting His praises. Eradicating egotism leads to purity.
The Shaastras advise righteous actions, but hypocritical people are ruined by doubt and greed. Chanting the Naam leads to emancipation. Eradicating egotism purifies and elevates one's status.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling overwhelmed by worldly desires and attachments. Should you:

These verses emphasize that all actions are guided by the Lord's will. Meditating on the Lord and meeting the True Guru leads to absorption in the Lord's Name.

We are instruments of the Lord's will. The Gurmukh meditates on the Inaccessible Lord and finds the Lord's Name dwelling within. The Lord's Name is the support of His servants, and Guru's Grace leads to the Lord's Court.

blocks.scenario: You are facing a difficult decision and unsure of which path to take. Should you:

choices.text: Seek guidance from the True Guru and meditate on the Lord's Name to understand His will.

blocks.why: Seeking guidance from the True Guru aligns with the tags 'hukam,' 'guru,' and 'naam' by emphasizing reliance on spiritual wisdom and devotion to understand the Lord's will.

blocks.question: What is the only support of His humble servants?

blocks.text: By seeking the True Guru and meditating on the Lord's Name, one can understand His will and attain His Court.
These verses describe the body as a field of karma where Gurmukhs harvest essence. The Ambrosial Water of the Naam extinguishes desires.

The Naam manifests as a priceless jewel. Dedicating mind and intellect to the Guru allows one to speak the Unspoken. While self-willed people are consumed by desire, the Guru's teachings provide the Ambrosial Water of the Naam to extinguish that fire.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling consumed by desires and unable to find peace. Should you:

choices.text: Follow the Guru's teachings and seek the Ambrosial Water of the Naam to extinguish the fire of desire.

blocks.why: Following the Guru's teachings aligns with the tags 'karma,' 'naam,' and 'desire' by emphasizing devotion and detachment from worldly desires.

This mind dances before the True Guru. The egotistical person performs rituals, but these are like sand castles that crumble.

B) Rely solely on your own understanding, disregarding advice.

blocks.why: Option A aligns with the lesson by suggesting humility before the Guru, while option B reflects ego.

Just as waves merge back into the ocean, we can merge with the Divine. Being in the company of holy people and serving them can bring us closer to this union.

blocks.scenario:

Isolate yourself and avoid social interaction.

blocks.why: Option A reflects the value of Sangat, while option B is the opposite.

blocks.text: Connecting with others on a spiritual path can help us merge with the Divine.

Renouncing worldly life alone does not quiet the mind. True peace comes when the mind finds refuge in the company of holy people and the Divine.

blocks.scenario:

B) Constantly pursue new experiences and possessions.

Constantly pursue new experiences and possessions.

blocks.why: Option A reflects seeking sanctuary, while option B reflects the wandering mind.

blocks.question: When does the wandering mind return home?
blocks.answer: When it seeks the Sanctuary of the Lord's Holy people.

Minds still yearn for riches. Satisfaction and tranquility do not come, but meeting the Holy Saints, they are satisfied through the Name of the Lord.
Desires for material things do not bring lasting peace. True contentment arises from connecting with holy people and focusing on the Divine Name.

Obsess over acquiring more wealth and material goods.

blocks.why: Option A reflects contentment through Naam, while option B reflects yearning for riches.

blocks.question: How can one attain satisfaction and tranquility?
blocks.answer: By meeting the Holy Saints and through the Name of the Lord.

blocks.text: True wealth lies not in possessions, but in contentment and connection with the Divine.
The Lord has showered His Mercy upon him. Hearing the Word of the Guru's Teachings, my mind is pierced by His arrow.
Divine grace is received through the Guru's teachings. These teachings can deeply affect the mind, awakening a thirst for the Divine.

blocks.scenario:
You are feeling lost and confused. Do you:
A) Seek guidance from a spiritual mentor or teacher.
B) Ignore your feelings and continue as before.

choices.text: Seek guidance from a spiritual mentor or teacher.
Ignore your feelings and continue as before.

blocks.why: Option A reflects seeking the Guru's teachings, while option B is the opposite.

blocks.question: What pierces the mind?
blocks.answer: The Word of the Guru's Teachings.

blocks.text: Guidance from the Guru can awaken a deep longing for the Divine within us.
I have a great longing to see my God. I sacrifice my mind and body to the Guru, who has shown me the Way.
A deep yearning for the Divine can inspire devotion. Surrendering to the Guru's guidance can reveal the path to God.

blocks.scenario:
You feel a strong desire to connect with something greater than yourself. Do you:
A) Dedicate time to spiritual practices and seek guidance from a trusted mentor.
B) Dismiss your feelings and focus solely on worldly pursuits.

choices.text: Dedicate time to spiritual practices and seek guidance from a trusted mentor.
Dismiss your feelings and focus solely on worldly pursuits.

blocks.why: Option A reflects devotion and seeking the Guru, while option B is the opposite.

blocks.question: What do you sacrifice to the Guru?

blocks.text: Devotion and surrender to the Guru can reveal the path to the Divine.
If the soul-bride adorns herself with compassion and forgiveness, her mind is illumined with the lamp of the Guru's wisdom. My mind tinged with devotion is the intricate ornament.
Compassion and forgiveness are virtues that please the Divine. A mind filled with devotion is a beautiful adornment.

blocks.scenario:
Someone has wronged you. Do you:
A) Practice forgiveness and try to understand their perspective.
B) Hold onto resentment and seek revenge.

choices.text: Practice forgiveness and try to understand their perspective.
Hold onto resentment and seek revenge.

blocks.why: Option A reflects compassion and forgiveness, while option B is the opposite.

blocks.question: What adorns the soul-bride?

blocks.text: Compassion, forgiveness, and devotion are virtues that illuminate the mind.
My mind and body are filled with love for my Inaccessible Lord. Gazing upon the Guru, my mind's faith is fulfilled.
Love for the Divine fills the being with faith. Seeing and connecting with the Guru fulfills the mind's longing.

blocks.scenario:
You are feeling doubtful about your spiritual path. Do you:
A) Seek the company of your Guru and reflect on their teachings.
B) Give up on your spiritual practices and lose faith.

choices.text: Seek the company of your Guru and reflect on their teachings.
Give up on your spiritual practices and lose faith.

blocks.why: Option A reflects faith in the Guru, while option B is the opposite.

blocks.question: What is filled with love for the Inaccessible Lord?

blocks.text: Love and faith in the Guru can fulfill the mind's deepest longings.
This lesson explores the pain of separation from God and the intense thirst for reunion. It speaks of the suffering caused by this separation and the longing for divine connection.

The verses describe the pain felt in every part of the being due to separation from God. Like someone addicted to opium, the writer feels they cannot live without their Beloved. Only union with God can quench this thirst and end the suffering.

blocks.scenario: You feel disconnected from your friends and family. Do you:

choices.text: Acknowledge the feeling of separation and seek ways to reconnect with them.
Ignore the feeling and distract yourself with other activities.

blocks.why: Acknowledging the feeling of separation and seeking connection mirrors the lesson's emphasis on recognizing the pain of separation and longing for union.

blocks.question: According to the lesson, what causes pain in the mind and body?

blocks.text: Recognizing the feeling of separation can motivate us to seek deeper connection.
This lesson contrasts the self-willed individual with one who seeks the Guru's guidance. It highlights the importance of devotion and surrendering to a higher power.

The verses suggest that those who are self-centered wander aimlessly, while those who seek the Guru find union with God without delay. True devotion, inspired by the Guru, leads to merging with the Divine.

blocks.scenario: You are facing a difficult decision. Do you:

choices.text: Seek advice from a trusted mentor or guide.
Rely solely on your own judgment.

blocks.why: Seeking guidance from a trusted source aligns with the lesson's emphasis on the importance of the Guru in finding the right path.

blocks.question: According to the lesson, what helps one find union with God?

blocks.text: Seeking guidance can help us navigate life's challenges with greater clarity.
This lesson focuses on the grace of God and the importance of seeking refuge in Him. It emphasizes abandoning other attachments and surrendering to the Divine will.

The verses describe God's mercy in uplifting and saving those who seek His sanctuary. The writer expresses their inability to fully praise God and declares their devotion, stating that there is nowhere else to go but to Him.

blocks.scenario: You feel overwhelmed by life's challenges. Do you:

choices.text: Seek comfort and strength in your faith or spiritual practice.
Try to handle everything on your own without seeking support.

blocks.why: Seeking comfort in faith aligns with the lesson's emphasis on finding refuge in God during difficult times.

blocks.question: According to the lesson, what does God shower upon us?

blocks.text: Finding solace in faith can provide strength and resilience in the face of adversity.
This lesson explores the power of chanting the Lord's Name and the importance of associating with holy people. It highlights the transformative effect of love and devotion.
The verses suggest that chanting the Lord's Name cleanses sins and leads to emancipation. The company of saints guides one across the world-ocean, and love for the Lord binds the mind to the Divine.

blocks.scenario: You want to improve your well-being. Do you:

choices.text: Engage in practices that bring you closer to your values and connect with others who share them.
Focus solely on material possessions and personal achievements.

blocks.why: Engaging in meaningful practices and connecting with like-minded individuals aligns with the lesson's emphasis on the power of Naam and Sangat.

blocks.question: According to the lesson, what is burnt off by chanting the Lord's Name?

blocks.text: Connecting with our values and community can lead to a more fulfilling life.
This lesson emphasizes the importance of constantly remembering God and serving Him. It highlights the power of devotion and the limitations of human understanding.

The verses suggest that those who remember God will never go to hell, and those who listen to the Divine Word will not fear death. The Lord is under the power of His devotees, and His limits are unknown.

blocks.scenario: You want to cultivate inner peace. Do you:

choices.text: Regularly engage in practices that connect you to something larger than yourself.
Focus solely on your own needs and desires.

blocks.why: Engaging in practices that connect you to something larger aligns with the lesson's emphasis on remembering God and serving Him.

blocks.question: According to the lesson, what happens to those who constantly remember God?
blocks.answer: They will never go to hell.

blocks.text: Connecting to something larger than ourselves can bring a sense of peace and purpose.
This lesson focuses on humility, seeking the company of the holy, and meditating on the Lord's Name. It emphasizes surrendering to God's will and yearning for divine connection.

The verses express a desire to be the dust of the feet of the holy and to be released from birth and death. The writer finds sweetness in the Lord's love and seeks to be attached to His robe, meditating on the Naam.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling proud of an accomplishment. Do you:

choices.text: Acknowledge your accomplishment with gratitude and humility.
Brag about your accomplishment and seek praise from others.

blocks.why: Acknowledging accomplishments with gratitude and humility aligns with the lesson's emphasis on humility and surrendering to God's will.

blocks.question: According to the lesson, what does Nanak meditate on?
blocks.answer: The Naam, the Name of the Lord.

blocks.text: Practicing humility can foster deeper connections with ourselves and others.
This lesson warns against the dangers of worldly attachments, greed, and fear. It emphasizes seeking refuge in God and surrendering to His will.

The verses describe the world as a pit of poison and the human body as being bound by greed and attachment. The writer seeks God's hand to be saved and acknowledges that without Him, there is no place to go.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling anxious about the future. Do you:

choices.text: Acknowledge your fears and seek comfort in your faith or spiritual practice.
Try to control every aspect of your life to avoid uncertainty.

blocks.why: Acknowledging fears and seeking comfort in faith aligns with the lesson's emphasis on seeking refuge in God.

blocks.question: According to the lesson, what is the world?

blocks.text: Finding comfort in faith can help us navigate uncertainty with greater peace.
This lesson expresses intense love and devotion for God, emphasizing hope and longing for His presence. It uses metaphors to describe the depth of this love.

The verses describe the mind's thirst for God's love and the longing for His blessed vision. The writer states that they cannot survive without Him and uses metaphors like the partridge and the moon, the fish and water, to illustrate the depth of their love.

blocks.scenario: You want to deepen your connection with a loved one. Do you:

choices.text: Express your love and appreciation for them in meaningful ways.
Take their presence in your life for granted.

blocks.why: Expressing love and appreciation aligns with the lesson's emphasis on love and devotion.

blocks.question: According to the lesson, what is the mind thirsty for?
blocks.answer: God's Love and the Blessed Vision of His Darshan.

blocks.text: Expressing love and appreciation can strengthen our relationships and bring greater joy.
This pauri uses analogies to describe devotion. Just as a moth is drawn to a lamp, and a deer to a bell's sound, our tongue should chant the Naam.
Singing praises, hearing them, and writing them brings rewards. Joining the Saadh Sangat (holy congregation) allows us to sing praises. Nanak seeks sanctuary and blessings.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling overwhelmed by daily tasks.  You remember this teaching.

choices.text: Join an online sangat to listen to kirtan (devotional singing).
Continue working, hoping the feeling will pass.

blocks.why: Joining the sangat and singing praises aligns with the teaching on devotion.

blocks.question: What is the Saadh Sangat?

blocks.text: Devotion, like a moth to a flame, can guide us.
This pauri speaks of the One Creator, seen in every heart. It emphasizes the importance of the Guru's grace and the Shabad.
The Creator is unique, beyond form, yet found within. Through the Guru's Shabad, the Lord's presence is revealed. Without the Shabad, there is no release.

blocks.scenario: You feel disconnected and alone. You recall this teaching about the Guru's Shabad.

choices.text: Listen to or recite Gurbani (Guru's word).

blocks.why: Listening to or reciting Gurbani connects you to the Guru's Shabad, as described in the teaching.

blocks.question: What reveals the Lord's presence?

blocks.text: The Guru's Shabad can reveal the Divine within.
This pauri describes the creation of the universe and all beings. It emphasizes that the Creator watches over all.
The True Lord created the universe, joining and separating elements. There is no other Creator. The One who fashioned all things knows their value and pervades them.

blocks.scenario: You are amazed by the complexity of nature during a walk in the park. You remember this teaching.

choices.text: Reflect on the Creator who made and watches over all of this.
Simply enjoy the scenery without further thought.

blocks.why: Reflecting on the Creator aligns with the teaching that the One who created the Creation also watches over it.

blocks.question: Who watches over the Creation?

blocks.text: The Creator's presence is in all creation.

Some are consumed by doubt and desire, while others taste the Shabad's essence. Through Truth, the truthful merge with the True Lord. Following the Guru's teachings leads to devotional worship.

blocks.scenario: You feel envious of someone's possessions. You remember this teaching.

choices.text: Reflect on the Shabad and find contentment in what you have.
Continue to dwell on your desires and envy.

blocks.why: Reflecting on the Shabad aligns with the teaching about finding satisfaction in its essence.

blocks.question: What can satisfy our desires?

blocks.text: The Shabad can bring contentment.

When the body is filled with Truth and contentment, and the mind is focused on the Lord, one is protected. This world is the child of Maya, but God is the eternal protector.

blocks.scenario: You are worried about the future. You remember this teaching.

choices.text: Remember that God is your protector from the beginning.
Continue to worry about what might happen.

blocks.why: Remembering God as your protector aligns with the teaching about God's eternal protection.

blocks.question: Who is the protector from the beginning?

blocks.text: God is our eternal protector.
This pauri emphasizes meditating on the Naam, the purity of Truth, and detachment. The Gurmukh is emancipated through practicing Truth.
Meditating on the Naam and giving to charity purifies us. Truth cannot be polluted. The Gurmukh, practicing Truth, finds emancipation.

blocks.scenario: You are tempted to gossip about someone. You remember this teaching.

choices.text: Refrain from gossiping and focus on Truth.
Give in to the temptation and gossip.

blocks.why: Refraining from gossip and focusing on Truth aligns with the teaching about practicing Truth.

blocks.question: Who is emancipated through practicing Truth?

blocks.text: Truth leads to emancipation.
This pauri speaks of detachment, compassion, and the all-encompassing nature of the One Lord. Purity and self-discipline are found in knowing the Truth.
Detachment from worldly desires and faith in the Guru protect us. Compassion and charity are important. The One Lord is contained in all three worlds.

blocks.scenario: You see someone in need of help. You remember this teaching.

choices.text: Offer help and show compassion.
Ignore the person and continue with your day.

blocks.why: Offering help and showing compassion aligns with the teaching about compassion and charity.

blocks.question: What are important qualities to practice?

blocks.text: Compassion and charity are key.
This pauri discusses focusing on God, contemplating the Shabad, and the cycle of reincarnation. Detachment amidst attachment is valued.
By focusing on God and contemplating the Shabad, one merges with Him. The self-willed are caught in reincarnation. Detachment amidst attachment is a virtue.

blocks.scenario: You are caught up in a conflict at work. You remember this teaching.

choices.text: Try to remain detached and find a peaceful resolution.
Become emotionally involved and escalate the conflict.

blocks.why: Remaining detached aligns with the teaching about detachment amidst attachment.

blocks.question: What is valued amidst attachment?

blocks.text: Detachment can bring peace.
This lesson focuses on the pervasiveness of the Divine. The Lord is woven into everything, and understanding this brings peace.

The verses state that the Lord is the Primal Being, present in all things. Whatever happens is by the Creator's will. Being imbued with the Naam brings lasting peace, but understanding this through the Guru is rare.

blocks.scenario: You're feeling overwhelmed by daily tasks and worries. Do you:

choices.text: Remember that the Lord is present in all things and find peace in that understanding.
Continue to feel overwhelmed and try to control everything yourself.

blocks.why: Choosing A aligns with the lesson's message of finding peace by recognizing the Lord's presence in everything, connecting to the tags of oneness and naam.

blocks.question: According to the lesson, what brings lasting peace?

blocks.text: Recognizing the Divine presence can bring peace amidst daily challenges.
This lesson explores how attachment to Maya and egotism can be overcome. Understanding comes through the Guru's Shabad.

The verses explain that the Lord created attachment to Maya and assigns tasks to everyone. Understanding comes through the Guru's Shabad, burning away egotism. The Gurmukh contemplates the Shabad, purifying the mind and obtaining lasting glory.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling consumed by material possessions and pride. Do you:

blocks.why: Choosing A aligns with the lesson's message of overcoming egotism and attachment to Maya through the Guru's Shabad, connecting to the tags of maya, haumai, and shabad.

blocks.question: According to the lesson, what burns away egotism and self-conceit?

blocks.text: Contemplating the Guru's Shabad can help overcome attachment and egotism.
This lesson discusses the pitfalls of duality and the importance of truth. A Gurmukh practices truth and self-restraint.

The verses state that beings attached to duality are deluded. The Creator supports all, and one meets Him only by His will. A Gurmukh contemplates the Lord and practices truth and self-restraint. Without understanding, rituals lead to duality.

choices.text: Seek truth and practice self-restraint, contemplating the Lord.

blocks.question: According to the lesson, what does a Gurmukh practice?

blocks.text: Practicing truth and self-restraint can help overcome duality and find inner peace.
This lesson emphasizes serving the True Guru and embracing love for the Divine. It also touches on emotional attachment to Maya.

The verses state that those who serve the True Guru are fortunate and embrace love for the Lord. The Lord is the giver of peace. Beings attached to Maya experience coming and going, while meeting the Guru leads to understanding and merging in Truth.

blocks.scenario: You have an opportunity to help someone in need. Do you:

choices.text: Selflessly offer your help, embracing love for the True Lord.
Ignore the opportunity, focusing on your own needs and desires.

blocks.why: Choosing A aligns with the lesson's message of serving the True Guru and embracing love, connecting to the tags of seva and love.

blocks.question: According to the lesson, who are very fortunate?
blocks.answer: Those who serve the True Guru.

blocks.text: Serving others and embracing love can lead to inner peace and understanding.
This lesson explores pre-ordained destiny and the importance of serving the True Guru. It also emphasizes the concept of oneness.

The verses state that those with pre-ordained destiny have the One God in their minds. The Lord created the Universe and beholds all. Serving the True Guru leads to understanding and finding the Lord's Door. Renouncing duality leads to knowing the One Lord.

blocks.scenario: You are facing a difficult situation that seems beyond your control. Do you:

blocks.answer: The One God abides within their mind.

This lesson highlights the protection and fearlessness that come from belonging to the Lord. It also emphasizes the importance of serving the True Guru.

The verses state that the Lord's servant is under His protection and is forgiven by Him. Through the Guru's teachings, peace abides within. Serving the True Guru is the most excellent action, leading to truth in the Lord's Court.

blocks.scenario: You are facing a situation that makes you feel afraid. Do you:

blocks.why: Choosing A aligns with the lesson's message of finding fearlessness by belonging to the Lord, connecting to the tag of fearlessness.

blocks.question: According to the lesson, what abides within through the Guru's teachings?

This lesson emphasizes the importance of the True Guru and the pitfalls of duality. It also touches on the soul's loving attunement to the Lord.

blocks.why: Choosing A aligns with the lesson's message of seeking guidance from the True Guru and lovingly attuning oneself to the Lord, connecting to the tags of guru and love.

blocks.why: Option A aligns with the verses' emphasis on connecting with the Divine to burn away fear, reflecting the tags of love, truth, and Naam.

blocks.question: According to these verses, what dwells within when loving the One Lord?

blocks.text: Union with the Divine brings peace, joy, and fulfillment.

This lesson highlights the importance of devotion to the Divine and detachment from worldly desires. It warns against the dangers of ego and a vicious tongue. True fulfillment comes from loving the Lord.

The verses emphasize that without God, we cannot live. A vicious tongue that does not chant the Name is condemned. The verses encourage embracing love for the Lord and detaching from egotism and worldly pleasures.

blocks.scenario: You are offered a promotion that comes with a lot of prestige and material benefits, but it would take you away from your spiritual practices. Do you:

choices.text: Choose to continue with your spiritual practices, detaching from the allure of the promotion.
Accept the promotion, prioritizing prestige and material benefits.

blocks.why: Choosing spiritual practices over material gain is like embracing detachment and devotion, while prioritizing the promotion is like being consumed by ego. This relates to the tags devotion, detachment, and ego.

blocks.question: What should one give up along with sandalwood oil and expensive clothes?

blocks.text: True happiness lies in devotion to the Divine and detachment from worldly desires.

This lesson emphasizes the importance of seeking the Lord through the company of the holy (Saadh Sangat). It highlights the benefits of chanting the Divine Name (Naam) and remembering the Divine. Serving God leads to fulfillment.
The verses encourage joining the Saadh Sangat and singing praises of the Lord. Chanting the Naam brings coolness and peace to the mind. Remembering the Lord helps one cross over to the other shore.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling lost and disconnected. Do you:

choices.text: Seek out a community of like-minded individuals to share and learn from.
Isolate yourself and try to figure things out on your own.

blocks.why: Seeking out a community is like joining the Saadh Sangat, while isolating yourself is the opposite. This relates to the tags sangat, naam, and remembrance.

blocks.question: What cools and soothes the mind and heart?

blocks.text: Finding the company of the holy and remembering the Divine brings peace and fulfillment.

This lesson speaks of the transformative power of Divine love and the importance of the Guru's wisdom. It emphasizes the merging of one's light with the Divine Light. Following the Guru's teachings dispels ignorance.
The verses describe the joy of being drenched in the Lord's love. The light of the individual merges with the Divine Light. The Guru's wisdom dispels darkness and rejuvenates the mind.

blocks.scenario: You are struggling with a difficult decision and feeling lost. Do you:

choices.text: Seek guidance from a trusted mentor or spiritual teacher.
Rely solely on your own understanding, ignoring external advice.

blocks.why: Seeking guidance is like following the Guru's wisdom, while ignoring advice is the opposite. This relates to the tags love, oneness, and guru.

blocks.question: What dispels the darkness of ignorance?
blocks.answer: The light of the Guru's wisdom.

blocks.text: Divine love and the Guru's wisdom lead to enlightenment and union with the Divine.

This lesson emphasizes the all-pervading nature of the Divine and the importance of meditating on the Lord. It warns against self-willedness (Manmukh) and hypocrisy. Serving the Lord brings peace and absorption in the Naam.

The verses describe the Lord as permeating the entire universe. Meditating on the Lord brings deliverance. Self-willedness and hypocrisy prevent one from finding peace. Eradicating self-conceit allows the Divine to dwell within.

blocks.scenario: You are faced with a difficult situation and are unsure of what to do. Do you:

choices.text: Reflect on the Divine and seek guidance from within.
Act impulsively based on your own desires.

blocks.why: Seeking guidance from within is like meditating on the Lord, while acting impulsively is like being self-willed. This relates to the tags oneness, naam, and manmukh.

blocks.question: What does a Gurmukh eradicate from within?

blocks.text: Meditating on the Divine and eradicating self-conceit leads to peace and union with the Lord.

This lesson emphasizes the presence of the Divine within all beings and the importance of following the Guru's will. It warns against egotism (Haumai) and highlights the benefits of serving the Guru. The Lord is the friend of His devotees.
The verses describe the Lord as being within all beings. Walking in harmony with the Guru's will leads to knowing God. Serving the Guru allows one to be freed of egotism and disease.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling proud of your accomplishments and superior to others. Do you:

choices.text: Remember that the Divine is within all beings and treat everyone with humility and respect.
Continue to revel in your superiority and look down on others.

blocks.why: Treating everyone with humility is like remembering the Divine within all beings, while reveling in superiority is like being consumed by egotism. This relates to the tags oneness, guru, and haumai.

blocks.question: What is one freed of when their heart is filled with the Lord?

blocks.text: Recognizing the Divine within all beings and following the Guru's will leads to freedom from egotism and union with the Lord.

This lesson emphasizes the greatness of the Divine Name (Naam) and the importance of meditating on the Lord through the Guru. It highlights the peace that comes from following the Guru's teachings. The Guru's Shabad is Ambrosial Nectar.

The verses describe the greatness of the Naam and the benefits of meditating on the Lord. Telling the secrets of one's soul to the Guru brings peace. The Guru's Shabad is described as Ambrosial Nectar that banishes hunger and thirst.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling overwhelmed by worries and anxieties. Do you:

choices.text: Seek guidance from a spiritual mentor and focus on meditating on the Divine Name.
Try to suppress your feelings and distract yourself with worldly activities.

blocks.why: Seeking guidance and meditating on the Naam is like finding peace through the Guru's teachings, while suppressing feelings is the opposite. This relates to the tags guru, naam, and peace.

blocks.question: What is the Guru's Shabad?

blocks.text: Meditating on the Divine Name through the Guru brings peace and fulfillment.
The Guru contains the greatness of the Name, magnified by the Creator. Servants live by gazing upon it, pleasing their hearts. Slanderers cannot see this greatness.

Hopes in duality tie us to Maya, causing suffering when we forsake the Lord's peace.  The ignorant are reborn repeatedly, regretting their actions.  By abandoning ego through Guru's Grace, one can cross over.

blocks.scenario: You feel pulled between spending time with loved ones and quiet reflection. Which do you choose?

Focus solely on loved ones, setting aside personal reflection.

blocks.question: According to the lesson, what helps one cross over?

The Lord is everywhere, the True Judge. False faces are cursed, while devotees are blessed.  Worship the True Lord and find peace.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling stressed and overwhelmed.  Do you:

choices.text: Listen to spiritual teachings and reflect on the Lord's Name.
Distract yourself with entertainment and ignore your feelings.

blocks.why: This aligns with the lesson's emphasis on Naam, peace, and virtue through Guru's teachings.

blocks.question: What does listening to the Guru's teachings help one obtain?

blocks.text: By connecting with the Guru's teachings, we can find inner peace and virtue.
All rulers are created by the Lord and dependent on Him. Serving the Lord conquers inner enemies. The Lord protects devotees with grace.
Hypocrisy brings pain, while those attuned to the True Name find peace. Meeting the True Guru through karma removes doubt and fear. The Gurmukh finds the Lord's Name pleasing and dispels ignorance.

blocks.scenario: You notice a colleague spreading rumors about another. Do you:

choices.text: Offer support to the person being gossiped about and avoid participating in the rumor mill.
Listen to the rumors and share them with others.

blocks.why: This reflects serving others and avoiding hypocrisy, aligning with the tags of seva, karma, and fear.

blocks.question: What runs away when one is naturally at peace?

blocks.text: By serving others and attuning to the True Name, we can find peace and dispel fear.
Self-willed people die foolishly. Gurmukhs keep the Lord in their hearts. Serve the True Guru to remove ego.
Skepticism causes pain, and attachment to Maya leads to uselessness. True devotion brings the Lord's wealth, while detachment burns away ego. Those imbued with the Naam are balanced and poised.

blocks.scenario: You are offered a promotion that would significantly increase your income but also require longer hours and less time with family. Do you:

choices.text: Consider the impact on your well-being and relationships before making a decision.
Accept the promotion without hesitation, focusing solely on the financial benefits.

blocks.why: This reflects detachment from Maya and prioritizing devotion, aligning with the tags of haumai, devotion, and detachment.

blocks.question: What happens when you serve the True Guru?
blocks.answer: The filth of your ego shall be gone.

blocks.text: By serving the True Guru and detaching from Maya, we can remove ego and find balance.
Praise the One who controls everything. Remember Him, as there is no other. Gurmukhs are at peace within.
Those who don't earn the Lord's Name are bankrupt. Gurmukhs receive the wealth of the Naam through loving service, free from doubt and worry. The Lord hears those He makes His own.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling uncertain about a major life decision. Do you:

choices.text: Seek guidance through prayer and reflection, trusting in the Lord's will.

blocks.why: This reflects seeking the Lord's will and trusting in guidance, aligning with the tags of naam, seva, and doubt.

blocks.question: What departs from within the Gurmukh?

blocks.text: By trusting in the Lord and serving with love, we can overcome doubt and find peace.
One who conquers death has the Immaculate Name within. They remain awake and aware, singing praises to the Lord. Meeting them brings peace.
The Lord's wealth is a jewel granted by the Guru. The Lord's gifts increase continuously. The world is burning, so shower it with mercy. The Guru shows the way to peace, and the Lord is forgiving.

blocks.scenario: You see someone struggling with a difficult task. Do you:

choices.text: Offer your help and support with compassion.
Ignore their struggle and continue with your own tasks.

blocks.why: This reflects showing compassion and mercy, aligning with the tags of naam, compassion, and mercy.

blocks.question: Who is the one who is forgiving?

blocks.text: By showing compassion and seeking the Lord's mercy, we can find peace and help others.
Egotism traps people in duality. Maya is burnt away through the Shabad. The body and mind become pure.
The Guru's greatness is a mark of the Lord's will. The Guru subdues egotistical pride. The Shabad is the killer of Maya, obtained by the Gurmukh.

blocks.scenario: You feel tempted to boast about your accomplishments. Do you:

choices.text: Practice humility and acknowledge the contributions of others.
Take full credit for your achievements and highlight your superiority.

blocks.why: This reflects subduing egotistical pride and focusing on humility, aligning with the tags of maya, shabad, and haumai.

blocks.question: What is the killer of Maya?

blocks.text: By burning away ego through the Shabad, we can purify our minds and connect with the Divine.
Those with the Lord in mind are carried across. The Lord's will prevails. The compassionate Guru eradicates doubts and fears.
The Lord has carried me across. The Guru has destroyed demons. In the Saadh Sangat, birth and death are redeemed. Those who forget the Naam are false, and are plundered by thieves.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling isolated and disconnected. Do you:

choices.text: Seek out the company of spiritual community and engage in uplifting activities.
Withdraw further and avoid social interaction.

blocks.why: This reflects seeking the Saadh Sangat and engaging in uplifting activities, aligning with the tags of naam, sangat, and compassion.

blocks.question: What is redeemed in the Saadh Sangat?

blocks.text: By seeking the Saadh Sangat and remembering the Naam, we can find redemption and overcome isolation.
Serving the True Guru transforms the powerless. With every breath, the Lord abides in their minds, and Maya becomes their servant.
Those who serve the Guru find strength. They remember the Lord constantly, and are protected from negative influences. They value devotion above worldly possessions.

blocks.scenario: You feel overwhelmed by daily tasks and desires. Do you:

choices.text: Take a moment to remember the Lord and seek guidance from the Guru's teachings.
Continue to focus solely on your tasks and desires, hoping the feeling will pass.

blocks.why: Choosing A aligns with the tags by emphasizing the importance of remembering the Lord and seeking guidance from the Guru to overcome feelings of being overwhelmed.

blocks.question: According to this passage, what happens to those who serve the True Guru?
blocks.answer: They are transformed from powerless into powerful.

blocks.text: By remembering the Lord and following the Guru's teachings, we can find strength and overcome challenges.
The Gurmukh chants the Naam, finding bliss. Meeting the True Guru quenches thirst and hunger, bringing celestial peace.
Chanting the Lord's Name brings joy and fulfillment. Connecting with the True Guru satisfies our inner longings. This connection leads to a state of profound peace.

blocks.scenario: You feel restless and unfulfilled. Do you:

choices.text: Engage in Naam Simran and seek the company of those who follow the Guru's path.
Look for external distractions to temporarily alleviate the feeling.

blocks.why: Choosing A aligns with the tags by emphasizing Naam Simran and Sangat as paths to inner peace and fulfillment.

blocks.question: What does meeting the True Guru do?
blocks.answer: It quenches thirst and hunger, and brings celestial peace.

blocks.text: By chanting the Naam and connecting with the True Guru, we can find lasting peace and satisfaction.
Everyone will be taken by the Messenger of Death. The Lord's servants, pleasing to Him, are unique. They never die, remaining with the Supreme Lord.
Death is inevitable for all. Those devoted to the Lord are special and connected to the Divine. They transcend the cycle of birth and death, staying united with the Lord.

blocks.scenario: You are worried about the future and the inevitability of death. Do you:

choices.text: Focus on living a life pleasing to the Lord, seeking to understand His will (Hukam).

blocks.why: Choosing A aligns with the tags by emphasizing devotion to the Lord and acceptance of Hukam as a way to overcome fear of death.

blocks.question: What is unique about those who are pleasing to the Lord?
blocks.answer: They do not come and go, and they never die; they remain with the Supreme Lord God.

blocks.text: By living a life devoted to the Lord, we can find peace and transcend the fear of death.
Renouncing worldly attachments leads to union with the Lord.  The speaker describes being consumed with chanting and hearing the Lord's praises.

Detachment from material possessions and relationships can deepen one's connection with the Divine.  Total devotion can feel like a form of "insanity" to those focused on the material world. The speaker embraces this devotion.

Completely abandon your responsibilities in pursuit of devotion.

blocks.text: By balancing worldly duties with devotion, we can deepen our love for the Divine.
The True Guru removes doubt.  One who doesn't understand themself doesn't know the Lord.  Understanding oneself leads to knowing the One Lord.
The Guru's guidance dispels uncertainty.  Self-awareness is crucial for spiritual understanding.  Knowing oneself is a path to recognizing the Oneness of the Divine.

blocks.scenario: You are struggling with doubts about your spiritual path. Do you:

choices.text: Seek guidance from the Guru and strive for self-understanding.
Ignore your doubts and continue on your path without reflection.

blocks.why: Choosing A aligns with the tags by emphasizing the importance of the Guru's guidance and self-reflection in overcoming doubt and realizing Oneness.

blocks.question: According to the passage, what happens when someone understands themself?

blocks.text: By seeking the Guru's guidance and understanding ourselves, we can overcome doubt and realize the Oneness of the Divine.
One must be intoxicated with the Lord's Love now.  Even abandoning one's household may not save one from this terrifying world-ocean. Seek refuge in the Lord.
True devotion requires present engagement.  External acts alone are insufficient to overcome worldly fears.  Seeking the Lord's protection is essential for navigating life's challenges.

choices.text: Seek refuge in the Lord's love and guidance, while remaining engaged in the world.

blocks.why: Choosing A aligns with the tags by emphasizing the importance of the Lord's love and guidance in overcoming fear and detachment from the world.

blocks.question: What does the passage say about seeking refuge?

blocks.text: By seeking the Lord's love and guidance, we can navigate the world's challenges with courage and detachment.
The speaker struggles with the desire for sin. Life passes without doing good. The Lord is merciful, despite the speaker's sinfulness.

Give in to the habit, feeling hopeless about changing.

blocks.why: Choosing A aligns with the tags by emphasizing the importance of acknowledging sin, seeking compassion, and continuing to strive for improvement.

blocks.question: According to the passage, what is the Lord's nature?

blocks.text: By acknowledging our struggles and seeking the Lord's compassion, we can find strength to overcome negative desires.
One is absorbed in the Lord, not worldly weaving.  Since the son began chanting, there has been no peace.  The boy has ruined the weaving business.

The Lord is the source of all peace, and the Guru has blessed me with His Name. God is the saving grace of His saints.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling anxious about an upcoming presentation. You remember this teaching.

choices.text: Quietly repeat the Guru's Name, seeking peace and strength.

Remember the Lord, and skepticism and doubt will disappear. Practice humility and remember that you have disobeyed.
