The verses suggest that death is a natural process of returning to the source. They highlight the bonds of doubt and attachment that cause suffering, and the illusory nature of life.

blocks.scenario: You experience a loss and feel overwhelmed with grief. Do you cling to your sorrow or try to accept the impermanence of life?

choices.text: Try to accept the impermanence of life.
Cling to your sorrow.

blocks.why: Accepting impermanence aligns with the verses' message of the merging of elements and the illusory nature of life, connecting to the tags of death and attachment.

blocks.question: According to these verses, what binds mortal beings?
blocks.answer: The bonds of doubt and attachment.

blocks.text: Reflecting on the nature of death and impermanence can help us let go of attachments and find peace.
These verses speak of the imperishable nature of the soul. They emphasize the importance of meditating on the Lord and the role of the Guru in dispelling doubt.
The verses suggest that the soul is eternal and does not perish. By meditating on the Lord's Name and following the Guru's guidance, one can overcome doubt and live a fulfilling life.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling uncertain about your future. Do you dwell on your fears or focus on meditating on the Divine and seeking guidance?

choices.text: Focus on meditating on the Divine and seeking guidance.
Dwell on your fears.

blocks.why: Meditating on the Divine and seeking guidance aligns with the verses' message of overcoming doubt and living a fulfilling life through Naam and the Guru, connecting to the tags of naam and guru.

blocks.question: According to these verses, what is imperishable?

blocks.text: Meditating on the Divine and seeking guidance can help us overcome doubt and live with purpose.
We read that after wandering through countless lifetimes, one may find the Saadh Sangat, the Company of the Holy, through destiny. It is said that without the Perfect Guru, no one is saved.

This passage emphasizes the importance of the Saadh Sangat and the Guru in achieving salvation. It suggests that finding the company of the holy is a matter of destiny and that the Guru is essential for spiritual liberation. Deep reflection is needed to understand this.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling lost and disconnected. You have the option to either A) attend a local gathering of spiritual seekers or B) continue isolating yourself.

choices.text: Attend a local gathering of spiritual seekers.
Continue isolating yourself.

blocks.why: Choosing to attend the gathering aligns with the teaching of finding the Saadh Sangat, which is tied to the tags 'sangat' and 'destiny'.

blocks.question: According to this passage, what is needed for salvation?

blocks.text: Finding the right guidance and community can be a matter of destiny.
This passage speaks of the 'village of truth' and how it has diminished over time. It also uses the metaphor of beads on a thread to illustrate how things come together in one place.

The passage suggests that truth has become less prevalent over time, but the One Lord is still revealed. It also uses the analogy of beads on a thread to show how diverse elements are connected and can unite when the thread is pulled.

blocks.scenario: You notice divisions and disagreements in your community. You can either A) focus on the shared values and common ground or B) dwell on the differences and conflicts.

choices.text: Focus on the shared values and common ground.
Dwell on the differences and conflicts.

blocks.why: Focusing on shared values aligns with the idea of 'the one thread' bringing things together, which is tied to the tag 'oneness'.

blocks.question: What is used as a metaphor for unity in this passage?

blocks.text: Despite differences, there is an underlying unity that connects everything.
This passage describes the body as a temple with many windows. It questions why one should be proud of it.
The passage suggests that the body, though created by the Lord, is a temporary and somewhat treacherous dwelling. It questions the basis for pride, implying humility is more appropriate.

blocks.scenario: You receive a compliment on your appearance. You can either A) acknowledge the compliment with humility or B) become overly proud and boastful.

choices.text: Acknowledge the compliment with humility.
Become overly proud and boastful.

blocks.why: Responding with humility aligns with the passage's questioning of pride in the body, which is tied to the tag 'ego'.

blocks.question: According to this passage, what is the body?

blocks.text: Humility is a more appropriate response than pride regarding the body.
This passage speaks of a restless mind that is never satisfied. It suggests one should feel ashamed to beg from others while abandoning the Lord Master.
The passage highlights the dissatisfaction that comes from a wandering mind and unfulfilled desires. It emphasizes the importance of devotion to the Lord Master over seeking fulfillment elsewhere.

blocks.scenario: You feel a constant urge to acquire more possessions, but never feel truly content. You can either A) reflect on what truly fulfills you or B) continue seeking satisfaction through material things.

choices.text: Reflect on what truly fulfills you.
Continue seeking satisfaction through material things.

blocks.why: Reflecting on true fulfillment aligns with the passage's critique of being 'not satisfied' and the importance of the Lord Master, which is tied to the tag 'desire'.

blocks.question: What should one feel when begging from others while abandoning the Lord Master?

blocks.text: True fulfillment comes from within, not from external sources.
This passage describes the one who receives the Master's Mercy and has the Name as their patched coat. Meeting with the Gurmukh brings joy.
The passage emphasizes the importance of the Master's Mercy and the power of the Naam. It suggests that meeting with the Gurmukh leads to experiencing divine love and stability.

blocks.scenario: You have the opportunity to either A) spend time with someone who embodies spiritual wisdom or B) isolate yourself and avoid seeking guidance.

choices.text: Spend time with someone who embodies spiritual wisdom.
Isolate yourself and avoid seeking guidance.

blocks.why: Spending time with a wise person aligns with the idea of 'Meeting with the Gurmukh,' which is tied to the tag 'gurmukh'.

blocks.question: What brings joy according to this passage?

blocks.text: Seeking guidance from those who embody spiritual wisdom can lead to joy and stability.
This passage describes the sweet essence of the Lord and the rare Gurmukh who tastes it. It expresses gratitude for the blessings received.

The passage highlights the transformative power of the Ambrosial Name and the importance of gratitude. It suggests that experiencing the Lord's essence leads to immortality, freedom from desire, and bliss.

blocks.scenario: You experience a moment of profound peace and joy. You can either A) express gratitude for the experience or B) take the experience for granted and move on without reflection.

choices.text: Express gratitude for the experience.
Take the experience for granted and move on without reflection.

blocks.why: Expressing gratitude aligns with the passage's emphasis on being 'forever a sacrifice' and acknowledging the blessings received, which is tied to the tag 'gratitude'.

blocks.question: What does drinking in the Ambrosial Name lead to?

blocks.text: Expressing gratitude for blessings received enhances our spiritual journey.
This passage speaks of being summoned to the Mansion of the Lord's Presence and having the Ambrosial Naam poured into one's mouth. It emphasizes being forever a sacrifice to the Guru.
The passage highlights the transformative power of the Guru and the Naam. It suggests that through the Guru's grace, one is connected to divine service and experiences inner peace.

blocks.scenario: You are presented with an opportunity to either A) volunteer your time to a cause you believe in or B) remain focused solely on your own needs and desires.

choices.text: Volunteer your time to a cause you believe in.
Remain focused solely on your own needs and desires.

blocks.why: Volunteering aligns with the idea of being 'linked to His service' and being 'forever a sacrifice,' which is tied to the tag 'seva'.

blocks.question: What is poured into the mouth by the Divine Guru?

blocks.text: Serving others and connecting to a higher purpose brings inner peace.
This passage describes the glory of the Lord and the one who is blessed with patience. It emphasizes worshipping the One Immaculate Lord alone and seeing the Merciful Lord everywhere.
The passage highlights the importance of faith, patience, and seeing the divine in all things. It suggests that through grace, one overcomes doubt and duality and experiences the oneness of the Lord.

blocks.scenario: You are faced with a difficult situation and feel uncertain about the future. You can either A) trust in the divine and maintain faith or B) succumb to doubt and despair.

choices.text: Trust in the divine and maintain faith.
Succumb to doubt and despair.

blocks.why: Trusting in the divine aligns with the passage's emphasis on 'no doubt' and worshipping the 'One Immaculate Lord alone,' which is tied to the tag 'doubt'.

blocks.question: What should one worship according to this passage?

blocks.text: Trusting in the divine and seeing the good in all things brings peace and clarity.

This lesson focuses on eliminating self-conceit and finding sweetness in God's will. The Guru's protection leads to beholding the wondrous Lord. Wisdom dawns, demons vanish, and thirst is quenched through the Guru's instruction.
When self-conceit is gone, God's will becomes dear. Whatever He does feels sweet. The Guru's mercy and guidance attach us to the Lord's feet, leading to a mind held in check.

blocks.scenario: You feel frustrated when a project at work doesn't go your way. You start to blame others and feel angry.

choices.text: Remember that the Will of God is dear, and try to find the sweetness in the situation. Reflect on what you can learn.
Continue to blame others and dwell on your frustration, letting your anger consume you.

blocks.why: Choosing A aligns with the lesson's tags by reducing haumai (ego) and accepting hukam (God's will), guided by the guru.

blocks.question: According to this passage, what happens when self-conceit is eliminated?
blocks.answer: The Will of God becomes dear.

blocks.text: By letting go of self-conceit and embracing the Guru's guidance, we can find peace and wisdom.
This lesson emphasizes seeing God in all and fostering universal brotherhood. It speaks of having no enemies and walking in peace with everyone. The Guru's blessing brings peace and love of the Lord.

Recognizing God's presence in everyone leads to seeing all as brothers and sisters. When blessed with peace by the Guru, one is cherished and imbued with the love of the Lord. This understanding transcends enmity and fosters unity.

blocks.scenario: You encounter someone with very different political views than your own. You feel tempted to argue and see them as an adversary.

choices.text: Remember that God dwells in all, and try to find common ground. Treat them as a brother or sister.
Engage in a heated argument, focusing on your differences and seeing them as an enemy.

blocks.why: Choosing A aligns with the lesson's tags by promoting oneness and peace, recognizing God in all and avoiding enmity.

blocks.question: According to this passage, where does God dwell?

blocks.text: By seeing God in all and embracing universal brotherhood, we can cultivate love and peace in our lives.

This lesson critiques rituals performed without inner transformation. It questions placing importance on idols and external practices while the mind wanders. True salvation is not found in these ways.

The passage suggests that rituals and outward displays are insufficient if the mind is not focused on the Divine. Eradicating anger and focusing inward is more important than external acts. Salvation is not achieved through these superficial means.

blocks.scenario: You feel pressured to participate in a religious ceremony that feels empty and performative to you.

choices.text: Reflect on the true meaning of the ceremony and focus on connecting with the Divine internally, rather than just going through the motions.
Participate in the ceremony without questioning it, focusing only on the external rituals and hoping for good fortune.

blocks.why: Choosing A aligns with the lesson's tags by addressing ego and doubt, seeking inner meaning rather than being caught in maya (illusion).

blocks.question: According to this passage, what should be eradicated from the mind?

blocks.text: True devotion involves inner transformation and focusing on the Divine, rather than just performing external rituals.

This lesson emphasizes the importance of living the Guru's Shabad and seeking His sanctuary. By embracing the Lord's Name, one overcomes troubles and Maya. The Guru's guidance is essential for spiritual growth.

Living the Guru's Word leads to freedom from Maya and the containment of the Vedas within the Lord's Name. Seeking the Guru's protection shields one from troubles. The Lord's support ensures efforts are fulfilled.

blocks.scenario: You feel overwhelmed by challenges and temptations in your daily life.

choices.text: Turn to the Guru's Shabad for guidance and seek refuge in the Lord's Name, trusting in His support.
Try to handle everything on your own, relying on your own strength and ignoring spiritual guidance.

blocks.why: Choosing A aligns with the lesson's tags by emphasizing the shabad (Guru's word), naam (Lord's name), and seeking the guru's guidance for overcoming challenges.

blocks.question: According to this passage, what leaves a person who lives the Word of the Guru's Shabad?

blocks.text: By living the Guru's Shabad and seeking the Lord's Name, we can overcome challenges and find true support.

This lesson highlights the importance of the Saadh Sangat (holy congregation) for enlightenment and peace. It emphasizes that true worship and meditation are performed by those blessed by the Lord. The Guru's grace brings faith and fulfillment.

Joining the Saadh Sangat leads to enlightenment and celestial peace. True devotion is granted by the Lord, and the Guru blesses one with faith. Being a servant of the servants of the Lord is the ultimate goal.

blocks.scenario: You feel disconnected and spiritually uninspired.

choices.text: Seek out the Saadh Sangat and participate in the holy congregation, seeking enlightenment and peace.
Isolate yourself and continue with your routine, hoping that inspiration will come on its own.

blocks.why: Choosing A aligns with the lesson's tags by emphasizing sangat (holy congregation), faith, and the pursuit of peace through spiritual community.

blocks.question: According to this passage, what is found by joining the Saadh Sangat?

blocks.text: By joining the Saadh Sangat and seeking the Guru's grace, we can find enlightenment, peace, and fulfillment.

This lesson teaches that our actions determine our fate and warns against attachment to worldly possessions. It emphasizes the importance of the Naam (Lord's Name) for true enlightenment. Without the Naam, everything turns to dust.
We are bound by our own actions, not by others. Worldly possessions are temporary and false. True understanding comes through the Guru's Word, and without the Naam, everything is meaningless.

blocks.scenario: You experience a setback and feel tempted to blame others for your misfortune.

choices.text: Reflect on your own actions and take responsibility for your part in the situation, seeking guidance from the Guru's Word.
Blame others for your misfortune and dwell on your anger and resentment.

blocks.why: Choosing A aligns with the lesson's tags by emphasizing karma (actions), detachment from maya (blaming others), and seeking enlightenment through the Guru's word.

blocks.question: According to this passage, what binds us?

blocks.text: By taking responsibility for our actions and seeking the Naam, we can find true enlightenment and break free from the cycle of Maya.

This lesson contrasts egotistical doubt with the ambrosial nectar of the Lord's Name. It emphasizes that worldly possessions are fleeting and that true fulfillment comes from pleasing the Guru. The Saintly remain detached, absorbed in the Supreme Lord.

Egotism leads to delusion, while the Lord's Name is the true nectar. Worldly possessions are temporary. Pleasing the Guru allows one to behold the Lord in every heart. The Saintly remain detached and absorbed in the Divine.

blocks.scenario: You feel tempted to boast about your accomplishments and possessions.

choices.text: Remember that worldly possessions are fleeting and focus on pleasing the Guru through humility and service.
Give in to the temptation and boast about your accomplishments, seeking validation from others.

blocks.why: Choosing A aligns with the lesson's tags by reducing haumai (ego), focusing on the naam (Lord's name), and practicing detachment from worldly possessions.

blocks.question: According to this passage, what is the Ambrosial Nectar in this Dark Age?

blocks.text: By letting go of egotism, embracing the Naam, and practicing detachment, we can find true fulfillment and union with the Divine.

This lesson describes the realm of celestial peace and bliss found in the Saadh Sangat. It emphasizes meditating on the Naam and finding rest in the love of God. By Guru's Grace, one overcomes doubt and fear and enters a state of deep Samaadhi.

The Saadh Sangat is a place of peace where the Lord's praises are sung. Meditating on the Naam and finding love of God leads to a permanent seat in the infinite. By Guru's Grace, one overcomes Maya and enters a state of deep connection with the Divine.

blocks.scenario: You feel anxious and overwhelmed by the challenges in your life.

choices.text: Seek out the Saadh Sangat and meditate on the Naam, trusting in the Guru's Grace to overcome your fears and find peace.
Isolate yourself and dwell on your anxieties, feeling helpless and overwhelmed.

blocks.why: Choosing A aligns with the lesson's tags by emphasizing peace, seeking the sangat (holy congregation), and relying on grace to overcome challenges.

blocks.question: According to this passage, what is found in the Saadh Sangat?

blocks.text: By seeking the Saadh Sangat, meditating on the Naam, and trusting in the Guru's Grace, we can find peace and overcome our fears.
Meeting with the Sangat brings the Supreme Lord into consciousness. In the Sangat, the mind finds contentment. Bowing to the saints is a sign of humility.
Being in the company of the holy (Sangat) allows one to remember God. This remembrance brings a sense of peace and satisfaction. Humility is expressed through reverence for those who are holy.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling restless and dissatisfied. Where might you find peace?

choices.text: Attend a gathering of spiritual people (Sangat).
Go shopping for new things.

blocks.why: The lesson emphasizes finding contentment through the Sangat, aligning with the tags.

blocks.question: What feeling does the mind experience in the Sangat?

blocks.text: Finding peace and contentment can come from connecting with others in a spiritual community.
The grace of the saints protects us. Seeing the saints brings life. They are a treasure of virtue.
The company of holy people (Sangat) is seen as a source of grace and protection. Their presence is uplifting and provides hope. They embody virtue and are a valuable influence.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling lost and unsure of what to do. Who might you turn to for guidance?

choices.text: Seek the company of wise and virtuous people.
Isolate yourself until you figure things out.

blocks.why: The lesson highlights the importance of seeking guidance from virtuous people, aligning with the tags.

blocks.question: What is gained by gazing upon the saints?

blocks.text: Seeking the company of virtuous people can provide guidance and support in life.
Worldly possessions are temporary. Only the Name of the Lord goes with you. Remembering the Lord protects you.
Material things and relationships are not permanent. Focusing on the divine (Naam) is the only thing that truly lasts. Remembering the Lord provides protection from negative forces.

blocks.scenario: You are worried about losing your job and possessions. What should you focus on?

choices.text: Remembering the divine and what truly matters.
Working harder to accumulate more wealth.

blocks.why: The lesson emphasizes the importance of focusing on the divine rather than material possessions, aligning with the tags.

blocks.question: What goes along with you after death?

blocks.text: Focusing on the divine provides lasting value, beyond temporary worldly concerns.
Even the greatest become exhausted trying to fulfill worldly tasks. The Name of the Lord is the support of devotees. Saints' actions are approved.
Efforts focused solely on worldly achievements are ultimately limited. Devotion to the divine (Naam) provides true support. Actions aligned with saintly values are considered virtuous.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling overwhelmed by your workload. What should you consider?

choices.text: Balancing work with devotion and service.
Pushing yourself harder to get everything done.

blocks.why: The lesson suggests balancing worldly tasks with devotion, aligning with the tags.

blocks.question: What is the anchor and support of the Lord's devotees?
blocks.answer: The Naam, the Name of the Lord

blocks.text: Balancing worldly efforts with devotion and service can bring greater fulfillment.
Life is temporary, and attachment to Maya is a dream. Without the Naam, the body is reduced to dust. Focus on what is lasting.
Attachment to worldly illusions (Maya) is fleeting. Without connection to the divine (Naam), life loses its true value. It is important to recognize the impermanence of things.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling anxious about aging and losing your physical appearance. What perspective might help?

choices.text: Recognizing the impermanence of the body and focusing on inner growth.
Spending more money on beauty products to maintain your youth.

blocks.why: The lesson emphasizes detachment from the physical and focusing on the divine, aligning with the tags.

blocks.question: What happens to the body without the Naam?

blocks.text: Recognizing the impermanence of life encourages us to focus on what truly matters.
The Lord is compassionate and merciful. Without the Naam, people are plundered by Maya. Ask for forgiveness and union with the Lord.
The divine is characterized by compassion and mercy. Attachment to worldly illusions (Maya) can lead to spiritual loss. Seeking forgiveness and union with the divine is encouraged.

blocks.scenario: You see people making harmful choices. How should you respond?

choices.text: With compassion, hoping for their forgiveness and guidance.
With judgment and condemnation.

blocks.why: The lesson emphasizes compassion and forgiveness, aligning with the tags.

blocks.question: What is a characteristic of the Lord?

blocks.text: Approaching others with compassion and seeking forgiveness can lead to spiritual growth.
Rituals and egotistical displays do not bring salvation. Without the Naam, there is no peace. The Lord inspires those who chant His name.
External actions and ego-driven behaviors are insufficient for spiritual progress. True peace comes from connecting with the divine (Naam). Chanting the Naam is inspired by the Lord.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling stressed and disconnected. What might you do?

choices.text: Chant the Name of the Lord and seek inner peace.
Engage in activities to impress others.

blocks.why: The lesson emphasizes finding peace through the Naam, aligning with the tags.

blocks.question: What is needed to tear away the screen of illusion?

blocks.text: Inner peace comes from connecting with the divine, not from external displays.
Accepting the Will of God brings happiness. The Saadh Sangat encourages the mind. Truth leads to merging with the True Lord.
Finding joy in God's will is a path to contentment. The company of the holy (Sangat) provides encouragement. Embracing truth leads to union with the divine.

blocks.scenario: You are facing a difficult situation that you cannot change. What is a helpful perspective?

choices.text: Accepting the situation as the Will of God and finding peace within it.
Fighting against the situation and becoming resentful.

blocks.why: The lesson emphasizes accepting the Will of God, aligning with the tags.

blocks.question: What happens when truth is received?
blocks.answer: It is merged in the True Lord

blocks.text: Accepting the Will of God and embracing truth can bring inner peace and connection to the divine.
Meditations rest in the Guru. When we obtain the Blessed Vision, bliss comes and doubts run away.
The Guru's presence is like a sacred pilgrimage site.  The Lord is in every heart, and His glory is radiant. Meeting the Perfect Guru brings peace.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling lost and uncertain.  You can either:

choices.text: Seek guidance and wisdom from a respected mentor or spiritual guide.
Isolate yourself and try to figure things out on your own.

blocks.why: Seeking guidance from a 'Guru' can help dispel doubts and bring peace, aligning with the lesson's tags.

blocks.question: According to this passage, where does the Lord reside?

blocks.text: Finding a Guru can bring peace and dispel doubts.
The Lord's Name is of great value. One who has the Lord's Name within their heart is brave, wise, peaceful, and healthy.
The greatness of the Lord's Name is beyond description.  Those with the Name in their hearts are liberated, their affairs resolved, and they remain unwavering.

blocks.scenario: You are facing a difficult decision. You can either:

choices.text: Reflect on your values and seek inner peace before deciding.
Make a quick decision based on immediate circumstances.

blocks.why: Seeking inner peace aligns with the lesson's emphasis on the Name bringing peace and wisdom.

blocks.question: What qualities does a person with the Lord's Name in their heart possess?
blocks.answer: Brave, patient, perfectly wise, peaceful, blissful, and healthy.

blocks.text: The Lord's Name brings peace and wisdom.
God is Merciful. The Guru blesses us with the Naam. We should fall at the feet of the Perfect Guru.
Meditating on God removes worries.  Singing praises and chanting the Lord's Name provides a home even for the homeless.  Guru's Grace allows us to cross the world-ocean.

blocks.scenario: You feel overwhelmed by life's challenges. You can either:

choices.text: Seek guidance and support from a spiritual mentor or community.
Try to handle everything on your own without asking for help.

blocks.why: Seeking guidance from a 'Guru' and community support aligns with the lesson's emphasis on grace and the Naam.

blocks.question: What removes worries?

blocks.text: Seeking Guru's Grace and chanting the Lord's Name can help overcome life's challenges.
Meditate on the Naam. Drink in the Guru's Shabad. Renounce cleverness and trickery.
The eternal treasure is the Naam.  Meditate on the Lord in the Saadh Sangat (holy congregation). Without the Lord's Name, there is no rest.

blocks.scenario: You are tempted to use dishonest tactics to get ahead. You can either:

choices.text: Choose honesty and integrity, even if it means slower progress.
Use clever tactics to gain an advantage.

blocks.why: Renouncing cleverness and trickery aligns with the lesson's emphasis on detachment and the Naam.

blocks.question: Where should we meditate on the Lord?

blocks.text: Meditating on the Naam and renouncing trickery brings peace.
Play joyfully with the Lord in the Saints' Congregation.  Egotistical intellect shall be dispelled. Peace comes to my home.
In the company of saints, sing the Lord's praises.  Religious rituals and egotism are useless.  By the Grace of the Saints, the heart blossoms.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling stressed and overwhelmed. You can either:

choices.text: Join a community gathering or spend time with supportive friends.
Isolate yourself and try to deal with your stress alone.

blocks.why: Joining a community aligns with the lesson's emphasis on the Saints' Congregation and finding peace.

blocks.question: What is dispelled in the Saints' Congregation?

blocks.text: The Saints' Congregation brings peace and dispels egotism.
The gift of the jewel of the Name brings contentment. Hearing the Lord's sermon brings purity. Such a humble being is exalted.
One who has the Name is content and doesn't need to beg.  Chanting the Lord's sermon leads to salvation.  Humility is valued.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling envious of someone else's possessions. You can either:

choices.text: Practice gratitude for what you have and find contentment.
Focus on acquiring more possessions to feel better.

blocks.why: Practicing gratitude and contentment aligns with the lesson's emphasis on the Name and humility.

blocks.question: What does the gift of the jewel of the Name bring?

blocks.text: The Name brings contentment and humility.
This is the pure philosophy: without the Lord's Name, there is no salvation. Meeting with the Perfect Guru, one is saved. Maya deceives.
Maya seems pleasing but ultimately deceives.  She is unstable and bewitches many.  The Lord's servants detach from her.

blocks.scenario: You are tempted by material possessions and worldly pleasures. You can either:

choices.text: Focus on spiritual growth and detachment from material things.
Indulge in worldly pleasures and seek material possessions.

blocks.why: Focusing on detachment aligns with the lesson's emphasis on detaching from Maya and seeking the Guru.

blocks.question: What happens without the Lord's Name?

blocks.text: Detachment from Maya and seeking the Guru leads to salvation.
Renounce Maya and join the Society of the Saints. See the Lord in all. Drink in the Ambrosial Nectar by the Grace of the Saints.
Those attached to Maya remain unfulfilled.  See the Lord in everything, knowing the priceless jewel is within.  The Ambrosial Nectar is obtained by Grace.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling disconnected from others and the world around you. You can either:

choices.text: Seek connection with others and recognize the divine in all beings.
Isolate yourself and focus on your own needs and desires.

blocks.why: Seeking connection and recognizing the divine aligns with the lesson's emphasis on oneness and the Society of Saints.

blocks.question: What should we see in all?

blocks.text: Recognizing the Lord in all and seeking the Society of Saints brings grace.
This pauri speaks of devotion. It says that those who sing God's praises with joy are protected.

God knows all and is always with devotees. Those who joyfully sing God's praises are blessed, and the Messenger of Death does not approach them. By blessing us with His Name, God purifies us and links us to His service.

blocks.scenario: You feel down and disconnected. You could:

choices.text: Sing or listen to devotional music.
Isolate yourself and dwell on negative thoughts.

blocks.why: Singing God's praises is said to bring joy and protection, aligning with the tags of devotion and Naam.

blocks.question: According to this pauri, what happens to those who sing God's praises with joy?
blocks.answer: The Messenger of Death does not approach them.

blocks.text: Singing praises can bring us closer to the Divine.
This pauri focuses on the transformative power of the Divine Name and the company of the holy. It emphasizes awakening and being saved through mercy.

The unstruck sound current vibrates, and humble servants sing God's praises with love. Through destiny and the company of the holy, aversion is gone, and the mind is imbued with love. The Merciful Lord saves us, even without our own merit, lifting us from suffering.

blocks.scenario: You feel lost and disconnected from your purpose. You could:

choices.text: Join a community gathering focused on spiritual growth and support.
Continue isolating yourself, feeling hopeless about finding direction.

blocks.why: Joining a holy company (sangat) aligns with the pauri's emphasis on the transformative power of community and divine mercy (kirpa).

blocks.question: According to this pauri, what happens in the Saadh Sangat, the Company of the Holy?
blocks.answer: Aversion is gone, and the mind and body are imbued with love for the Lord.

blocks.text: The company of the holy and the Lord's mercy can bring awakening and save us from suffering.
This pauri contrasts the joy of listening to God's praises with the allure of Maya. It questions why one would choose the crooked path of worldly enticements.

Listening to His Praises brings joy, and singing them leads to the supreme status. However, some are enticed by Maya, giving up jewels for shells and taking the crooked path. The pauri asks if such unfortunate people have no shame, forgetting the ocean of peace within.

blocks.scenario: You are tempted to spend money on something unnecessary, even though you have important bills to pay. You could:

choices.text: Resist the impulse and focus on your responsibilities.
Give in to the temptation and worry about the consequences later.

blocks.why: Resisting the temptation aligns with the pauri's message of avoiding the crooked path of Maya and remembering the ocean of peace (Naam).

blocks.question: According to this pauri, what happens when one listens to God's praises?
blocks.answer: Joy wells up within the mind.

blocks.text: Remembering the Divine can help us resist the allure of Maya and stay on the right path.
This pauri describes the state of those attached to Maya and ego. It highlights the contrast between worldly desires and the love of the Divine.

To those attached to Maya, nectar seems bitter, and poison is sweet. They are fond of falsehood and egotism, feeling stung by the Naam. They yearn for Maya but do not love the fearless, formless Giver. Only through God's Mercy are they saved from entanglement.

blocks.scenario: You find yourself constantly comparing yourself to others and feeling envious. You could:

choices.text: Focus on gratitude for what you have and appreciate the unique qualities of others.
Continue dwelling on what you lack and feeling resentful of others' success.

blocks.why: Focusing on gratitude aligns with the pauri's message of detaching from Maya and ego, and recognizing God's mercy (kirpa).

blocks.question: According to this pauri, what happens when someone attached to Maya hears the Naam?
blocks.answer: They feel like they have been stung by a scorpion.

blocks.text: Detachment from Maya and ego, along with God's mercy, can lead to true contentment.
This pauri emphasizes the benefits of chanting the Lord's Name and seeking the company of those who know God. It contrasts this with the futility of worldly efforts.
Chanting the Lord's Name brings bliss and freedom from ego. Seek those who know God and meditate on the Lord. Worldly calculations are useless; only love of God can carry you across the world-ocean.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling anxious about the future and trying to plan every detail. You could:

choices.text: Focus on the present moment and trust in the Divine.
Continue obsessively planning and worrying about what might happen.

blocks.why: Trusting in the Divine aligns with the pauri's message that worldly efforts are limited and that love of God (Naam) is the true path.

blocks.question: According to this pauri, what is the result of chanting the Lord's Name?
blocks.answer: It brings bliss and freedom from ego.

blocks.text: Love of God is the true path to cross the world-ocean.
This pauri speaks of the limitations of outward cleansing and the increase of duality through egotism. It emphasizes the medicine of the Name and seeking refuge in the Guru.

Merely washing the body does not remove inner filth; egotism only increases duality. Taking the medicine of the Name eradicates all diseases. Seek refuge in the Guru, who is your protection, and become the dust of the feet of His slaves.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling judgmental towards others and focusing on their flaws. You could:

choices.text: Turn your attention inward and focus on your own shortcomings.
Continue criticizing others and feeling superior.

blocks.why: Turning inward aligns with the pauri's message of overcoming ego and duality, and seeking refuge in the Guru.

blocks.question: According to this pauri, what happens when one takes the medicine of the Name?

blocks.text: The medicine of the Name and refuge in the Guru can help us overcome ego and duality.
This pauri describes the power of the Divine Name to carry us across and the importance of love for the Lord's lotus feet. It speaks of fearlessness and the pure lifestyle of the Guru.

The Name is the boat to carry us across, and the mind grasps only Your protection. Chanting Your Name brings life, and pain and darkness disappear. Love for the Lord's feet is enshrined, fear runs away, and the Guru's lifestyle is pure.

blocks.scenario: You are facing a difficult challenge and feeling overwhelmed with fear. You could:

choices.text: Focus on chanting or meditating on the Divine Name.
Give in to fear and avoid the challenge.

blocks.why: Chanting the Divine Name aligns with the pauri's message that it brings life, removes fear, and provides protection.

blocks.question: According to this pauri, what happens when one chants and meditates on the Divine Name?
blocks.answer: Pain and darkness disappear from the mind.

blocks.text: The Divine Name is a source of protection, fearlessness, and love.
This pauri describes the Naam as a precious jewel that brings truth, contentment, and spiritual wisdom. It speaks of the inexhaustible treasure entrusted to devotees.

The Naam is a jewel that brings truth, contentment, and spiritual wisdom. The Lord entrusts treasures of peace and kindness to devotees. This treasure is inexhaustible, never running out, and devotees look beautiful in the Court of the Lord.

blocks.scenario: You are constantly seeking external validation and material possessions to feel happy. You could:

choices.text: Focus on cultivating inner peace and contentment through spiritual practice.
Continue chasing external things, believing they will bring lasting happiness.

blocks.why: Cultivating inner peace aligns with the pauri's message that the Naam brings contentment and spiritual wisdom, an inexhaustible treasure.

blocks.question: According to this pauri, what does the Naam bring?

blocks.text: The Naam is an inexhaustible treasure that brings true contentment and spiritual wisdom.
The Lord's Kirtan is a priceless diamond, an ocean of bliss. The Guru's Bani holds the wealth of the unstruck sound current. Saints hold the key to this treasure.
Singing praises and connecting with the Divine brings immense joy and virtue. The Guru's teachings contain a profound inner peace. Those who are devoted have access to this inner peace.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling overwhelmed by daily life and its challenges. You want to find a sense of peace and joy.

choices.text: Listen to or participate in devotional music and reflect on the Guru's teachings.
Focus on your worries and try to solve them through intense planning.

blocks.why: This pauri connects devotional music and the Guru's teachings to inner peace and bliss, aligning with the tags 'naam,' 'devotion,' and 'peace.'

blocks.question: According to this passage, what is the Kirtan of the Lord's Praise?
blocks.answer: A priceless diamond and an ocean of bliss and virtue.

blocks.text: Devotion and reflection can bring inner peace.
The Vedas, Brahma, and even incarnations do not know God's greatness or limits. Only He Himself knows His own state. Others speak of Him only by hearsay.
The Divine is beyond complete understanding by any being. Our knowledge of the Divine is limited. The Divine's true nature is known only to itself.

blocks.scenario: You are discussing the nature of the Divine with a friend, and they express certainty about their understanding.

choices.text: Acknowledge that the Divine is beyond complete understanding and that our knowledge is limited.
Argue that your understanding is more accurate based on your personal beliefs.

blocks.why: This pauri emphasizes the limitations of human understanding regarding the Divine, aligning with the tags 'oneness,' 'hukam,' and 'spiritual_wisdom.'

blocks.question: According to this passage, who knows God's own state?

blocks.text: The Divine is beyond complete human understanding.
The Creator Lord plays His own plays, separating and uniting. Some wander, others are linked to devotion. Saints speak only of what they see; God is all-in-all.
The Divine orchestrates all events, both separation and union. Some are drawn to devotion, while others remain lost. The Divine is beyond virtue and vice.

blocks.scenario: You observe different people following various paths in life, some seemingly lost and others deeply devoted.

choices.text: Recognize that the Divine guides each person's journey, whether through wandering or devotion.
Judge those who seem lost and praise those who are devoted.

blocks.why: This pauri describes the Divine's role in guiding different paths, aligning with the tags 'oneness,' 'devotion,' and 'truth.'

blocks.question: According to this passage, what do the Saints speak of?
blocks.answer: Only of what they see with their eyes.

blocks.text: The Divine guides all paths.
O Beloved God, I am Yours. Your Name is the support of my mind. Hearing Your Name, I live; it is my mind's consolation. Your Name destroys sins.
The Divine's Name provides strength and comfort. Remembering the Divine brings life and peace. The Divine's Name has the power to purify.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling weak and discouraged.

choices.text: Remember the Divine's Name as a source of strength and comfort.
Rely solely on your own willpower and ignore any spiritual support.

blocks.why: This pauri emphasizes the power of the Divine's Name to provide support and consolation, aligning with the tags 'naam,' 'devotion,' and 'grace.'

blocks.question: According to this passage, what is the support of the mind?

blocks.text: The Divine's Name is a source of strength.
All creation rests its hopes in You. All worship and adore You. Nanak is a sacrifice to You, O infinite Lord.
All beings depend on the Divine. The Divine is worthy of all praise and adoration. Surrender to the Divine is a path to connection.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling anxious about the future and uncertain about your path.

choices.text: Place your trust in the Divine and recognize that all beings depend on the Divine's grace.
Try to control every aspect of your future and rely solely on your own efforts.

blocks.why: This pauri emphasizes reliance on the Divine and the importance of worship and adoration, aligning with the tags 'kirpa,' 'devotion,' and 'oneness.'

blocks.question: According to this passage, where does all creation rest its hopes?

blocks.text: Trust in the Divine.
My mind has grasped His Support, and my bonds are shattered. I meditate on the Lord, the embodiment of bliss. The Lord's Sanctuary is the boat to carry us across.
Finding support in the Divine leads to freedom from limitations. Meditating on the Divine brings supreme joy. The Divine is a refuge and a means of crossing over difficulties.

blocks.scenario: You are facing a difficult challenge and feeling trapped by your circumstances.

choices.text: Seek refuge in the Divine and meditate on the Divine's name for support and guidance.
Isolate yourself and try to solve the problem on your own without seeking any external support.

blocks.why: This pauri connects finding support in the Divine with freedom and inner peace, aligning with the tags 'naam,' 'peace,' and 'devotion.'

blocks.question: According to this passage, what is the Lord's Sanctuary?
blocks.answer: The boat to carry us across.

blocks.text: Find support in the Divine.
Abandon clever tricks, become His servant, and erase self-conceit. Be aware with your Guru. Do not think God and Guru are separate.
Humility and service are important. Erasing ego and connecting with the Guru leads to fulfillment. The Guru is a manifestation of the Divine.

blocks.scenario: You are tempted to take credit for a successful project, even though others contributed significantly.

choices.text: Acknowledge the contributions of others and remain humble.
Take all the credit for yourself to enhance your reputation.

blocks.why: This pauri emphasizes humility, service, and erasing self-conceit, aligning with the tags 'haumai,' 'seva,' and 'guru.'

blocks.question: According to this passage, what should you erase?

blocks.text: Practice humility and service.
Hold tight to the Guru, give up other hopes, and ask for the treasure of the Name. Accept what happens as good and sing the Lord's praises.
The Guru is a source of support and guidance. The Divine Name is a valuable treasure. Accepting the Divine's will and praising the Divine is the purpose of life.

blocks.scenario: You experience an unexpected setback in your plans.

choices.text: Accept the setback as part of the Divine's plan and continue to praise the Divine.
Become angry and resentful, blaming others for your misfortune.

blocks.why: This pauri emphasizes reliance on the Guru, the importance of the Divine Name, and accepting the Divine's will, aligning with the tags 'guru,' 'naam,' and 'devotion.'

blocks.question: According to this passage, what should you ask for?
blocks.answer: The treasure of the Name of the Lord.

blocks.text: Accept the Divine's will.
Meditate on the Lord and renounce cleverness. Bow down to the Guru's feet, placing your hopes in the One Lord.
By chanting the Guru's mantra and the Lord's name, one can find bliss. The Lord is a great giver with endless treasures. Bowing to the Guru can lead to salvation.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling overwhelmed by complex problems at work. Should you:

choices.text: Take a moment to meditate and remember the Guru.
Rely solely on your own skills and strategies.

blocks.why: Meditating on the Lord and remembering the Guru can help one renounce cleverness and find inner peace, aligning with the lesson's tags of 'naam', 'devotion', and 'guru'.

blocks.question: According to this passage, what should we renounce?

blocks.text: Remembering the Divine can bring inner peace.
Sing the Lord's praises and make this life fruitful. Chanting the immaculate Name leads to emancipation.
By singing praises and chanting the Lord's name, one can obtain honor and glory. This treasure is obtained only by His Grace. He will save you at the very last moment.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling anxious about an upcoming important event. Should you:

choices.text: Sing praises and remember the Lord.
Focus only on the potential negative outcomes.

blocks.why: Singing praises and remembering the Lord can bring honor, glory, and a sense of being saved, aligning with the lesson's tags of 'grace', 'naam', and 'devotion'.

blocks.question: According to this passage, how is this treasure obtained?

blocks.text: Remembering the Divine can bring honor and glory.
Meditate on the Lord while standing and sitting. Listen to the Guru's teachings.
Meditating on the Lord and listening to the Guru can bring peace. All enemies become friends, and consciousness becomes pure. You shall be absorbed in celestial peace.

blocks.scenario: You are experiencing conflict with a neighbor. Should you:

choices.text: Meditate on the Lord and listen to wise counsel.
Escalate the conflict and assert your dominance.

blocks.why: Meditating on the Lord and listening to wise counsel can help turn enemies into friends and bring peace, aligning with the lesson's tags of 'naam', 'peace', and 'guru'.

blocks.question: According to this passage, what happens to enemies when you meditate on the Lord?

blocks.text: Remembering the Divine can bring peace and harmony.
Honor the One to whom everything belongs and leave egotistical pride behind. Accept whatever the Lord has done as good.
Without the Naam, nothing is of any use. By Guru's Grace, the Lord comes to dwell in the mind. Accepting the Lord's will brings sweetness.

blocks.scenario: You experience a setback in your personal goals. Should you:

choices.text: Accept it as the Lord's will and seek guidance.
Become consumed by anger and resentment.

blocks.why: Accepting the Lord's will and seeking guidance can help one leave egotistical pride behind and find peace, aligning with the lesson's tags of 'ego', 'naam', and 'hukam'.

blocks.question: According to this passage, what should we leave behind?

blocks.text: Accepting the Divine will can bring inner peace.
Meditate on Him twenty-four hours a day. Sing the Glorious Praises of the Lord in the Saadh Sangat.
Meditating on the Lord dispels pain and makes your face radiant. Even the sinking iron is saved in the Saadh Sangat, as His Grace is received. All fears and terrors are taken away.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling isolated and fearful. Should you:

choices.text: Meditate on the Lord and seek the company of the holy (Sangat).
Withdraw further into isolation and dwell on your fears.

blocks.why: Meditating on the Lord and seeking the company of the holy can dispel pain, remove fears, and bring grace, aligning with the lesson's tags of 'naam', 'sangat', and 'grace'.

blocks.question: According to this passage, what is saved in the Saadh Sangat?

blocks.text: Remembering the Divine and seeking holy company can bring peace and grace.
Service to the Divine Guru is fruitful. Continually serve Him.
Meditating on Him and continually serving Him brings truth, intuition, and peace. He is the Doer, the Cause of causes, and the Saving Grace.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling lost and uncertain about your path. Should you:

choices.text: Serve others and remember the Divine.
Focus solely on your own desires and ambitions.

blocks.why: Serving others and remembering the Divine can bring truth, intuition, and peace, aligning with the lesson's tags of 'seva', 'truth', and 'peace'.

blocks.question: According to this passage, what does service to the Divine Guru bring?

blocks.text: Serving the Divine and others can bring inner peace and clarity.
Reliance on mortal man is useless; the Lord is your only support. Meditate on the Name of the Lord alone.
Discard all other hopes and rely on the Lord. Meditating on the Name resolves all affairs. The Lord is the treasure of virtue.

blocks.scenario: You are facing a difficult challenge and feel tempted to rely on others for help. Should you:

choices.text: Rely on the Lord and meditate on the Name.
Place all your hopes on others.

blocks.why: Relying on the Lord and meditating on the Name can resolve affairs and bring virtue, aligning with the lesson's tags of 'naam', 'devotion', and 'reliance'.

blocks.question: According to this passage, what is useless?

blocks.text: Relying on the Divine can bring strength and resolve.
Be the dust of all men's feet and eradicate self-conceit. Meditate on the Naam, night and day.
Meditating on the Lord reveals His form. Remembering the Lord in meditation obtains the treasure. This is the most rewarding activity.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling proud of your accomplishments. Should you:

choices.text: Be humble and remember the Divine.
Brag about your achievements.

blocks.why: Being humble and remembering the Divine can help eradicate self-conceit and obtain the treasure, aligning with the lesson's tags of 'naam', 'humility', and 'detachment'.

blocks.question: According to this passage, what should we eradicate?

blocks.text: Practicing humility and remembering the Divine can bring inner peace and reward.
Reflect on the bountiful and merciful Lord, the cause of all causes. Remember the Lord, the destroyer of fear, who is unseen and infinite. Humbly invoke the Universal Lord God, who is all-pervading.

The Lord is the doer of everything, cherishing all beings with mercy. God is beyond our sight and understanding, yet great and endless. By praying, we connect with the Lord of the World, who is everywhere.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling anxious about an upcoming presentation. Do you:

choices.text: Remember the Lord as the destroyer of fear and the cause of all causes.
Focus only on memorizing your notes and ignore your anxiety.

blocks.why: Remembering the Lord can bring peace and courage, aligning with the tags of fearlessness and oneness.

blocks.question: According to the lesson, what qualities does the Lord possess?
blocks.answer: Bountiful, merciful, unseen, infinite, all-pervading, and destroyer of fear.

blocks.text: Remembering the Lord can help us face challenges with courage and compassion.
Reflect on the One and only merciful Master, the Dispenser of justice. Remember the Lord, powerful and merciful, the support of every heart. Pray for kindness and devotion.

The Lord is the ultimate source of mercy and justice, present in every heart. The luminous Lord is everywhere, though His ways are beyond our understanding. We should seek devotion and meditate on the Creator.

blocks.scenario: You see someone struggling to carry groceries. Do you:

choices.text: Offer to help, remembering the Lord's compassion.
Continue walking, assuming someone else will help.

blocks.why: Offering help reflects compassion, aligning with the lesson's emphasis on the merciful Master.

blocks.question: What does the lesson say about the nature of the Lord?
blocks.answer: Powerful, merciful, all-pervading, and the support of every heart.

blocks.text: Seeking devotion and acting with compassion connects us to the Divine.
Meditate on the Lord, Har, Har, and sing the praises of the Lord of the World. When the Lord's lotus feet are enshrined in the mind, sins are eradicated. Serve God night and day.
By meditating on the Lord, pain will not afflict you. Singing praises merges one's light into the Light. Serving God quenches hunger and thirst, and is a sign of meeting the Lord.

blocks.scenario: You feel restless and unfulfilled. Do you:

choices.text: Engage in selfless service and meditate on the Lord's name.
Seek distractions through entertainment and material possessions.

blocks.why: Selfless service and meditation align with the lesson's emphasis on seva and naam, leading to fulfillment.

blocks.question: What are the benefits of meditating on the Lord?
blocks.answer: Eradication of sins, freedom from pain, and quenching of hunger and thirst.

blocks.text: Serving God and meditating on the Lord's name brings inner peace and fulfillment.
When God becomes merciful, worldly entanglements end. Gazing upon the Guru's Darshan brings joy. Sing the praises of the Lord and focus your heart's meditation on the Lord's lotus feet.

God's mercy frees us from worldly attachments. The Guru's vision brings rapture, activating our pre-destined karma. The Saints are accepted by the Lord, and the dust of their feet brings supreme status.

blocks.scenario: You feel stuck in a difficult situation. Do you:

choices.text: Pray for God's mercy and seek guidance from the Guru.
Try to solve the problem on your own without seeking help.

blocks.why: Praying for mercy and seeking guidance aligns with the lesson's emphasis on kirpa and the Guru.

blocks.question: What brings an end to worldly entanglements?

blocks.text: Seeking God's mercy and the Guru's guidance can help us overcome challenges.
Chant the Name of the Lord and accept the Word of the Guru's Shabad as Truth. Sing the Glorious Praises of the Lord and know that the Lord is close at hand. Meditate on the Lord of the Universe.
Chanting the Name eradicates egotistical pride. Devotion to the Guru involves singing praises of the Lord. Accepting the Shabad brings contentment, and meditating on the Lord covers all faults.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling stressed and overwhelmed. Do you:

choices.text: Find a quiet place to meditate and chant the Lord's name.
Continue working without taking a break.

blocks.why: Meditation and chanting align with the lesson's emphasis on naam and shabad, bringing peace and contentment.

blocks.question: What does accepting the Guru's Shabad bring?

blocks.text: Chanting the Lord's name and accepting the Guru's Shabad brings peace and covers our faults.
Remember that the Guru is the Supreme Lord God. Attach your mind to the Guru's feet. In the Saadh Sangat, the Company of the Holy, love Him in your mind. Serve that home, which will save you.

The Guru is the Great Giver, merciful and forgiving. One whose mind is attached to the Guru's feet is blessed with perfect destiny. The Lord is our only true companion, and loving Him in the Sangat brings salvation.

blocks.scenario: You feel lonely and disconnected. Do you:

choices.text: Seek the company of the holy (Sangat) and remember the Lord.
Isolate yourself and avoid social interaction.

blocks.why: Seeking the Sangat and remembering the Lord aligns with the lesson's emphasis on love and the Guru.

blocks.question: According to the lesson, who is our true companion?

blocks.text: Attaching our mind to the Guru and loving the Lord in the Sangat brings perfect destiny.
Recognize that life is passing away in egotism and conflict. You cannot cross over the sea of Maya. There is none other than the Lord to save you. Grasp the Sanctuary of the Lord.
Egotism and sin lead to suffering and dissatisfaction. Only the Lord can save us from the impassable sea of Maya. Salvation comes through God's Grace. The Lord's Name purifies sinners.

blocks.scenario: You are tempted to act selfishly for personal gain. Do you:

choices.text: Remember that life is passing away in egotism and seek God's grace.
Give in to the temptation and prioritize your own desires.

blocks.why: Remembering the transient nature of life and seeking God's grace aligns with the lesson's emphasis on haumai and grace.

blocks.question: What can save us from the sea of Maya?

blocks.text: Seeking God's Grace and grasping His Sanctuary can save us from egotism and Maya.

Find peace in this world through friendship with the Saints. The Lord has blessed me with His Name. Attach your consciousness to the Guru's feet and apply the dust of the Saints' feet to your forehead.
Friendship with the Saints brings peace and respect in the Court of the Lord. The Lord's Name fulfills our pre-ordained destiny. Applying the dust of the Saints' feet eradicates sins and pains.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling troubled and restless. Do you:

choices.text: Seek the company of the Saints and remember the Lord's Name.
Withdraw from others and dwell on your troubles.

blocks.why: Seeking the company of the Saints and remembering the Lord's Name aligns with the lesson's emphasis on peace and sangat.

blocks.question: What brings peace in this world?

blocks.text: Friendship with the Saints and remembering the Lord's Name brings peace and eradicates sins.
This lesson focuses on the importance of service and remembering God. When we engage in true service, we purify our minds. God's Name dwells within every heart.
Performing true service brings about a vision of the Lord. Troubles and sufferings are removed, and we merge with our origin. God is seen as perfect and forgiving.

blocks.scenario: A friend is feeling overwhelmed by challenges. You offer to help them with a task and remind them to find peace through prayer.

choices.text: Help your friend and encourage them to remember God's presence.
Tell your friend that everyone faces challenges and they should deal with it themselves.

blocks.why: This reflects true service and recognizing God's presence, aligning with the tags of seva, naam, and compassion.

blocks.question: According to this passage, where does God's Name reside?

blocks.text: True service and remembering God can bring peace and resolution to suffering.
This lesson explores the boundless mercy and virtues of God. The Guru's grace can transform the impossible into reality. Through devotion, one can be linked to service.
God is a treasure of mercy, with countless virtues beyond description. The Guru's power can bring forth new life and extinguish negativity. The Guru connects devotees to service.

blocks.scenario: You feel overwhelmed by a difficult situation. You remember the Guru's teachings and decide to approach the problem with faith and devotion.

choices.text: Trust in the Guru's guidance and approach the situation with devotion.
Give up and assume that nothing can be done.

blocks.why: This reflects the importance of kirpa, guru, and devotion in overcoming challenges.

blocks.question: What is the Guru described as putting out?

blocks.text: With devotion and the Guru's grace, even the most difficult situations can be transformed.
This lesson highlights God's boundless compassion and the importance of the Saadh Sangat. Even the ungrateful are saved through His mercy. In the company of the holy, fear vanishes.
God's compassion extends to all, even those who may not deserve it. The Saadh Sangat provides a space where the fear of reincarnation disappears. God is forever forgiving and protects devotees.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling anxious about the future. You decide to spend time with a group of spiritual people and focus on remembering God.

choices.text: Seek the company of the holy and meditate on God to overcome your fear.
Isolate yourself and worry about the future alone.

blocks.why: This reflects the importance of compassion, sangat, and fearlessness in finding peace.

blocks.question: What disappears in the Saadh Sangat?

blocks.text: Finding solace in the Saadh Sangat and remembering God can bring fearlessness and peace.
This lesson explores the path to peace through devotion and grace. By connecting with loving worship, one can experience peace. Surrender to His will, and sing His praises.

Through devotion, sins are burned away, and bliss becomes manifest. Crossing the world-ocean becomes easy through His grace. Vice and virtue are not in our control, but singing His praises brings us closer.

blocks.scenario: You are struggling with feelings of guilt and regret. You decide to focus on devotion and singing praises to find inner peace.

choices.text: Turn to devotion and praise to find peace and release from guilt.
Dwell on your mistakes and allow them to consume you.

blocks.why: This reflects the importance of peace, devotion, and grace in overcoming negative emotions.

blocks.question: What happens when one is linked to loving devotional worship?

blocks.text: Devotion and singing praises can lead to inner peace and a release from suffering.
This lesson warns against attachment to Maya and emphasizes seeking refuge in the Lord. Entanglement in fraud leads to regret. True wealth is found through the Gurmukh.

Our bodies and minds are not truly our own, and attachment to Maya leads to deception. Worldly affairs remain unresolved, and desires bring regret. Seeking the Lord's refuge and becoming a Gurmukh leads to true wealth.

blocks.scenario: You are tempted to pursue material possessions at the expense of your spiritual well-being. You remember the teachings and choose to focus on seeking the Lord's refuge.

choices.text: Focus on spiritual growth and seek the Lord's refuge.
Prioritize material possessions and ignore your spiritual needs.

blocks.why: This reflects the importance of detaching from Maya and seeking true wealth through the Gurmukh.

blocks.question: What will catch you in its noose?

blocks.text: Detachment from Maya and seeking the Lord's refuge can lead to true wealth and fulfillment.
This lesson warns against the pain of greed and emphasizes the importance of God's mercy. When the Lord is merciful, we are attached to His robe. Seeking His sanctuary brings fearlessness.

Practicing deception and forgetting the giver of life leads to the pain of greed. When the Supreme Lord is merciful, we are drawn closer to Him. Merging with the Truest of the True brings fearlessness.

blocks.scenario: You are tempted to cheat someone for personal gain. You remember the teachings and choose to act with honesty and integrity.

choices.text: Act with honesty and integrity, trusting in God's mercy.
Cheat the person for personal gain, ignoring the consequences.

blocks.why: This reflects the importance of overcoming greed and seeking fearlessness through God's kirpa.

blocks.question: What never leaves you?

blocks.text: Overcoming greed and seeking God's mercy can lead to fearlessness and true fulfillment.
This lesson emphasizes the importance of the Guru and His grace in dispelling fear. When the Lord abides in the mind, all affairs are resolved. Being blessed by His mercy leads to liberation.

When the Lord resides in the mind, one does not see the world-ocean as impassible. The Guru's hand dispels the fear of birth and death. Those blessed by His mercy cross over the terrifying world-ocean.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling anxious about a difficult decision. You remember the Guru's teachings and seek guidance through prayer and reflection.

choices.text: Seek the Guru's guidance and trust in His grace to overcome your fear.
Make the decision impulsively without seeking guidance.

blocks.why: This reflects the importance of the Guru, kirpa, and overcoming fear through faith.

blocks.question: What is dispelled when the Guru places His hand on your forehead?
blocks.answer: The fear of birth and death.

blocks.text: Seeking the Guru's guidance and trusting in His grace can dispel fear and lead to liberation.
This lesson encourages drinking in the Ambrosial Nectar and abandoning corruption. Meditate on the Lord to cross over. His devotees never forget Him.
By embracing the Lord's teachings and abandoning corruption, one's face becomes radiant. The Lord's power is such that the impossible becomes possible. His devotees constantly remember Him.

blocks.scenario: You are tempted to engage in dishonest behavior. You remember the teachings and choose to act with integrity and meditate on the Lord.

choices.text: Act with integrity and meditate on the Lord.
Engage in dishonest behavior for personal gain.

blocks.why: This reflects the importance of naam, devotion, and detachment from corruption.

blocks.question: What should you abandon?

blocks.text: Meditating on the Lord and abandoning corruption can lead to a radiant life.
This passage speaks of joining the society of saints and chanting the Lord's name. It emphasizes contemplating and meditating on God.
The verses use analogies to illustrate spiritual concepts. Ultimately, the passage encourages joining the Society of Saints and remembering God, as this is how one attains the supreme status.

blocks.scenario: You feel lost and disconnected. Do you:

choices.text: Seek out a community of like-minded people and engage in prayer or meditation.
Isolate yourself and try to solve your problems alone.

blocks.why: Joining a community and remembering God can provide guidance and support, aligning with the tags of sangat, naam, and remembrance.

blocks.question: According to this passage, what practice helps one attain the supreme status?
blocks.answer: Contemplating and meditating on God within the Society of Saints.

blocks.text: Remembering God in the company of others can lead to spiritual growth.
This passage discusses the will of God, the consequences of actions, and the illusion of attachment. It reminds us that worldly possessions will not accompany us in the end.
The verses highlight that whatever pleases God happens, and we should seek His sanctuary. Attachment to worldly things is an illusion, and negative actions lead to negative consequences.

blocks.text: Strive to be truthful and compassionate in your words and actions, seeking the Guru's guidance.

This passage emphasizes the importance of the Society of Saints and the perfection of the Guru. It speaks of obtaining eternal peace in His Sanctuary.

This passage speaks of the peace that comes from longing for the Naam and the dispelling of pains through remembrance. It emphasizes the role of the Perfect Guru in eradicating anxiety.

The verses highlight that one who feels hunger for the Naam sleeps in peace. Meditating on the Lord dispels all pains, and the Perfect Guru removes all anxiety. The passage encourages constant remembrance of God.

blocks.scenario: You are having trouble sleeping due to worries. Do you:

choices.text: Engage in prayer or meditation, focusing on the Divine Name.

blocks.why: Remembering the Divine Name (naam) is said to bring peace and dispel worries, aligning with the tags of peace and guru.

blocks.question: According to this passage, what sleeps in peace?
blocks.answer: One who feels hunger for the Naam.

blocks.text: Find peace and comfort by longing for the Naam and remembering God.
This passage speaks of the permeation of the One Creator Lord throughout all creation. It emphasizes the depth and profundity of the Naam.

blocks.answer: The One, the One and Only Creator Lord.

blocks.text: Remember the presence of the Creator in all things and the depth of the Naam.
This lesson discusses detachment from worldly pleasures. It reminds us that beauty, treasures, and relationships are temporary.

We are asked to abandon attachment to beauty, pleasures, and material possessions, as these are part of Maya. Even the riches that delight our minds and our relationships will not go with us in the end. Finding peace comes from seeking sanctuary in faith.

choices.text: Acknowledge the excitement but remember that true peace comes from faith, not material possessions.

blocks.why: This choice reflects detachment from Maya and aligns with the lesson's tags of 'maya' and 'detachment'.

blocks.text: True and lasting peace comes from faith, not from worldly possessions or relationships.
This lesson emphasizes the importance of remembering the Lord's Name. It highlights the benefits of devotion and singing praises.

Taking support of the Lord's Name dispels evil-mindedness and leads to a state of peace. Singing praises is fortunate, washing away sins and leading to a heavenly realm. Even at the last moment, awareness of the Lord can bring about a desired state.

The mind is often entangled in Maya, lacking spiritual wisdom. The way to adopt is one that dispels evil-mindedness and vibrates in devotional worship. The Lord bestows the gift of fearlessness.

This lesson focuses on the importance of compassion and remembering God's praises. It reminds us that life is fleeting.

Singing the Kirtan of God's Praises is equivalent to performing all religious rituals. Enshrining the Lord's Name in your heart, even for an instant, eradicates the fear of death. Focus your thoughts on the Lord, as life is constantly passing.

blocks.question: What fear is eradicated by enshrining the Lord's Name in your heart?

blocks.text: Remembering God's praises and acting with compassion can help us make the most of our fleeting lives.
This lesson discusses the dangers of being intoxicated with Maya and forgetting the Lord. It emphasizes the importance of remembrance and detachment.

Youth wasted in corrupt pleasures and childhood in ignorance leads to entanglement in evil-mindedness. We should not forget the Lord who blessed us with human life. Maya will not go along with us, so we should remember the Lord, the fulfiller of desires.

Despite the changing times, the moon, stars, sun, earth, and wind remain the same. We are encouraged to give up attachment to life. Tyranny is a sign of Kali Yuga, which is not confined to any specific place.

blocks.why: This choice reflects 'detachment' and aligns with the lesson's message of maintaining inner peace amidst the challenges of Kali Yuga.

blocks.question: What are we encouraged to give up?

blocks.text: Detachment and inner integrity can help us navigate the challenges of any age.

In Kali Yuga, practicing truth may lead to frustration, and chanting the Lord's Name may be met with scorn. The justice of previous ages is gone, and virtue is only obtained if the Lord bestows it. Chant the praises of the Lord.

blocks.why: Focusing on the Shabad and detachment aligns with the lesson's emphasis on overcoming negative influences through the divine word.

It suggests that all are in the One, and the One is in all, as shown by the True Guru. This emphasizes the interconnectedness of all beings.

blocks.question: According to this passage, what has the True Guru shown us?

blocks.text: Strive to see the Divine in all beings and cultivate a sense of unity and connection.
This passage states that the Creator of the universe cannot be fully known. It speaks of the Divine Light illuminating the three worlds.
It suggests that the Guru is attuned to the Fearless Lord. This emphasizes the importance of inner illumination and connection to the Divine.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling lost and uncertain about your path in life. You are searching for guidance and meaning.

blocks.text: Trust in your inner wisdom and connect with the Divine Light within.
This passage describes the Guru as a detached Yogi who entices the hearts of all. It speaks of finding emancipation in God's Sanctuary.
It suggests that the True Guru becomes our true help and support. The Divine power is infused into the earth and the sky.
