This lesson highlights the importance of 'Saadh Sangat' (holy congregation) and attuning oneself to 'Naam'. It emphasizes that joining the company of the holy leads to salvation and is a gift of grace.

The verses express devotion to the Saadh Sangat, stating that joining them leads to being saved. It also emphasizes being attuned to the Divine Name with both mind and body. This is seen as a blessing from God.

blocks.scenario: You're feeling lost and disconnected. You can either A) attend a community gathering or B) isolate yourself at home.

choices.text: Attend a community gathering or religious service.
Isolate yourself at home and avoid social interaction.

blocks.why: Attending a community gathering aligns with the concept of 'Sangat,' finding support and connection, reflecting the tags of sangat and grace.

blocks.question: What happens when joining the Saadh Sangat?

blocks.text: Finding solace and guidance in the company of the holy can lead to salvation.
This lesson focuses on detaching from worldly entanglements and singing praises of the Lord. It emphasizes the all-powerful nature of God and seeking His Name as a blessing.

The verses encourage abandoning corruption and singing the Lord's praises. It acknowledges God's infinite power and limitless nature. Seeking the blessing of His Name is presented as a humble request.

blocks.scenario: You're caught up in material possessions. You can either A) donate some items or B) continue accumulating more.

choices.text: Donate some of your possessions to charity.
Continue to accumulate more material possessions.

blocks.why: Donating possessions aligns with detaching from worldly entanglements, connecting to the tags of detachment and oneness.

blocks.question: What should we abandon according to the verse?

blocks.text: Detaching from worldly things and praising the Divine can bring inner peace.
This lesson emphasizes seeking sanctuary in the Lord and recognizing His all-pervading presence. It highlights God as the friend of the meek and the ultimate reality.

The verses express surrendering to God and seeking refuge in Him. God is described as the friend of the humble and the lover of devotees. The verses affirm that God alone exists in the beginning, middle, and end, permeating all creation.

blocks.scenario: You're facing a difficult challenge. You can either A) seek inner strength through prayer or B) rely solely on your own abilities.

choices.text: Seek inner strength through prayer and meditation.
Rely solely on your own abilities to overcome the challenge.

blocks.why: Seeking inner strength through prayer aligns with seeking sanctuary in the Lord, connecting to the tags of devotion and grace.

blocks.question: Who is the friend of the meek?

blocks.text: Finding strength and solace in the Divine can help overcome life's challenges.
This lesson focuses on experiencing God through hearing, seeing, and singing His praises. It emphasizes the blessing of receiving the Divine Name and the beauty of the Lord's creation.

The verses describe hearing God's praises, beholding His vision, and singing His glories. It expresses gratitude for the blessing of the Divine Name. The verses also celebrate the beauty and sweetness of the Lord's presence in the world.

blocks.scenario: You're feeling disconnected from the Divine. You can either A) listen to devotional music or B) ignore your spiritual needs.

choices.text: Listen to devotional music or read scripture.
Ignore your spiritual needs and focus on other activities.

blocks.why: Listening to devotional music aligns with hearing God's praises, connecting to the tags of naam and devotion.

blocks.question: What do we do with our ears, eyes, and tongue?
blocks.answer: Hear God's praises, behold His vision, and sing His glories.

blocks.text: Engaging with the Divine through our senses can deepen our connection.
This lesson expresses gratitude for the Divine and the blessings in creation. It celebrates the Lord's presence and playfulness.

The verses express blessings for various aspects of the Divine and creation. It acknowledges the Lord's presence in different forms and celebrates His joyful play. The verses convey a sense of wonder and appreciation for the Divine.

blocks.scenario: You notice the beauty of nature. You can either A) appreciate the moment or B) ignore it and move on.

choices.text: Take a moment to appreciate the beauty of nature.
Ignore the beauty and continue with your activities.

blocks.why: Appreciating the beauty of nature aligns with expressing gratitude for the Divine, connecting to the tag of gratitude.

blocks.question: What is blessed in these verses?
blocks.answer: Various aspects of the Divine and creation.

blocks.text: Cultivating gratitude for the Divine and creation can enrich our lives.
This lesson highlights the Lord's grace and protection. It emphasizes seeking sanctuary in Him and remembering His acts of salvation.

The verses describe the Lord as a protector and savior. They recall instances where the Lord saved devotees in distress. Seeking sanctuary in the Lord is presented as a path to purification and grace.

blocks.scenario: You're facing a personal crisis. You can either A) turn to faith for support or B) feel hopeless and alone.

choices.text: Turn to your faith and seek spiritual support.
Feel hopeless and isolated in your crisis.

blocks.why: Turning to faith aligns with seeking sanctuary in the Lord, connecting to the tags of devotion and faith.

blocks.question: What did the Lord save the life of?

blocks.text: Trusting in the Divine can provide strength and guidance during difficult times.
This lesson focuses on recognizing the Lord's presence in all beings and detaching from worldly desires. It emphasizes remembering the One Infinite Lord and becoming dispassionate.

The verses affirm that the Lord speaks within all hearts and is present in all forms of life. It encourages remembering the One Lord and abandoning other hopes. The verses suggest that detachment leads to a state of dispassion and understanding.

blocks.scenario: You're feeling attached to a specific outcome. You can either A) accept whatever happens or B) try to control the situation.

choices.text: Accept whatever happens without trying to control the situation.
Try to control the situation to achieve your desired outcome.

blocks.why: Accepting whatever happens aligns with detaching from specific outcomes, connecting to the tags of detachment and oneness.

blocks.question: Who speaks within all hearts?

blocks.text: Recognizing the Divine in all and detaching from desires can lead to inner peace.
Let's explore a verse about devotion. It speaks of remaining the dust of the Divine's feet and seeking protection.

The verse expresses a desire to always be humble and close to the Divine. It also highlights seeking refuge and recognizing the Divine's presence. The mind, if not focused on the Divine Name, can be lost in doubt.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling overwhelmed by daily worries. Do you:

choices.text: Quietly reflect and try to connect with a sense of the Divine's presence.
Continue to worry without pause.

blocks.why: Reflecting connects to the idea of seeking protection and recognizing the Divine's presence, aligning with the tags of devotion and humility.

blocks.question: According to the verse, what is the state of a mind that has not found the Divine Name?

blocks.text: Even in moments of doubt, remember to seek the Divine's protection with humility.
This verse touches upon destiny and the balance between joy and pain. It also considers separation from and union with the Divine.

The verse suggests that life involves both pleasure and suffering, which are part of a pre-ordained destiny. Separation from the Divine is described as the ultimate separation. Union with the Divine is achieved through destiny and is something to praise.

blocks.scenario: You experience a setback after a period of success. Do you:

choices.text: Accept it as part of life's journey and maintain faith.
Become completely discouraged and lose hope.

blocks.why: Accepting setbacks aligns with the idea of pre-ordained destiny and maintaining faith, connecting to the tags of destiny and detachment.

blocks.question: According to the verse, what is the worst kind of separation?

blocks.text: Remember that both joy and pain are part of life's journey, and faith can help you navigate them.
This verse explores the nature of the mind and the importance of detachment. It reminds us that worldly possessions are temporary.

The verse speaks of the creation of the body and the inscription of destiny. It cautions against pride and attachment to worldly pleasures, as everything must eventually be left behind. Finding peace involves detaching from worldly tastes.

blocks.scenario: You are tempted to buy something you don't really need. Do you:

choices.text: Consider whether it aligns with your values and brings lasting peace.
Buy it without thinking.

blocks.why: Considering your values aligns with the idea of detaching from worldly tastes and finding intuitive peace, connecting to the tags of maya and detachment.

blocks.question: According to the verse, what happens when joining with Maya?

blocks.text: Strive for detachment from worldly pleasures and seek lasting peace within.
This verse discusses the consequences of sin and the importance of overcoming fear. It emphasizes the role of actions and the mind.

The verse describes how attachment to worldly things is ultimately futile when facing death. It compares sin to a stone that cannot float and suggests that the fear of God can be a boat to carry one across. Actions and thoughts shape our destiny.

blocks.scenario: You are tempted to act dishonestly to gain an advantage. Do you:

choices.text: Choose honesty, even if it means missing the opportunity.
Act dishonestly to get ahead.

blocks.why: Choosing honesty aligns with the idea of avoiding sin and using the 'boat' of fear to carry your soul across, connecting to the tags of fear and mind.

blocks.question: According to the verse, what is sin compared to?
blocks.answer: A stone which does not float.

blocks.text: Let the fear of God guide your actions and help you overcome temptation.
This verse explores the importance of remembering the Divine and avoiding attachment. It uses metaphors to describe the mind's struggles.

The verse emphasizes the importance of keeping the Divine in consciousness, as forgetting leads to the decay of virtues. It describes the world as full of traps and warns against being caught by them. The body and mind are compared to a furnace heated by desires and anxieties.

blocks.scenario: You find yourself constantly worrying about the future. Do you:

choices.text: Try to focus on the present moment and remember the Divine.
Continue to worry without pause.

blocks.why: Focusing on the present and remembering the Divine aligns with the idea of keeping Him in consciousness and avoiding the traps of the world, connecting to the tags of mind and attachment.

blocks.question: According to the verse, what happens to virtues when the Lord is forgotten?

blocks.text: Remember to keep the Divine in your consciousness and avoid being trapped by worldly anxieties.
This verse highlights the transformative power of the Guru and the importance of the Divine Name. It uses the lotus flower as a symbol of detachment.

The verse suggests that even something impure can be transformed through the Guru's guidance. The Divine Name is described as Ambrosial and capable of steadying the body. Like a lotus flower, one can remain untouched by the world's impurities.

blocks.scenario: You are surrounded by negativity. Do you:

choices.text: Seek guidance and focus on the Divine Name to remain unaffected.
Become consumed by the negativity.

blocks.why: Seeking guidance and focusing on the Divine Name aligns with the idea of transformation through the Guru and remaining untouched by pollution, connecting to the tags of guru and detachment.

blocks.question: According to the verse, what can transform something impure into gold?

blocks.text: Seek guidance and focus on the Divine Name to remain pure amidst the world's impurities.
This verse explores the limitations of the mind and the difficulty of overcoming ingrained tendencies. It uses metaphors to illustrate these points.

The verse suggests that one can be close to wisdom but not truly understand it, like a bee drawn to fragrance from afar. It emphasizes that ingrained tendencies are hard to escape, like a flea's love for blood or a dog's crooked tail. True wisdom involves transcending these tendencies.

blocks.scenario: You are struggling to overcome a bad habit. Do you:

choices.text: Recognize the challenge and persistently work towards change.
Give up, believing it's impossible to change.

blocks.why: Persistently working towards change aligns with the idea that ingrained tendencies are hard to escape but not impossible to overcome, connecting to the tags of mind and wisdom.

blocks.question: According to the verse, what is something that cannot be escaped?

blocks.text: Recognize your tendencies and persistently work towards positive change.
This verse contrasts hypocrisy with genuine devotion and emphasizes the importance of chanting the Divine Name. It also touches upon destiny.

The verse distinguishes between those who are merely pretending to be devoted and those who are truly absorbed in the Divine. It suggests that one receives what is destined and encourages chanting the Divine Name. The Name is said to have the merits of all pilgrimage sites when destined.

blocks.scenario: You are tempted to show off your spiritual knowledge. Do you:

choices.text: Instead, focus on humbly chanting the Divine Name.
Show off your knowledge to impress others.

blocks.why: Focusing on chanting the Divine Name aligns with the idea of genuine devotion and humility, connecting to the tags of naam and humility.

blocks.question: According to the verse, what should one chant with their tongue?

blocks.text: Strive for genuine devotion and humbly chant the Divine Name.
This passage speaks of pain and longing. It expresses the feeling that without the Divine, the soul cannot survive.
The verses convey a sense of misery and regret. There's a yearning for connection with the Divine, recognizing the Lord as a wise master. Serving with humility is also mentioned.

blocks.scenario: You feel overwhelmed by a difficult situation and long for inner peace. Do you:

choices.text: Reflect on your connection to something greater than yourself.
Focus only on the immediate problem and try to solve it logically.

blocks.why: Reflecting on a connection to something greater aligns with the theme of longing for the Divine and finding solace.

blocks.question: According to the passage, what is essential for the soul to survive?

blocks.text: Even in times of pain, remember to look inward and connect with your spirituality.
This passage emphasizes servitude and obedience. It speaks of being connected to the Divine through the Guru's Word.

The verses highlight the idea of surrendering to the Divine will. It suggests that one's fortune comes from being a servant and following the Guru's teachings. Cleverness is useless, and one should strive to follow the Lord's command.

blocks.scenario: You are asked to help with a task that you don't fully understand. Do you:

choices.text: Humbly accept and do your best to follow instructions.
Question the task and try to find a more efficient way to do it.

blocks.why: Humbly accepting and following instructions aligns with the theme of servitude and following the Hukam.

blocks.question: According to the passage, what is exchanged at the store?
blocks.answer: Oneself in exchange for the Guru's Word.

blocks.text: Strive to follow the Guru's teachings and accept the Divine will with humility.
This passage describes devotion and service. It speaks of being a child of the Divine's servants and offering humble service.

The verses emphasize the importance of humility and devotion. It suggests offering service, such as providing water, grinding corn, fanning, and washing feet, while chanting the Divine Name. It also asks for forgiveness, acknowledging human fallibility.

blocks.scenario: A friend makes a mistake that affects you. Do you:

choices.text: Offer forgiveness and understanding.
Hold a grudge and demand an apology.

blocks.why: Offering forgiveness aligns with the theme of asking for forgiveness and recognizing the Divine's greatness.

blocks.question: What actions are mentioned as forms of service?
blocks.answer: Getting water, grinding corn, waving the fan, and washing feet.

blocks.text: Practice humility, offer service, and seek forgiveness to connect with the Divine.
This passage explores the idea of being consumed by devotion. It speaks of being 'insane' with the Fear of God and recognizing only the Divine.

The verses suggest that true devotion may appear unconventional to others. It emphasizes recognizing the oneness of the Divine and seeing nothing else. This 'insanity' is born from a deep connection and fear of God.

blocks.scenario: You feel a strong pull towards a spiritual practice that others find strange. Do you:

choices.text: Continue to pursue your practice with devotion.
Stop your practice to avoid being judged by others.

blocks.why: Continuing with devotion aligns with the theme of being 'insane' with the Fear of God.

blocks.question: What causes Nanak to go 'insane'?

blocks.text: Embrace your devotion, even if it seems unconventional to others, and recognize the oneness of the Divine.
This passage discusses the Command of the Lord and love for the Divine. It contrasts those who follow the Hukam with the self-willed.

The verses suggest that true devotion involves recognizing and following the Lord's Command. It emphasizes love for the Divine and seeing oneself as flawed while viewing others as good. The self-willed (manmukh) are seen as wandering and distant from the Divine.

blocks.scenario: You are faced with a difficult decision that goes against your personal desires. Do you:

choices.text: Consider what aligns with a higher purpose or the needs of others.
Prioritize your own desires and immediate gratification.

blocks.why: Considering a higher purpose aligns with the theme of recognizing the Hukam and prioritizing love for the Divine.

blocks.question: What does the self-willed manmukh think about the Divine?

blocks.text: Strive to recognize and follow the Lord's Command, cultivate love for the Divine, and see the good in others.
This passage speaks of the wealth of the Naam (Divine Name). It describes its unique qualities and the benefits of possessing it.

The verses highlight the value of the Naam as an inner treasure. It suggests that this wealth cannot be destroyed or stolen, and those blessed with it are liberated. Gazing upon its greatness brings peace.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling anxious about losing your material possessions. Do you:

choices.text: Focus on cultivating inner peace and spiritual wealth.
Become more attached to your possessions and try to protect them.

blocks.why: Focusing on inner peace aligns with the theme of the wealth of the Naam being indestructible and bringing liberation.

blocks.question: What cannot happen to the wealth of the Naam?
blocks.answer: It cannot burn, be stolen, or drown.

blocks.text: Cultivate the wealth of the Naam within your heart and find liberation and peace.
This passage emphasizes the importance of the Guru and spiritual wisdom. It speaks of obtaining supreme status through the Guru's guidance.

The verses suggest that true wealth and supreme status are obtained by meeting the True Guru. It highlights the importance of listening to the Unspoken Speech of the Lord and finding balance within oneself.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling lost and unsure of your path in life. Do you:

choices.text: Seek guidance from a trusted mentor or spiritual teacher.
Try to figure things out on your own without seeking help.

blocks.why: Seeking guidance aligns with the theme of meeting the True Guru and obtaining spiritual wisdom.

blocks.question: How is the wealth mentioned in this passage obtained?

blocks.text: Seek guidance from the True Guru and cultivate inner balance to obtain true wealth and supreme status.
This passage addresses the delusion of doubt and the importance of remembering the Divine. It speaks of detaching from the impermanent and drinking in the Nectar.

The verses suggest that doubt leads one astray from the detached Lord. It emphasizes the need to overcome doubts, control the mind, and dwell upon the Divine with every breath to experience the Ambrosial Nectar.

blocks.scenario: You are struggling with doubts about your spiritual path. Do you:

choices.text: Focus on remembering the Divine and detaching from your doubts.
Allow your doubts to consume you and abandon your spiritual practice.

blocks.why: Focusing on remembering the Divine aligns with the theme of overcoming doubt and drinking in the Nectar.

blocks.question: What should one leave behind to drink in the Nectar?

blocks.text: Overcome your doubts, remember the Divine, and detach from the impermanent to experience the Ambrosial Nectar.
Consider how desires affect your mind. The jewel within the mind, attached to truth, can help subdue the mind.
The world's desires can be like intoxicating wine, clouding judgment. However, by focusing on truth, the mind can be controlled. Like a boat carrying merchandise, truth helps us cross over obstacles.

blocks.scenario: You feel overwhelmed by wanting a new phone. You could:

choices.text: Reflect on whether you truly need it or if it's just a passing desire.
Immediately buy it to satisfy the urge.

blocks.why: Reflecting on the need aligns with subduing the mind and attaching to truth, as referenced by the tags.

blocks.question: According to the lesson, what can help subdue the mind?
blocks.answer: The jewel within the mind, attached to truth.

blocks.text: By focusing on truth, we can better manage our desires.
Reflect on the importance of the Guru and Naam. Spiritual wisdom cleanses the mind.
The Guru is described as the wealth of the poor and the strength of the weak. The True Name brings satisfaction, and spiritual wisdom cleanses the mind, preventing it from becoming dirty again.

blocks.scenario: You feel lost and unsure of what to do. You could:

choices.text: Seek guidance from a spiritual mentor or reflect on teachings.
Ignore the feeling and hope it goes away.

blocks.why: Seeking guidance aligns with the importance of the Guru and Naam, as referenced by the tags.

blocks.question: What is said to cleanse the mind?

blocks.text: Guidance and wisdom can help us overcome obstacles.
Consider the concept of oneness and the importance of Naam. Spiritual wisdom is a cleansing bath.
The One Name and One Light pervade all. Spiritual wisdom is like a cleansing bath. Praise of the Lord is like a leaf-offering.

blocks.scenario: You notice differences between yourself and a new acquaintance. You could:

choices.text: Focus on shared humanity and common ground.
Dwell on the differences and feel distant.

blocks.why: Focusing on shared humanity aligns with the concept of oneness, as referenced by the tags.

blocks.question: What pervades the three worlds?
blocks.answer: The One Name and One Light.

blocks.text: Recognizing oneness can help us connect with others.
Reflect on the role of the Guru and Shabad. Consider the idea of detachment.
The True Guru saves us, and the Word of the Shabad abides within. What is outside is the same as what is inside. One who feels the pain of separation from God truly knows.

blocks.scenario: You are upset about losing a game. You could:

choices.text: Accept the loss and learn from it.
Become angry and blame others.

blocks.why: Accepting the loss aligns with the idea of detachment, as referenced by the tags.

blocks.question: What abides within?

blocks.text: Detachment can help us find peace in both success and failure.
Consider the Gurmukh and the importance of Naam. The Shabad helps conquer the mind.
A Gurmukh understands and is linked to the Lord's praise. The soul-bride is in love with her Husband Lord. Through the Shabad, one can conquer and subdue the mind.

blocks.scenario: You are struggling with a difficult task. You could:

choices.text: Focus your mind and seek guidance.
Give up and avoid the challenge.

blocks.why: Focusing the mind and seeking guidance aligns with the tags of Gurmukh, Naam, and Shabad.

blocks.question: What helps conquer and subdue the mind?
blocks.answer: The Word of the Guru's Shabad.

blocks.text: With focus and guidance, we can overcome challenges.
Reflect on the dangers of ego and worldly attachment. The Naam is like ambrosial nectar.
Egotism makes one forget the Lord. Worldly attachment distracts. The True Guru blesses with the Ambrosial Nectar of the Naam.

blocks.scenario: You feel proud of an accomplishment. You could:

choices.text: Acknowledge the accomplishment but remain humble.
Brag about it and seek praise from others.

blocks.why: Remaining humble aligns with avoiding ego, as referenced by the tags.

blocks.question: What makes one forget the Lord?

blocks.text: Humility can help us avoid the pitfalls of ego.
Consider the order of the Lord and the importance of praise. Recognize the source of good and bad deeds.
We are seated and sent where the Lord wills. Thinking good and bad deeds come from oneself is the source of evil. Everything happens by the Order of the Lord.

blocks.scenario: You experience a setback. You could:

choices.text: Accept it as part of the Lord's order and learn from it.
Become angry and blame yourself or others.

blocks.why: Accepting it as part of the Lord's order aligns with the tags of Hukam and ego.

blocks.question: What is the source of all evil?
blocks.answer: Thinking that good and bad deeds come from oneself.

blocks.text: Acceptance can help us find peace in difficult times.
Reflect on the nature of desires and the role of the Guru. Consider how duality can be ended.
Sexual desires are strong, but the Creator stages all plays. By Guru's Grace, duality is ended. Accepting His Will loosens the noose of Death.

blocks.scenario: You are tempted to act impulsively. You could:

choices.text: Pause, reflect, and seek guidance.
Give in to the impulse without thinking.

blocks.why: Pausing and seeking guidance aligns with the tags of Guru and desire.

blocks.question: How is duality ended?

blocks.text: Reflection and guidance can help us make wise choices.
Coming and going in reincarnation no longer exist when one dwells in the home of the self within. Remember the Dear Lord, and abandon the corruption of your mind.
When one realizes the self, the cycle of reincarnation ends. It is important to remember the Dear Lord and let go of the mind's corruption. Meditating on the Guru's Shabad helps focus on truth.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling anxious about the future. A) You focus on remembering the Lord and letting go of negative thoughts. B) You dwell on your worries and fears.

choices.text: Focus on remembering the Lord and letting go of negative thoughts.
Dwell on your worries and fears.

blocks.why: Choosing to remember the Lord and abandon corruption of the mind aligns with the lesson's tags of naam and mind.

blocks.question: What happens when one dwells in the home of the self within?
blocks.answer: Coming and going in reincarnation no longer exist.

blocks.text: By remembering the Lord and focusing on truth, one can find peace within.
By great good fortune, I have found the Guru. He bestows His Glance of Grace. Eradicate self-conceit from within.
Finding the Guru is a blessing. The Divine bestows grace upon us. It is important to let go of ego and pride.

blocks.scenario: You receive help from a mentor. A) You acknowledge their guidance and appreciate their help. B) You take all the credit for your success.

choices.text: Acknowledge their guidance and appreciate their help.
Take all the credit for your success.

blocks.why: Acknowledging guidance and help aligns with the lesson's tags of guru, grace, and humility.

blocks.question: What should one eradicate from within?

blocks.text: Finding the Guru and letting go of ego can lead to spiritual growth.
Meditate on the Name of the Lord. Doubts have been cut away. This mind wanders around, driven by greed.
By meditating on the Lord's Name, doubts can be removed. It is important to be aware of the mind's tendency to wander, driven by greed. The Guru inspires understanding of the Naam.

blocks.scenario: You are tempted to buy something you don't need. A) You reflect on whether it's a genuine need or driven by desire. B) You immediately purchase it without thinking.

choices.text: Reflect on whether it's a genuine need or driven by desire.
Immediately purchase it without thinking.

blocks.why: Reflecting on needs versus desires aligns with the lesson's tags of naam and greed.

blocks.question: What can be cut away through the Word of the Shabad?

blocks.text: Meditating on the Name and being mindful of greed can bring clarity.
God Himself is all-in-all. Gurmukhs abide in peace. Seek and find those who are imbued with Truth.
The Divine is the ultimate reality. Those who follow the Guru find peace. It is valuable to seek out and connect with those who are connected to Truth.

blocks.scenario: You feel disconnected from others. A) You seek out people who embody truth and wisdom. B) You isolate yourself and dwell on your loneliness.

choices.text: Seek out people who embody truth and wisdom.
Isolate yourself and dwell on your loneliness.

blocks.why: Seeking out people who embody truth aligns with the lesson's tags of oneness, peace, and truth.

blocks.question: Who abides in peace?

blocks.text: Recognizing the Divine in all and seeking truth can lead to inner peace.
All serve the One True Lord. Gurmukhs merge with Him. Self-willed manmukhs are deluded by doubt.
Everyone serves the Divine in some way. Those who follow the Guru unite with the Divine. Those who are self-willed are often lost in doubt. The Naam abides within the mind of the Gurmukh.

blocks.scenario: You are faced with a difficult decision. A) You seek guidance from a trusted mentor or spiritual leader. B) You rely solely on your own understanding, ignoring advice.

choices.text: Seek guidance from a trusted mentor or spiritual leader.
Rely solely on your own understanding, ignoring advice.

blocks.why: Seeking guidance aligns with the lesson's tags of hukam and gurmukh.

blocks.question: Who merges with the True Lord?

blocks.text: Serving the Divine and seeking guidance can lead to clarity and union.
Meditate on the Lord's Name. Contemplate the Word of the Guru's Teachings. Praise the True Lord.
It is important to meditate on the Divine Name. Reflecting on the Guru's teachings is valuable. We should praise the True Lord, who is beyond compare.

blocks.scenario: You feel grateful for something in your life. A) You express your gratitude through prayer or kind words. B) You keep your gratitude to yourself and don't acknowledge it.

choices.text: Express your gratitude through prayer or kind words.
Keep your gratitude to yourself and don't acknowledge it.

blocks.why: Expressing gratitude aligns with the lesson's tags of naam and praise.

blocks.question: What should one contemplate?
blocks.answer: The Word of the Guru's Teachings.

blocks.text: Meditating, reflecting, and praising can deepen our connection to the Divine.

Those who forsake the True Guru and attach themselves to duality will face consequences. Run to His Sanctuary; granting His forgiveness, He merges us into Himself. Through loving devotional worship, one can cross over.

Turning away from the Guru and embracing duality can lead to suffering. Seeking refuge in the Divine leads to forgiveness and union. Devotion and love are pathways to liberation. God is independent and self-sufficient.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling lost and disconnected. A) You seek guidance from the True Guru and engage in devotional practices. B) You continue down your current path without seeking spiritual guidance.

choices.text: Seek guidance from the True Guru and engage in devotional practices.
Continue down your current path without seeking spiritual guidance.

blocks.why: Seeking guidance and engaging in devotion aligns with the lesson's tags of grace and devotion.

blocks.question: What happens to those who forsake the True Guru and attach themselves to duality?

blocks.text: Seeking the Divine and practicing devotion can lead to forgiveness and union.
Chanting the Naam, the Name of the Lord, you will be saved. The Naam is the supreme wealth. Whoever chants the Naam, all his sins and mistakes are taken away.
Repeating the Divine Name can lead to salvation. The Naam is the most valuable treasure. By chanting the Naam, sins and mistakes can be forgiven. The Naam saves the humble devotees.

blocks.scenario: You have made a mistake and feel regretful. A) You chant the Naam and seek forgiveness. B) You dwell on your mistake and feel hopeless.

choices.text: Chant the Naam and seek forgiveness.
Dwell on your mistake and feel hopeless.

blocks.why: Chanting the Naam and seeking forgiveness aligns with the lesson's tags of naam, devotion, and sin.

blocks.question: What is the supreme wealth in this Dark Age?

blocks.text: Chanting the Naam can bring salvation and forgiveness.
God takes pity on humble servants and makes them His own. He saves the honor of those who seek His Sanctuary. Nanak says the Lord has enshrined the Lord's Name within his heart.
This passage speaks of God's grace and protection for those who are devoted. By enshrining the Lord's Name, one finds salvation. God's mercy extends to those who seek refuge in Him.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling overwhelmed by a difficult situation. Do you:

choices.text: Remember the Lord's Name and seek His sanctuary.
Try to solve the problem completely on your own.

The passage suggests that outward practices like meditation, celibacy, and pilgrimage are insufficient if the mind is still restless, filled with pride, or consumed by anger. True purity comes from being beyond worldly attachments. Meeting the Perfect Guru removes anxiety.

blocks.scenario: You are engaging in religious practices but still feel restless and anxious. You remember the teaching about the mind running around.

choices.text: You seek the guidance of a Perfect Guru to calm your mind and remove anxiety.
You continue with your practices, hoping they will eventually bring peace despite your restless mind.

blocks.why: Seeking the guidance of a Perfect Guru aligns with the teaching of removing anxiety and finding purity beyond attachment, connecting to the tags of 'mind' and 'ego'.

blocks.question: What is removed when meeting the Perfect Guru?

blocks.text: Seeking guidance from a Guru can help calm the mind and remove anxiety.

This lesson speaks of the Lord as the Inner-knower. It emphasizes the importance of Naam and the protection offered by the Guru. It highlights the connection between remembering the Lord and obtaining honor.

The passage suggests that the Lord knows everything within us. Those with the Lord's Name in their hearts are truly blessed. The Guru protects honor, and remembering the Lord brings perfect honor, while forgetting leads to degradation.

blocks.scenario: You are facing a challenging situation where your honor is at stake. You remember the teaching about the Guru protecting honor.

choices.text: You seek guidance from the Guru and remember the Lord to find strength and maintain your honor.

blocks.question: Who protects and preserves honor?

blocks.text: Remembering the Lord and seeking guidance can help you maintain your honor.
This lesson contrasts the fleeting pleasures of Maya with the lasting treasure of Naam. It speaks of being dyed in the Lord's Love through the Guru's grace. It emphasizes the greatness of the Lord.

The passage suggests that worldly pleasures bring both joy and sorrow. The Name of the Lord offers true peace and liberation. Those who meet the Guru and sing praises are dyed in the Lord's Love. Through Naam, one obtains greatness and respect.

blocks.scenario: You are tempted by worldly pleasures but feel a sense of emptiness. You remember the teaching about Maya fading away.

choices.text: You focus on Naam and seek the Guru's guidance to find lasting peace and love.

blocks.why: Focusing on Naam and seeking the Guru's guidance aligns with the teaching of finding lasting peace and love through the Guru's grace, connecting to the tags of 'naam' and 'love'.

blocks.question: What fades away like the shade of a passing cloud?

blocks.text: Focusing on Naam and seeking guidance can help you find lasting peace and love.
This lesson speaks of the One Creator Lord who created everything. It emphasizes the importance of understanding the Creator through the Guru's guidance. It contrasts ego with emancipation.

The passage suggests that everything originates from the One Creator. Understanding this comes through meeting the True Guru. Without the Guru, there is darkness, and the mind remains restless. Meeting the Guru leads to emancipation.

blocks.scenario: You feel disconnected from the world and struggle to understand its purpose. You remember the teaching about understanding the Creator Lord.

blocks.why: Seeking the guidance of the True Guru aligns with the teaching of understanding the Creator and finding emancipation, connecting to the tags of 'oneness' and 'guru'.

blocks.question: What is there without the Guru?

blocks.text: Seeking guidance from the Guru can help you understand the Creator and find connection.
The text discusses deeds done in egotism and being deluded. It speaks of meeting the Guru and realizing the One Lord.
Actions driven by ego create bonds. The world is enticed by Maya, engrossed in greed, and attached to possessions. However, only those who are pleasing to the Lord meet Him.

blocks.question: According to the text, what creates bonds?

This passage describes the Lord as fearless and merciful. It also speaks of people's attachment to wealth and possessions.
The Lord cherishes all beings. People become attached to wealth, some even more than their own lives. However, wealth is a fickle companion and will not remain with them.

choices.text: Buy a luxury item.
Save and donate.

blocks.why: Spending on luxury reflects attachment to wealth, while saving and donating shows detachment and aligns with the tags of fearlessness and detachment.

blocks.question: What is the Lord described as?

blocks.text: Consider the role of wealth in your life and how it affects your peace of mind.
The text mentions hermits, yogis, and others seeking spiritual paths. It emphasizes meditating in remembrance of the One Lord and finding liberation in the Saadh Sangat.
Maya clings to those in various lifestyles. Liberation comes when the Lord releases one from bonds. Meditating on the Lord covers faults, and finding the Saadh Sangat is rare and valuable.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling lost and disconnected. A) You isolate yourself and try to figure things out alone. B) You seek out a community of like-minded individuals for support and guidance.

blocks.answer: In the Saadh Sangat, the Company of the Holy.

blocks.text: Reflect on the importance of community and remembrance in your spiritual journey.
This passage discusses the intoxication of desires and the consequences of believing in falsehood. It also mentions the impact of past actions and the suffering that comes from forgetting God.

Those intoxicated with desire abandon what is their own and love what belongs to others. Desires are never quenched, and hopes are unfulfilled. Forgetting God leads to suffering, and the karma of past actions cannot be erased.

blocks.scenario: You see a product advertised that you really want, even though you don't need it and can't afford it. A) You buy it anyway, using your credit card. B) You resist the urge and focus on your needs.

choices.text: Buy it on credit.
Resist the urge.

blocks.why: Buying the product despite not needing it reflects the intoxication of desire, while resisting aligns with detachment and awareness of karma.

blocks.question: What are people intoxicated with, according to the text?

blocks.text: Reflect on your desires and how they influence your choices and actions.
The text speaks of seeking the Sanctuary of God and the Lord being the destroyer of sorrow. It emphasizes emancipation through loving devotion and the Guru as the embodiment of the Lord.

The Lord is merciful and emancipates those He pleases. Emancipation comes through loving devotional worship. The Guru saves us from the great fire, and the Lord is the giver of the true state of life.

blocks.scenario: You see someone struggling to carry groceries. A) You ignore them and continue on your way. B) You offer to help them carry their bags.

choices.text: Ignore them.
Offer help.

blocks.why: Offering help aligns with seva (selfless service) and compassion, while ignoring the person goes against it, connecting to the lesson's tags.

blocks.question: What is the Lord described as?
blocks.answer: The Destroyer of sorrow and suffering.

blocks.text: Consider how you can show compassion and offer seva to those around you.
This passage emphasizes the importance of meditating on the Lord's Name. It speaks of the Lord being the giver of peace and the Naam eradicating duality and doubt.
The Lord submits to the will of devotees and is the giver of peace. Meditating on the Name brings mercy and eradicates duality and doubt. The humble beg for the Naam.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling anxious and overwhelmed. A) You distract yourself with entertainment. B) You take a few moments to meditate or reflect quietly.

choices.text: Distract yourself.
Meditate or reflect.

blocks.why: Taking time to meditate aligns with the importance of Naam and devotion, while distraction goes against it, connecting to the tags of devotion and peace.

blocks.question: What does the Naam eradicate?

blocks.text: Reflect on how you can incorporate meditation and remembrance into your daily life.
The text describes the Lord as utterly powerful and dear to the mind and breath of life. It emphasizes that there is none other than Him.
The Lord is utterly powerful, and we are His servants. The Beloved is dear to the mind and blesses us with gifts. There is none other than Him, emphasizing oneness.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling envious of someone else's success. A) You dwell on their achievements and feel resentful. B) You appreciate their success and focus on your own path.

choices.text: Feel resentful.
Focus on your path.

blocks.why: Focusing on your own path aligns with recognizing the oneness of the Lord, while resentment goes against it, connecting to the tags of love and devotion.

blocks.question: What is the Lord described as?

blocks.text: Reflect on the importance of love and devotion in recognizing the oneness of all.
This passage speaks of the Lord as the redeemer of sinners and the sustainer of all beings. It expresses a desire to meet a Saint who can inspire meditation on the Lord.
The Lord sustains all beings and is the redeemer of sinners. Meeting a Saint can inspire meditation on the Lord. The text expresses a desire for grace and devotion.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling discouraged about your spiritual progress. A) You give up and lose hope. B) You seek guidance from a mentor or spiritual teacher.

choices.text: Give up.

blocks.text: Reflect on the importance of grace and guidance in your spiritual journey.
This passage speaks of devotion and humility. It uses the metaphor of a fish in water to describe the relationship with the Divine.

The verses express that the speaker is known only as a servant of the Divine. They find support and sustenance in this devotion. The Divine cherishes all, and the speaker offers humility as their only prayer, acknowledging that the Divine knows the way, like water to a fish.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling lost and unsure of your path. Do you:

choices.text: Reflect on your connection to something greater than yourself, acknowledging your dependence and seeking guidance.

blocks.why: This aligns with the tags of humility and devotion, recognizing a higher power and seeking guidance.

blocks.question: According to this passage, what is the speaker's only prayer?

blocks.text: Remember that humility and devotion can provide support and guidance.
This passage emphasizes the importance of the Society of Saints and the greatness of the Divine Name. It speaks of fulfillment and satisfaction found within this association.

The verses describe the Divine as eternal, unchanging, and infinite. It expresses a desire to be blessed with the company of the Saints and the humility to serve. The Saints are described as fulfilled, and the Divine Name is seen as a priceless, unattainable jewel.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling disconnected and unfulfilled. Do you:

choices.text: Seek out the company of people who inspire you and share your values, and reflect on the Divine Name.

blocks.text: Finding fulfillment can come from connecting with others and remembering the Divine.
This passage discusses contentment, the importance of the Guru, and the banishment of ego. It speaks of inner satisfaction and spiritual wisdom.

The verses describe a mind satisfied by belief in the Divine, seeing all in meditation. Meeting the Guru leads to awareness, fulfillment, and access to the Lord's treasure. Through the Guru, one can attain this state, banishing egotistical pride.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling restless and dissatisfied with your life. Do you:

blocks.why: This aligns with the tags of contentment, guru, and ego, emphasizing the importance of guidance and humility in finding inner peace.

blocks.question: What is banished from the mind in this passage?

blocks.text: Contentment can be found through guidance and letting go of ego.
This passage focuses on the importance of listening to and chanting the Divine Name. It highlights the washing away of sins and the attainment of spiritual wisdom through the Guru's Grace.

The verses advise abandoning clever tricks and ego, and instead chanting the Divine Name. Listening to the Name washes away past sins. Pain, poverty, and fear disappear, and meditation on the Lord becomes the essence of spiritual wisdom through the Guru's Grace.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling overwhelmed by past mistakes and anxieties about the future. Do you:

blocks.question: What is described as the essence of spiritual wisdom in this passage?

blocks.text: Listening to and chanting the Divine Name can help overcome past mistakes and anxieties.
This passage discusses the consequences of forgetting the Divine Name and the importance of chanting it continuously. It also touches on the transient nature of worldly attachments.

The verses state that those who forget the Divine Name are reduced to dust, and worldly attachments are fleeting. Chanting the Name brings peace and protects from suffering. Meeting with the Holy and worshipping the Divine is the only thing that truly lasts.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling overly attached to material possessions and relationships. Do you:

choices.text: Remind yourself of the impermanence of these things and focus on chanting the Divine Name.

blocks.why: This aligns with the tags of naam and detachment, emphasizing the importance of remembrance and non-attachment to find peace.

This passage speaks of the Divine as the Giver of peace, always present, and unaffected by change. It emphasizes the importance of loving the Divine Name and meditating on the compassionate Lord.

The verses describe the Divine as eternal and unchanging. Loving the Divine Name and thinking of the Lord is the purest way of life. Meditating on the compassionate Lord brings success, and the speaker's mind is filled with love for the Divine.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling anxious and overwhelmed by the uncertainties of life. Do you:

blocks.text: Loving the Divine Name and meditating on the compassionate Lord can bring peace and strength.

The verses advise contemplating the GurMantra at all times and joining the Company of the Holy. Enshrining the Divine Name within the heart and loving the Lord leads to forgetting everything else. Eliminating self-conceit and meditating on the Lord fulfills all desires.

blocks.question: What should be enshrined within the heart, according to this passage?

This passage speaks of renouncing self-conceit, becoming the dust of the feet of the Holy, and drinking in the Ambrosial Nectar of the Divine Name. It emphasizes the importance of Divine Grace and making the One Lord your only friend.

The verses advise renouncing self-conceit and seeking humility. The Divine Name is received through Divine Grace. Drinking in the Ambrosial Nectar of the Name leads to immortality. Making the One Lord your only friend brings companionship and support.

blocks.question: What should one drink in, according to this passage?

blocks.text: Humility, remembrance, and Divine Grace can help you overcome arrogance and find connection.
