Decline to volunteer, feeling that you are too busy.

blocks.why: Volunteering your time aligns with the teaching of serving the Divine and purifying the hands through service.

blocks.question: According to this lesson, what is the most beautiful path?
blocks.answer: To follow the Lord of the Universe.

blocks.text: By following the path of the Divine and serving others, we can purify ourselves and find true fulfillment.
Meditate on the Naam, it will be your support. The Name alone shall save you. The Guru liberates.

Meditating on the Divine Name provides support, especially in times of need. The Name is the ultimate savior. The Guru's grace frees one from bonds and allows one to see the Divine everywhere, leading to peace and satisfaction.

blocks.scenario: You are facing a difficult situation and feel like you have no one to turn to. You remember the teaching about the Name being your ultimate support.

choices.text: Take some time to meditate on the Divine Name and seek inner strength.
Continue to feel helpless and alone, without seeking inner support.

blocks.why: Meditating on the Divine Name aligns with the teaching of finding support and strength through the Name.

blocks.question: According to this lesson, what will save you at the very last instant?

blocks.text: By meditating on the Divine Name and seeking the Guru's guidance, we can find peace, liberation, and ultimate support.
Meditate on God by meeting the Guru. Sing the Glorious Praises of the Lord with each breath, never forgetting Him.
By remembering God constantly, one experiences His presence always. Being a sacrifice to the Guru's Lotus Feet leads to finding the Ocean of peace.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling overwhelmed by daily tasks. Do you:

choices.text: Take a moment to remember God and sing His praises.
Continue working without pause.

blocks.why: Remembering God and singing praises brings peace, aligning with the tags remembrance, devotion, and peace.

blocks.question: What happens when you never forget Him?

blocks.text: Constant remembrance brings peace.
The Guru's Shabad is sweet. Obtain the Ambrosial Nectar of the Naam in the Society of the Saints.
The Divine Radiance is manifest in every heart. By joining the Society of the Saints, one is dyed in the deep crimson color of His Love, which never fades.

blocks.scenario: You have a free afternoon. Do you:

choices.text: Attend a gathering with spiritual people.
Spend the afternoon alone.

blocks.why: Attending a spiritual gathering aligns with the tags naam, love, and sangat, fostering connection and devotion.

blocks.question: What is obtained in the Society of the Saints?
blocks.answer: The Ambrosial Nectar of the Naam.

blocks.text: Find love through the Society of Saints.
The Guru gives the Name of the Lord as a companion. When the Word of God dwells in the heart, all hunger is relieved.
Having hope in the Lord brings fulfillment. Gazing upon His Darshan brings immeasurable peace, and the fear of birth and death is gone.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling anxious about the future. Do you:

choices.text: Remember the Name of the Lord and place your hopes in Him.
Worry about all the possibilities.

blocks.why: Remembering the Lord and placing hope in Him brings peace and fearlessness, aligning with the tags naam, peace, and fearlessness.

blocks.question: What is given as a companion?

blocks.text: The Name brings peace and fearlessness.
The Ambrosial Amrit is within you, yet you are deluded. Become in tune with the Saints.
The mind is enticed by Maya. By connecting with the Saints, one obtains all treasures within the heart, and light merges into the Light.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling drawn to material possessions. Do you:

choices.text: Connect with spiritual people and focus on inner peace.
Indulge in acquiring more possessions.

blocks.why: Connecting with spiritual people and focusing on inner peace fosters detachment from Maya and aligns with the tags maya, detachment, and sangat.

blocks.question: What happens when light merges into the Light?
blocks.answer: All treasures are found within the heart.

blocks.text: Find detachment through Sangat.
Love God from the beginning. The True Guru blesses with Teachings. The Guru unites with the Lord.
The Guru is the Saving Grace. The Guru is deep, profound, calm and benevolent. Through the Guru, one finds the Bed of Peace.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling lost and confused. Do you:

choices.text: Seek guidance from a spiritual mentor or teacher.
Try to figure it out on your own.

blocks.why: Seeking guidance from a spiritual mentor aligns with the tags guru, grace, and peace, leading to inner peace and understanding.

blocks.question: What does the True Guru bless with?

blocks.text: Find peace through the Guru's grace.
Blessed is the day one remembers God. Offer your heart as a sacrifice to Him.
Gazing upon His Blessed Vision brings regal pleasures. When God says, "My servant, stay here with me", one knows unlimited peace.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling unfulfilled despite having many possessions. Do you:

choices.text: Offer your heart in devotion and seek God's presence.
Acquire more possessions to try and feel better.

blocks.why: Offering your heart in devotion and seeking God's presence brings contentment and peace, aligning with the tags devotion, contentment, and peace.

blocks.question: What happens when God says, 'My servant, stay here with me'?

blocks.text: Find peace through devotion.
Abandon skepticism and sorrow. Chant the Name of the Lord, meeting with the Guru.
The illness of egotism is eradicated. By subduing the five thieves, the mind becomes stable, steady, and fearless.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling arrogant and self-important. Do you:

choices.text: Chant the Name of the Lord and seek guidance from the Guru.
Continue to focus on your own accomplishments.

blocks.why: Chanting the Name of the Lord and seeking guidance from the Guru helps to overcome ego and fosters fearlessness, aligning with the tags ego, naam, and fearlessness.

blocks.question: What illness is eradicated?

blocks.text: Overcome ego through the Naam.
God is forever our Help and Support. He blesses with bliss. Join the Society of the Saints.
God cherishes us like a parent loves a child. By joining the Society of the Saints, one is lovingly attuned to the Lord.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling lonely and disconnected. Do you:

choices.text: Join the Society of the Saints and connect with the Lord.
Isolate yourself further.

blocks.why: Joining the Society of the Saints fosters love and devotion, aligning with the tags love, devotion, and sangat.

blocks.question: What happens when joining the Society of the Saints?
blocks.answer: One is lovingly attuned to the Lord.

blocks.text: Find love through Sangat.
Sing of your Lord and Master, your Best Friend. Meditate on God, the Giver of peace.

We should focus our devotion on God, who is the source of peace and joy. By seeking the Guru's guidance, we can find wisdom and understanding. When we connect with God, we no longer need to depend on others.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling anxious about an upcoming presentation. Should you:

choices.text: Take a few moments to meditate and remember God.
Rely solely on your own preparation and worry about the outcome.

blocks.why: Choosing to meditate connects to the tags of devotion and peace, reminding us to seek solace in God.

blocks.question: According to this passage, who is the giver of peace?

blocks.text: Remembering God can bring peace and reduce dependence on others.
I have the Almighty Support of my Dear Lord God. He has poured the medicine of the Naam into my mouth; I have fallen at the Guru's Feet.

blocks.question: What does following the Guru's teachings lead to?

blocks.text: Following the Guru's teachings and remembering the Naam can bring peace and safety to your life.

This lesson explores the importance of love and devotion to the Lord.  It contrasts those who are filled with love for the Lord with the self-willed who are driven by ego and desires.  Good karma is attained through worship and adoration of the Lord.

The verses express a longing for the Lord's love and vision.  The self-willed are consumed by negative emotions and fail to discern good from bad.  The Gurmukhs, filled with love for the Lord, receive the good karma of their actions.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling disconnected from the Divine. You can either focus on your own desires and ego, or you can seek to connect with the Lord through love and devotion.

choices.text: Seek to connect with the Lord through love and devotion.
Focus on your own desires and ego.

blocks.why: Choosing to connect with the Lord aligns with the tags 'love' and 'haumai', emphasizing the importance of love and overcoming ego.

blocks.question: What are the self-willed filled with?

blocks.text: Cultivating love and devotion to the Lord can bring you closer to the Divine.

This lesson contrasts attachment to Maya with meditation on the Naam and seeking the Guru's guidance.  Those attached to worldly possessions and pleasures face the consequences of their actions.  Those who meditate on the Naam and seek the Guru's protection find salvation.

The verses describe how people are often attached to the fleeting pleasures of Maya and forget the Naam.  This leads to punishment and continued cycles of reincarnation.  Meditating on the Naam, with the Guru's grace, leads to merging with the True Lord.

blocks.scenario: You are tempted to indulge in worldly pleasures and possessions. You can either give in to the temptation, or you can remember the Naam and seek the Guru's guidance.

choices.text: Remember the Naam and seek the Guru's guidance.
Give in to the temptation.

blocks.why: Choosing to remember the Naam and seek guidance aligns with the tags 'naam' and 'guru', emphasizing the importance of detaching from Maya and seeking spiritual guidance.

blocks.question: What happens to those who are attached to the flavors of Maya?
blocks.answer: They forget the Naam and receive punishment.

blocks.text: Meditating on the Naam and seeking the Guru's guidance can help you detach from Maya and find true fulfillment.

This lesson explores the path to peace through detachment and the Shabad.  It contrasts the pain of attachment with the supreme peace attained by the Gurmukhs.  The Shabad is described as a cooling and soothing force that dispels sorrow.

The verses highlight that hope and attachment lead to pain, while detachment brings supreme peace.  The Shabad, when it dwells in the mind and body, dispels sorrow and separation.  True understanding and peace are attained through the Guru's grace.

blocks.scenario: You are holding onto something that is causing you pain. You can either continue to hold on, or you can let go and find peace.

choices.text: Let go and find peace.
Continue to hold on.

blocks.why: Choosing to let go aligns with the tags 'detachment' and 'peace', emphasizing the importance of detachment in attaining peace.

blocks.question: What dispels sorrow and separation?

blocks.text: Detachment and the Shabad can lead to supreme peace and freedom from sorrow.

This lesson contrasts worldly attachments with the Ambrosial Nectar of the Naam and the power of the Shabad.  Worldly attachments, though seemingly loving, can lead to suffering.  The Naam and the Shabad offer true fulfillment and union with the Lord.

The verses describe how worldly attachments, such as family and possessions, can lead to conflict and suffering.  The Guru's Word, the Ambrosial Nectar of the Naam, satisfies all hunger and desire.  The Shabad is the life within all living beings and leads to union with the Lord.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling overwhelmed by your attachments to family and possessions. You can either continue to be consumed by these attachments, or you can seek solace in the Naam and the Shabad.

choices.text: Seek solace in the Naam and the Shabad.
Continue to be consumed by these attachments.

blocks.why: Choosing to seek solace in the Naam and the Shabad aligns with the tags 'naam' and 'shabad', emphasizing the importance of these in finding true fulfillment.

blocks.question: What is the Guru's Word described as?
blocks.answer: The Ambrosial Nectar of the Naam.

blocks.text: The Naam and the Shabad offer true fulfillment and union with the Lord, beyond worldly attachments.
This passage discusses attachment to Maya and forgetting the Divine. It highlights the importance of the Guru's guidance.

Being attached to Maya causes one to forget the Fear of God, the Guru, and love for the Infinite Lord. Greed obscures wisdom, preventing one from embracing love for the True Lord. The Word of the Shabad resides in the minds of Gurmukhs, leading them to salvation.

blocks.scenario: You are offered a promotion that requires you to work long hours and neglect your spiritual practices. Do you:

choices.text: Decline the promotion to maintain your spiritual focus.
Accept the promotion and try to balance work and spirituality.

blocks.why: Choosing to decline the promotion reflects detatchment from Maya and prioritizing the Guru, aligning with the lesson's tags.

blocks.question: According to this passage, what does attachment to Maya cause one to forget?
blocks.answer: The Fear of God, the Guru, and love for the Infinite Lord.

blocks.text: Remember to prioritize spiritual connection over worldly attachments.
This passage speaks of meditating on the Lord's Name and the blessings received through His Grace. It emphasizes the importance of accepting the Order of the Lord.

Meditating on the Lord's Name brings an end to pain, hunger, and misfortune. The Lord, by His Grace, summons those He approves. The Perfect Guru bestows gifts that increase daily, and the Merciful Lord's blessings cannot be hidden. The Order of the Lord is beyond challenge, so one should abandon self-conceit and accept His Will.

blocks.scenario: You face a difficult situation at work that seems impossible to resolve. Do you:

choices.text: Meditate on the Lord's Name and trust in His Grace to guide you.
Rely solely on your own efforts and cleverness to find a solution.

blocks.why: Choosing to meditate and trust in His Grace aligns with the lesson's emphasis on Naam, Kirpa, and Hukam.

blocks.question: According to this passage, what brings an end to pain, hunger, and misfortune?

blocks.text: Trust in the Lord's Grace and accept His Order in all situations.
This passage contrasts egotism with Truth and the importance of the Company of the Holy. It suggests abandoning self-conceit and seeking the True Guru.

The passage acknowledges that all gifts and beauty come from the Divine, while excessive cleverness and egotism belong to the mortal. It emphasizes that Truth should be one's foundation, and the True Guru leads to God. Joining the Saadh Sangat helps one cross over the world-ocean.

blocks.scenario: You are in a group project where you believe your ideas are superior to others. Do you:

choices.text: Humbly listen to others' ideas and work collaboratively.
Insist on your ideas being implemented, believing they are the best.

blocks.why: Choosing to listen and collaborate reflects abandoning ego and embracing the value of Sangat, aligning with the lesson's tags.

blocks.question: According to this passage, what should be one's food and clothes?

blocks.text: Strive for humility and seek guidance from the True Guru.
This passage describes the beauty of the Creator's Order and the importance of remembering the Divine. It highlights the Lord's Mercy and Will.

The passage speaks of the Creator Lord issuing His Order, bringing abundance and comfort to the world. Meditating in remembrance on the Inaccessible and Infinite Lord rejuvenates the mind and body. The Lord does whatever He pleases, and everyone walks in harmony with His Will.

blocks.scenario: You experience an unexpected setback in your personal life. Do you:

choices.text: Accept it as part of the Lord's Will and continue to remember Him.
Become discouraged and question the fairness of life.

blocks.why: Choosing to accept it as the Lord's Will and remember Him aligns with the lesson's emphasis on Hukam, Kirpa, and Remembrance.

blocks.question: According to this passage, what rejuvenates the mind and body?
blocks.answer: Meditating in remembrance on the Inaccessible and Infinite Lord.

blocks.text: Remember to accept the Lord's Will and meditate on His Name.
This passage discusses the impermanence of wealth and power, contrasting it with the stability of the Lord's Saints. It emphasizes joining the Sat Sangat and chanting the Lord's Name.

The passage states that wealth and power are temporary, like the green leaves of the forest. No one can take wealth with them when they depart. The Lord's Saints are steady and stable, worshipping and chanting the Lord's Name. Those blessed by the Lord join the Sat Sangat.

blocks.scenario: You are invited to a gathering that promises networking opportunities but clashes with your regular Sat Sangat meeting. Do you:

choices.text: Prioritize attending the Sat Sangat meeting.
Attend the networking event for potential career advancement.

blocks.why: Choosing to attend the Sat Sangat aligns with the lesson's emphasis on Sangat and detatchment from Maya.

blocks.question: According to this passage, what are the Lord's Saints doing?
blocks.answer: Worshipping, adoring, and chanting the Lord's Name.

blocks.text: Remember the impermanence of worldly possessions and seek the company of the holy.
This passage discusses the impermanence of relationships and wealth, urging remembrance of the Lord. It expresses devotion to the Saints.

The passage states that family and wealth will not accompany you in the end, urging meditation on the Lord. It expresses humility and devotion to the Saints. It also notes the changing nature of life, where laughter turns to tears and vice versa.

blocks.scenario: You experience a significant loss in your life, such as the passing of a loved one. Do you:

choices.text: Remember the Lord and seek solace in devotion.
Become consumed by grief and isolate yourself from others.

blocks.why: Choosing to remember the Lord and seek solace aligns with the lesson's emphasis on detachment and remembrance.

blocks.question: According to this passage, what will not go along with you in the end?
blocks.answer: Mother, father, spouse, children, and wealth.

blocks.text: Remember the impermanence of life and seek refuge in the Lord's remembrance.
This passage describes the transformative power of the Divine and devotion to the Saints. It emphasizes the Lord's Will and Oneness.

The passage illustrates how the Divine can transform water into a desert, a beggar into a king, and a fool into a scholar. It states that God is the Beloved of the Holy Saints, and the speaker is a sacrifice to His image.

blocks.scenario: You witness someone experiencing a sudden change in fortune, either for better or worse. Do you:

choices.text: Recognize it as part of the Divine's transformative power and accept it.
Judge the situation based on your own limited understanding.

blocks.why: Choosing to recognize it as the Divine's power aligns with the lesson's emphasis on Hukam and Oneness.

blocks.question: According to this passage, who is the Beloved of the Holy Saints?

blocks.text: Recognize the transformative power of the Divine and offer devotion to the Saints.
This passage warns against the allure of corruption and attachment to worldly pleasures. It uses metaphors to illustrate the dangers of these attachments.

The passage cautions against entering the "forest of corruption" and being misled by toxic drugs. It compares attachment to wealth and woman to a fish swallowing a hook. The bee stores honey, but it is taken away, and the cow stores milk, but it is milked by another.

blocks.scenario: You are tempted to engage in a risky financial investment that promises high returns. Do you:

choices.text: Refrain from the investment, recognizing the potential for corruption and attachment.
Proceed with the investment, hoping to gain financial wealth.

blocks.why: Choosing to refrain from the investment aligns with the lesson's warning against Maya and attachment.

blocks.question: According to this passage, what is the mortal being misled into eating?

blocks.text: Be mindful of the allure of worldly pleasures and avoid attachments that lead to corruption.

This lesson discusses how attachment to Maya can lead to unfulfilled desires. It speaks of someone working hard for Maya, burying wealth, and burning with desires, yet not appreciating what they have.

The verses highlight the futility of excessive attachment to worldly possessions and desires.  The pursuit of Maya can lead to a life of dissatisfaction and a failure to connect with the divine. Ultimately, the body turns to dust, while desires remain unfulfilled.

blocks.scenario: You receive a bonus at work. Do you:

choices.text: Save most of it, use some to help others, and appreciate what you have.
Immediately spend it all on something you've been wanting.

blocks.why: Option A reflects appreciating what you have and helping others, aligning with the lesson's message against excessive desire.

blocks.question: According to the lesson, what can happen when someone works only for Maya?
blocks.answer: They may burn with desire and not appreciate what they have.

blocks.text: Attachment to Maya can lead to dissatisfaction. Appreciating what you have and helping others can bring greater fulfillment.
This lesson explores the concept of oneness and devotion. It describes the divine as both the deity and the worshipper, emphasizing the interconnectedness of all things.

The verses suggest that the divine is present in everything, like waves arising from and returning to the water.  True devotion involves recognizing this oneness and seeing the divine in all aspects of existence.  The devoted are seen as being in the image of God.

blocks.scenario: You see someone struggling. Do you:

choices.text: Offer help, recognizing their inherent worth and connection to all beings.
Ignore them, assuming their problems are their own responsibility.

blocks.why: Option A reflects the lesson's emphasis on recognizing the divine in all and acting with compassion.

blocks.question: According to the lesson, what is the relationship between the deity and the worshipper?
blocks.answer: They are one and the same.

blocks.text: Recognizing the divine in all things can foster a sense of oneness and inspire acts of devotion and love.
This lesson focuses on the power of devotion and virtue. It describes how devotion can bind the divine, emphasizing the importance of a pure soul and illuminating love.

The verses suggest that devotion is a powerful force, even capable of influencing the divine.  The quality of one's soul determines the extent of divine love received.  True devotion inspires acts of kindness and generosity.

blocks.scenario: You have a strong desire to do something, but know it will hurt someone else. Do you:

choices.text: Choose to act virtuously, even if it means sacrificing your own desire.
Prioritize your own desire, even if it causes harm.

blocks.why: Option A aligns with the lesson's emphasis on virtue and considering the impact of one's actions on others.

blocks.question: According to the lesson, what determines the extent of divine love?

blocks.text: Cultivating devotion and virtue can lead to a deeper connection with the divine and inspire acts of love and kindness.
This lesson warns against the pitfalls of ego, greed, and sin. It highlights the consequences of unchecked desires, harmful speech, and lack of compassion.

The verses describe a life consumed by negative qualities such as lust, anger, greed, slander, and cruelty.  Such actions lead to a fruitless existence and negative consequences in the world beyond.  Joining the company of the holy is presented as an alternative path.

blocks.scenario: You feel tempted to gossip about a friend. Do you:

choices.text: Refrain from speaking negatively and focus on positive qualities.
Give in to the temptation and share the gossip.

blocks.why: Option A reflects the lesson's warning against harmful speech and its emphasis on kindness.

blocks.question: According to the lesson, what are some negative qualities that can lead to a fruitless life?
blocks.answer: Sexual desire, anger, greed, slander, and cruelty.

blocks.text: Overcoming ego, greed, and sin requires conscious effort and a commitment to cultivating positive qualities like kindness and compassion.
This lesson emphasizes detachment from worldly distractions and unwavering devotion to the divine. It speaks of dwelling with the Lord and dedicating oneself entirely to Him.

The verses advise against associating with those who have turned away from the Lord.  True devotees dedicate their minds, bodies, and everything they have to the divine.  They find joy in gazing upon the beauty of God and are cleansed of corruption.

blocks.scenario: You are invited to an event that you know will distract you from your spiritual practice. Do you:

choices.text: Politely decline, prioritizing your connection with the divine.
Attend the event, hoping to balance it with your spiritual practice.

blocks.why: Option A reflects the lesson's emphasis on detachment from distractions and prioritizing devotion.

blocks.question: According to the lesson, what should devotees dedicate to the Lord?
blocks.answer: Their minds, bodies, and everything they have.

blocks.text: Detachment from worldly distractions and unwavering devotion to the divine can lead to inner peace and spiritual growth.
This lesson explores detachment from worldly attachments and the importance of humility. It questions the reliance on wealth and emphasizes seeking to be the dust of all.

The verses suggest that attachments to family and material possessions are illusions.  True security lies in building a connection to the world hereafter, not in wealth.  Humility, desiring to be the dust of all, leads to righteousness and goodness.

blocks.scenario: You are offered a promotion that comes with a significant increase in salary. Do you:

choices.text: Consider the impact on your well-being and relationships, prioritizing what truly matters.
Accept the promotion without hesitation, focusing solely on the financial benefits.

blocks.why: Option A reflects the lesson's emphasis on questioning reliance on wealth and prioritizing what truly matters.

blocks.question: According to the lesson, where does true security lie?
blocks.answer: In building a connection to the world hereafter.

blocks.text: Detachment from worldly attachments and cultivating humility can lead to a more fulfilling and meaningful life.
This lesson reminds us of the inevitability of death and encourages detachment from worldly pleasures. It emphasizes meditating on the One Lord to find true honor.

The verses highlight how easily we forget about death amidst the distractions of daily life.  Meditating on the One Lord allows us to return to our true home with honor.  True fulfillment comes not from worldly possessions, but from serving and connecting with the divine.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling overwhelmed by the demands of your daily life. Do you:

choices.text: Take time for quiet reflection and connect with something greater than yourself.
Continue pushing yourself, hoping to eventually catch up.

blocks.why: Option A reflects the lesson's emphasis on meditating on the One Lord and finding true honor.

blocks.question: According to the lesson, what do we often forget amidst the distractions of daily life?

blocks.text: Remembering death and meditating on the divine can help us detach from worldly pleasures and find true meaning in life.
This lesson focuses on the importance of chanting the Naam and seeking guidance from the Guru. It speaks of purification through meditation and finding solace in divine love.
The verses suggest that meditating on the Naam purifies us.  Praying to the Guru can unite us with the divine.  Immersing oneself in divine love brings coolness and peace to the mind.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling stressed and anxious. Do you:

choices.text: Take time to meditate or chant, focusing on the divine.
Distract yourself with entertainment or other activities.

blocks.why: Option A reflects the lesson's emphasis on chanting the Naam and finding solace in divine love.

blocks.question: According to the lesson, what can chanting the Naam do?

blocks.text: Chanting the Naam and seeking guidance from the Guru can bring peace, purification, and a deeper connection with the divine.
The rain pours down, and the mind is drenched with His Love. The Guru has fascinated my mind, which is drenched in the sublime essence of the Lord.
This passage describes a state of being filled with divine love through the Guru's teachings. It speaks of intuitive peace and a mind pleased by the Guru, leading to joy and contentment.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling overwhelmed by daily life. Do you:

choices.text: Take a quiet moment to reflect on the Guru's teachings and feel gratitude.
Continue to rush through tasks, ignoring your inner feelings.

blocks.why: Reflecting on the Guru's teachings can bring peace and love to the mind, aligning with the tags love, guru, and peace.

blocks.question: According to this passage, what can fascinate the mind?

blocks.text: By connecting with the Guru's teachings, we can find love and peace within ourselves.
The mind is steady and stable, free from reincarnation, by taking shelter in the Guru. Some waste their lives in egotism, caught in attachment, but the Guru saves and protects.

This passage contrasts two paths: one of stability and freedom from rebirth through devotion to the Guru and chanting the Naam, and another of egotism and attachment, leading to suffering and wasted life.

blocks.scenario: You are offered a promotion that would significantly increase your income but require you to compromise your values. Do you:

choices.text: Decline the promotion, focusing on living according to your values and chanting Naam.
Accept the promotion, prioritizing financial gain over your values.

blocks.why: Choosing values and Naam over material gain aligns with the tags reincarnation, naam, and ego, suggesting a path away from egotism and attachment.

blocks.question: According to this passage, what can save and protect us?

blocks.text: By seeking the Guru's guidance and focusing on Naam, we can find stability and avoid the cycle of rebirth.
Focusing on selfless service and singing praises brings wisdom. By sacrificing to the Guru, one can be embellished through the Shabad. The Lord is present wherever there is self-realization.

This passage emphasizes the importance of selfless service (seva) and devotion to the Guru. It suggests that through these actions, one can attain wisdom, self-realization, and connection with the Divine.

blocks.scenario: You see a neighbor struggling to carry groceries. Do you:

choices.text: Offer to help them carry their groceries.
Continue walking, minding your own business.

blocks.why: Offering help is an act of selfless service (seva), aligning with the tags seva, guru, and shabad by embodying the Guru's teachings.

blocks.question: According to this passage, what brings wisdom?

blocks.text: Engaging in selfless service and devotion to the Guru can lead to wisdom and a deeper connection with the Divine.
Without knowing delight with the Lord, one may face sorrow due to karma. By sacrificing to the Guru, one can meet the Lord. Devotional worship brings liberation and glory.

This passage contrasts the consequences of lacking devotion with the benefits of surrendering to the Guru and engaging in devotional worship. It suggests that devotion can lead to liberation from the cycle of karma.

blocks.scenario: You made a mistake at work that caused a minor inconvenience for a colleague. Do you:

choices.text: Sincerely apologize and offer to help fix the issue.
Ignore the mistake and hope it goes unnoticed.

blocks.why: Taking responsibility and offering help demonstrates humility and a desire to learn from karma, aligning with the tags karma, guru, and devotion.

blocks.question: According to this passage, what can lead to liberation?

blocks.text: Through devotion to the Guru and engaging in worship, we can find liberation and break free from negative karma.

Meeting the True Guru leads to finding the Immaculate Lord and escaping the world-ocean. Leaning on the support of the Naam brings truth. The Guru unties bonds, leading to honor and union with the Lord.

This passage highlights the transformative power of the Guru and the Naam. It suggests that by connecting with the Guru and focusing on the Naam, one can achieve liberation, truth, and union with the Divine.

blocks.scenario: You find yourself becoming overly attached to material possessions. Do you:

choices.text: Practice detachment by donating some possessions and focusing on the Naam.
Continue to accumulate possessions, seeking happiness through material wealth.

blocks.why: Practicing detachment and focusing on the Naam aligns with the tags guru, naam, and detachment, suggesting a path towards liberation.

blocks.question: According to this passage, what unties bonds?

blocks.text: By seeking the Guru's guidance and focusing on the Naam, we can break free from attachments and achieve union with the Divine.
Give up greed and corruption. Harmony with the Guru's Shabad brings Ambrosial Nectar. See pleasure and pain as the same, and embrace love for the Guru in the Sat Sangat.

This passage encourages detachment from worldly desires and vices. It emphasizes the importance of aligning oneself with the Guru's teachings (Shabad) and finding love and support within the community of truth (Sat Sangat).

blocks.scenario: You are invited to a gathering where gossip and negative talk are prevalent. Do you:

choices.text: Politely excuse yourself and seek out a more positive and supportive environment.
Stay and participate in the gossip, feeling pressured to fit in.

blocks.why: Seeking a positive environment aligns with the tags greed, shabad, and sangat by prioritizing spiritual growth and avoiding negative influences.

blocks.question: According to this passage, what brings Ambrosial Nectar?

blocks.text: By detaching from negativity, aligning with the Guru's teachings, and seeking positive community, we can find inner peace and spiritual growth.
Profit is obtained through the Lord's Name, a gift from the Guru. The Creator blesses the Gurmukh with Grace. The Lord's Light is within the body, and the Gurmukh is united with Him.

This passage emphasizes the importance of the Lord's Name and the Guru's grace in achieving spiritual fulfillment. It suggests that through devotion and the Guru's guidance, one can realize the Divine presence within and achieve union with the Lord.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling lost and uncertain about your path in life. Do you:

choices.text: Seek guidance from the Guru and focus on chanting the Lord's Name.
Continue to drift without direction, hoping things will eventually work out.

blocks.why: Seeking guidance from the Guru and focusing on the Lord's Name aligns with the tags naam, guru, and grace, suggesting a path towards clarity and fulfillment.

blocks.question: According to this passage, who gives the gift of the Lord's Name?

blocks.text: By seeking the Guru's guidance and focusing on the Lord's Name, we can receive grace and achieve union with the Divine.
Words fail to describe the Lord's praises. He is beyond comprehension. One who is blessed remains lovingly attuned to the Lord, merging with the True Lord.

This passage acknowledges the limitations of human language in describing the Divine. It suggests that true understanding comes through inner experience and a loving connection with the Lord, leading to a state of oneness.

blocks.scenario: You are tempted to boast about your accomplishments. Do you:

choices.text: Practice humility by acknowledging the source of your abilities and expressing gratitude.
Take credit for your accomplishments and seek praise from others.

blocks.why: Practicing humility and expressing gratitude aligns with the tags oneness, love, and humility, suggesting a path towards merging with the True Lord.

blocks.question: According to this passage, what happens to the true person?
blocks.answer: He is merged in the True Lord.

blocks.text: By practicing humility and cultivating a loving connection with the Lord, we can move towards a state of oneness and true understanding.
This passage discusses selfless service, regardless of social standing. It also touches on the pain of separation and physical suffering.

The passage states that whether someone is of high or low social class, if they become a selfless servant, they are worthy of honor. It also describes the pain of separation and the suffering caused by disease, suggesting medicine is ineffective against these deeper pains.

blocks.scenario: You see a wealthy person volunteering at a homeless shelter and a person with limited means offering help to a neighbor. Which action aligns with the message of this passage?

choices.text: Both actions are equally valuable.
The wealthy person's action is more significant.

blocks.why: The passage emphasizes that selfless service is valuable regardless of social standing, aligning with the tags 'seva' and 'humility'.

blocks.question: According to the passage, what is one thing that causes pain?

blocks.text: Selfless service and humility are valuable, regardless of social status.
This passage speaks about the fleeting nature of worldly pleasures and the importance of remembering the Divine. It also mentions the body's eventual decay and salvation through the True Name.

The passage suggests that indulging in sensual pleasures while forgetting the Divine leads to punishment. It highlights the temporary nature of life, comparing it to the fragrance of sandalwood that fades. Ultimately, salvation is found through the True Name, eradicating pain and disease.

blocks.scenario: Someone is offered a promotion requiring long hours, leaving little time for reflection or community. Which choice reflects the message of this passage?

choices.text: Decline the promotion to maintain balance and connection to the Divine.
Accept the promotion and enjoy the increased wealth and status.

blocks.why: The passage warns against forgetting the Divine in pursuit of sensual pleasures, aligning with the tags 'maya' and 'naam'.

blocks.question: According to the passage, what saves a mortal?

blocks.text: Remembering the Divine is more valuable than fleeting worldly pleasures.
This passage describes the Lord's Name as an antidote to pain. It also emphasizes the importance of contentment and charitable giving as a means to spiritual well-being.

The passage equates pain to poison and the Lord's Name to its cure. It suggests grinding contentment and charity together as a daily practice to prevent the body from wasting away. Ultimately, this practice helps overcome the fear of death.

blocks.scenario: Someone feels overwhelmed by negative thoughts. Which action aligns with the message of this passage?

choices.text: Focus on chanting the Lord's Name, practicing contentment, and helping others.
Indulge in distractions to temporarily escape the negative thoughts.

blocks.why: The passage emphasizes the Lord's Name as an antidote to pain and the importance of contentment and charity, aligning with the tags 'naam', 'contentment', and 'charity'.

blocks.question: According to the passage, what is the antidote to pain?

blocks.text: Chanting the Lord's Name, practicing contentment, and giving charitably can lead to spiritual well-being.
This passage discusses controlling desires and aligning oneself with God's will (Hukam). It emphasizes that what pleases God is acceptable and highlights the importance of the Divine Name.

The passage suggests burning desires and greed like firewood and ghee. It states that rituals are less important than pleasing God. Intense meditation and the Divine Name are valuable treasures, and those who possess them are blessed.

blocks.scenario: Someone is torn between pursuing personal ambitions and fulfilling a responsibility to their family. Which choice reflects the message of this passage?

choices.text: Seek guidance and align actions with what pleases God, even if it means sacrificing personal desires.
Prioritize personal ambitions, as individual fulfillment is most important.

blocks.why: The passage emphasizes aligning oneself with God's will (Hukam) and controlling desires, aligning with the tags 'desire', 'naam', and 'hukam'.

blocks.question: According to the passage, what is acceptable?

blocks.text: Aligning oneself with God's will and controlling desires is more valuable than rituals or personal ambitions.
This passage speaks about the power of God's grace and the soul's longing for connection. It also touches on the role of karma and the importance of meditating on the Lord.

The passage describes the soul's desire to ascend to the heavens through God's power. It emphasizes that seeing and understanding are dependent on God's grace. Ultimately, meditating on the Lord through the Guru leads to absorption in the Truth, according to one's karma.

blocks.scenario: Someone is struggling to understand a difficult situation in their life. Which choice reflects the message of this passage?

choices.text: Seek guidance and meditate on the Lord, trusting that understanding will come through grace.
Rely solely on their own intellect and reasoning to find a solution.

blocks.why: The passage emphasizes the importance of God's grace and meditating on the Lord, aligning with the tags 'grace', 'karma', and 'truth'.

blocks.question: According to the passage, what is needed to be comforted and consoled?

blocks.text: Trusting in God's grace and meditating on the Lord can lead to understanding and absorption in the Truth.
This passage discusses the Formless Lord and the importance of obeying His command (Hukam). It also touches on the deluding nature of Maya and the role of the Guru in attaining understanding.

The passage states that the Formless Lord creates and beholds the creation, enjoining us as He pleases. True greatness lies in obeying His Hukam. By Guru's Grace, one can grasp His will and overcome the delusions of Maya, ultimately allaying anxiety.

blocks.scenario: Someone is faced with a difficult decision and unsure of the right path. Which choice reflects the message of this passage?

choices.text: Seek guidance from the Guru and strive to understand and obey God's will (Hukam).
Rely solely on their own judgment and ignore external guidance.

When you meet the Giver of peace, the Lord of the World, He resolves all your affairs. By Guru's Grace, you find the Lord within, and inner fire is quenched.

blocks.why: This reflects the message of finding peace and trusting in divine grace to resolve affairs, aligning with the tags of oneness, grace, and peace.

blocks.question: According to the text, how can one find the Lord?
blocks.answer: By Guru's Grace, within your own heart.

blocks.text: Finding peace and resolution comes from recognizing the divine within.
Why be proud of your body and wealth? They vanish quickly as the world wastes away in ego. The Lord is our saving grace.
Everything belongs to the Lord, who blesses those who follow the Guru with spiritual wisdom. The Lord is above all, destroying fear and doubt.

blocks.scenario: You receive a promotion at work and feel proud. You remember these words.

choices.text: Acknowledge the blessing with humility, recognizing the source of all gifts.

blocks.why: This aligns with the message of humility and recognizing the Lord's grace, connecting to the tags of ego, grace, and spiritual wisdom.

blocks.question: What destroys fear and doubt?

blocks.text: True wisdom lies in recognizing the impermanence of ego and the grace of the Divine.
The world is like a paper fortress, easily destroyed. Duality in the mind is like a snake bite.
Through the Guru's wisdom and meditation, vice is burned away. The mind and body are soothed, and Truth is obtained through devotion.

blocks.scenario: You are caught up in comparing yourself to others. You remember these words.

choices.text: Turn inward, seeking spiritual wisdom to overcome feelings of separation.
Continue to focus on external comparisons, striving to be better than others.

blocks.why: This reflects the message of overcoming duality through spiritual wisdom, aligning with the tags of maya, spiritual wisdom, and duality.

blocks.question: What burns away vice and corruption?
blocks.answer: The Guru's spiritual wisdom and meditation.

blocks.text: Find peace by burning away vice and embracing truth.
All beings beg of You, as You are merciful to all. Seek sanctuary in the Lord and be blessed with Truth.
Without the True Guru, one is blind and acts without understanding. Meeting the Guru brings comprehension and true spiritual wisdom.

blocks.scenario: You are struggling to understand a difficult situation. You remember these words.

choices.text: Seek guidance and understanding from a trusted spiritual source.

blocks.question: What does meeting the True Guru bring?

blocks.text: Seek truth and wisdom through grace and guidance.
Creatures find peace in what they love. Love for the Divine never ends, if it is His Will.
The rainbird finds peace in the rain, the fish in water. Our love for the Divine is sustained by His Will.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling disconnected from your spiritual practice. You remember these words.

choices.text: Trust in the Divine Will and renew your love for the Divine.
Become discouraged and give up on your spiritual practice.

blocks.why: This reflects the message of trusting in Divine Will and sustaining love for the Divine, aligning with the tags of love, will, and peace.

blocks.question: What sustains our love for the Divine?

blocks.text: Find peace and sustain love through Divine Will.
Egotism is exhausted, and the heart is filled with truth. Thirst for the Divine vision is strong.
By lovingly drinking in the Naam, one is satisfied. The desire for the Blessed Vision of the Divine is intense.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling restless and unfulfilled. You remember these words.

choices.text: Turn inward, seeking satisfaction through the Naam and the Divine vision.
Continue to seek fulfillment through external desires.

blocks.why: This reflects the message of finding satisfaction through the Naam and the Divine vision, aligning with the tags of ego, naam, and desire.

blocks.question: How can one be satisfied?
blocks.answer: By lovingly drinking in the Naam.

blocks.text: Find satisfaction by exhausting ego and embracing the Divine.
Without the Beloved, decorations burn and clothes don't look good. Without the Beloved, one cannot survive.
The Husband Lord is near, but the bride doesn't know it. The True Guru reveals Him.

choices.text: Seek guidance from a True Guru to reveal the Divine within.

blocks.why: This reflects the message of seeking guidance from the True Guru to reveal the Divine, aligning with the tags of love, guru, and detachment.

blocks.question: Who reveals the Husband Lord?

blocks.text: Seek the Guru to reveal the Divine within.
Meeting with ease brings peace, and the Shabad quenches desire. The mind is pleased and appeased.
Contemplating the Guru's Shabad brings calmness. Liberation is found by subduing the ego.

choices.text: Contemplate the Guru's Shabad to find peace and subdue the ego.
Give in to the desires and cravings.

blocks.why: This reflects the message of finding peace and subduing the ego through the Shabad, aligning with the tags of shabad, ego, and peace.

blocks.text: Find peace and liberation through the Shabad and subduing the ego.
This lesson focuses on seeking the Light of the Name. We find support and guidance through the Guru's teachings.

The verses express a longing for the Divine Light and support through Naam. The path is revealed through the Guru's Word, and dwelling on the Naam leads to realizing the Beauteous Word. Ultimately, it is through His Will that one finds the Door.

choices.text: Reflect on the Guru's teachings and try to connect with the Naam.

blocks.why: Reflecting on the Guru's teachings and connecting with Naam aligns with the lesson's emphasis on seeking guidance and support through devotion.

blocks.question: According to the lesson, how can one find the path?
blocks.answer: Through the Shabad, the Word of the True Guru.

blocks.text: By seeking the Light of the Name and support of the Guru, we can find our way.
This lesson explores the importance of the Guru and Naam. It also touches upon the significance of fear (bhau) in spiritual growth.

Without the Guru, understanding is limited, and the world remains in darkness. Through fear and love of God, one enshrines the Naam within their heart. The Guru's instructions and True Bani lead to realizing God's Light.

blocks.scenario: You are struggling to understand a difficult situation in your life. You feel lost and confused.

blocks.why: Seeking guidance from the Guru aligns with the lesson's emphasis on the Guru's role in understanding and overcoming darkness.

blocks.question: What is needed to understand and find the Naam?

blocks.text: With the Guru's guidance and love and fear of God, we can find understanding and enshrine the Naam within our hearts.
This lesson focuses on understanding Hukam (God's Will) and the importance of the Shabad. It also highlights the role of grace in spiritual realization.

Everything happens according to God's Will, and what is pre-ordained cannot be changed. By being bound to Hukam and permeated by the Shabad, one becomes immersed in Truth. Through His Grace, the Eternal One unites us with Himself.

blocks.scenario: You are facing a challenging situation that feels beyond your control. You are unsure of what to do.

choices.text: Accept the situation as part of God's Will and seek guidance through the Shabad.

blocks.why: Accepting the situation as part of God's Will and seeking guidance through the Shabad aligns with the lesson's emphasis on Hukam and the importance of the Shabad.

blocks.question: According to the lesson, what cannot be erased?

blocks.text: By understanding Hukam and connecting with the Shabad, we can find peace and acceptance in all situations.
This lesson speaks of the consequences of forgetting the Divine. It uses the metaphor of a stork caught in a net to illustrate this point.

The verses highlight the importance of remembering the Unseen Lord God in our hearts. Consuming many lives for one's own leads to regret and repentance when seized by Death. The lesson suggests reflecting on one's actions.

blocks.question: What does the lesson say one should remember in their heart?

blocks.text: By remembering the Divine and acting with compassion, we can avoid the path of regret and repentance.
This lesson contrasts the foolish self-willed (manmukh) with the path of wisdom and the Guru. It emphasizes the importance of virtuous conduct and contemplation.

The verses suggest that indulging in worldly pleasures without wisdom leads to being trapped. Salvation comes through virtuous conduct, spiritual wisdom, and contemplation, as well as serving the True Guru and dwelling on the True Word.

blocks.why: Reflecting on the potential consequences and choosing a path that aligns with virtuous conduct and wisdom aligns with the lesson's emphasis on these qualities.

blocks.question: According to the lesson, what can save one from being trapped?
blocks.answer: Virtuous conduct, spiritual wisdom and contemplation.

blocks.text: By cultivating virtuous conduct, wisdom, and contemplation, and by serving the True Guru, we can find liberation from worldly traps.
This lesson emphasizes the importance of the Naam and the Guru's teachings. It also touches upon the role of karma in finding the True Guru.

The verses highlight the excellence of the Guru's teachings and the importance of keeping the Name of the Lord in one's heart. Without the True Name, there is no liberation. Finding the True Guru is dependent on karma and His Will.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling disconnected from your spiritual path and unsure of how to reconnect.

choices.text: Focus on enshrining the Name of the Lord in your heart and seek guidance from the Guru's teachings.
Continue without making any changes, hoping the feeling will eventually pass.

blocks.why: Focusing on the Naam and seeking guidance from the Guru aligns with the lesson's emphasis on these elements for spiritual growth.

blocks.question: According to the lesson, what is needed for liberation?

blocks.text: By keeping the Name of the Lord in our hearts and following the Guru's teachings, we can find liberation and reconnect with our spiritual path.
This lesson focuses on the importance of focusing consciousness on the Naam. It also highlights the role of the Guru in dispelling cynicism and eradicating self-conceit (haumai).

By focusing on the Name of the Lord, one can merge with the True Lord through the Guru. Spiritual wisdom arises through the Guru, dispelling doubt. Eradicating self-conceit leads to finding the Door of Salvation.

blocks.why: Focusing on the Naam and seeking guidance from the Guru aligns with the lesson's emphasis on these elements for overcoming cynicism and self-doubt.

blocks.question: According to the lesson, what should one focus their consciousness on?

blocks.text: By focusing on the Naam and seeking guidance from the Guru, we can dispel cynicism, eradicate self-conceit, and find the Door of Salvation.
This lesson explores the concept of Maya (illusion) and the importance of the True Congregation (Sat Sangat). It also emphasizes the role of the Guru in crossing over the world-ocean.

By Guru's Grace, one can eradicate Maya and be reincarnated into the Home of the Lord. The world is a passing show, and without the True Guru, no one finds the path. By good fortune, one finds the Guru and crosses over the terrifying world-ocean.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling overwhelmed by worldly attachments and desires, making it difficult to focus on your spiritual path.

blocks.why: Seeking the company of the True Congregation and guidance from the Guru aligns with the lesson's emphasis on these elements for overcoming Maya and finding spiritual liberation.

blocks.text: By seeking the company of the True Congregation and guidance from the Guru, we can overcome Maya and cross over the world-ocean.

blocks.scenario: You are feeling unwell, but the doctor can't find anything physically wrong. Do you:
